Kazlahk University of Medicine: most healing schools focus on essence and ritual magic because the Magic Society and Adventure Society fund them; KazMed is "a prominent exception", focused on alchemical medicine, funded largely by trade associations, with some money from the Healer's church.
It runs a School of Alchemical Efficiency.
Magical Research Association: open-access research libraries for young researchers; see Magical_Research_Association.md.

Skill books: they are looked down on by some trained adventurers, who say "that's the first thing we have to beat out of skill book users at my family's academy"; see../03_Magic_and_Adventuring/Skill_Books_and_Learning.md.

The clan's schools: the clan has a school for ritual magic and a training centre where all essence users go through a basic programme, with children earning contribution points for their families by attending school.

Asano Academy: "the premier educational institution for magic on planet Earth"; international students are "one of the strongest cards the clan had to play"; full-time staff include Emi, Clive, Belinda and Lorelei, with guest lectures by Jason and a Rufus workshop on the integration of physicality and magic.
New Water: Knowledge's clergy set up schools and training programmes in the new city, with language training for adults and children from "both Earth and Pallimustus".
Earth's schools: Jason's own school was the private Casselton Educational Institute, with "excellent teachers, quality education. Exorbitant cost".
Reputation: "Elves are powerful spell casters and their skill with healing magic is unparalleled".
Aptitude: the elven aptitude is for spells rather than the special attacks humans favour.
Racial gift: Neil's elf racial ability, Life Affinity, evolves into Life Guard.
Local families: Greenstone has local elf families; Lucian Lamprey is an elf banished there who is not one of them, and Pochard Finn is an elf and a local.
Elf fashion: "flowing, tapered lines".
Notable elves: Allayeth and Charist, Yaresh's two diamond-rank elves; Hana Shavar, High Priestess of the Healer; Elspeth Arella, director of the Greenstone Adventure Society.
Predation: cannibals in Book 1 discuss elves as food.
Standing: "One of the most prominent kingdoms in the world" with a royal family; the Queen of Estercost and other members of its elite ask Jason to arbitrate over the System's withdrawal.

Population: a "large and densely populated kingdom" and the land from which Greenstone was colonised centuries earlier; the region is "filled with towns, villages and smaller cities, due to the idyllic climate and rich natural resources".

Capital and councils: Cyrion is the capital, yet the Adventure Society's continental council sits in Vitesse, where the royal family keeps a tower as a palace; in Book 7 the Cyrion branch takes over the site of the operation from Vitesse.
Vitesse: the city of flowers, on what Jason would know as the French Riviera, with garden towers that house the wealthy elite and key organisations.
Adventurers think of it as the continent's adventuring capital, because its high magic spawns powerful, frequent monster manifestations.
Aristocracy: the Remore family has no title, while the Gellers hold only the title from their small provincial city of origin and refuse all others; neither is begrudged a premier tower.
Cyrion's laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families".
House Headingway is "one of Estercost's pre-eminent families".

Cyrion's land: concentric walls ring the city with vast tracts of agricultural land between them, "some of the most magical and valuable growing land on the planet"; it is the largest city in the world, with lakes, forests and heavy air traffic.
Clothes and ships: the fitted "Estercost style" is worn in red and brown by one visitor; specialty airships that run only in high-magic zones are a signature of Estercost.
Kazlahk: a sandstone coastal city on Estercost's eastern border, surrounded by desert and used for spirit coin farms, with denominations more valuable than Greenstone's because the magic is higher.
Rivals: the Storm Kingdom treats Estercost as a friendly rival, its distance leaving few reasons for conflict.

Rule: "ostensibly a kingdom", it is "famously controlled by cartels known for producing substances that ranged from heavily controlled to outright banned"; the cartels keep power through under-the-table deals with powerful groups in neighbouring countries, which prop up a puppet government while their own governments pay lip service to suppression.
Economy: the cartels exploit the region's rare plants and minerals, and the nation is surrounded by strong public sanctions and border controls.
Smuggling culture: the border with the Storm Kingdom is jungle-covered hills with many semi-hidden smuggling paths to the shore.
The border city Casallini is a small city where the Adventure Society keeps a large force because it is a border city.
Neutral Society: the Adventure Society ignores borders and politics and keeps monsters out of population centres, so long as its work is not interfered with.
Reputation: Liara calls it "a stain full of drug dealers and smugglers".
Belinda finds it "famously sketchy" with "all the opportunities it offered to an enterprising and open-minded young lady".
Hired muscle: the men who attack Sophie's delivery are local hires from Casallini.
Goblins as monsters: Jason jokes about killing ten goblins for an uncommon spear in the cannibals' cave.
Transformed humans: in West Canfield, Detroit, people were "turned into goblins and their homes into underground warrens", which became a lawless combat zone.
Cabal beings: the Cabal's mythological beings include centaurs, ogres, fairies and more.
Elves, goblins and fairies: people in a magic city were "turned into elves and goblins and fairies".
Fairy manifestation: a small hovering fairy-like figure with an androgynous body bites Clive in Book 2.
Earth beings in the open: as the Cabal operated in the open, "centaurs, ogres, fairies, and more" were spotted by the media and revealed to the world.
A Network operative expects the Cabal to be "myths and fairy tale creatures".
Zone-turned people: Emi says people in a magic city "were all turned into elves and goblins and fairies", so they were let live there.
Jason's cloud city is described as a fairy tale kingdom, but that is a style, not a people.

Cabal members in human form: fifteen years after the revelation the Cabal is often relaxed about masking its nature, "from diminutive fairies to looming ogres"; "when you were nine feet tall, with three-foot antlers, taking human form was just easier".
The Cabal's members "seemed to have stepped straight out of folklore and fairy tales", which ties them to myriad belief systems. See The_Cabal.md.
Racial gifts: an affinity for special attacks, essences that advance more rapidly than others', and latent powers that adapt to the essences.
The latent gifts are dormant until awakened and then take a form based on the person's essences.

Evolution: Clive's blessing from the Celestial Book changes his human special attack affinity into a spell affinity; his Human Ambition becomes Thirst for Knowledge and Humphrey's Special Attack Affinity becomes Attack of the Mirage Dragon.
Taika's human abilities have been replaced with outworlder ones.
Distribution: the Greenstone region is human-dominated.
Humans and outworlders: an outworlder who has a child with another species produces offspring of that species, so a human and an outworlder have a human child.
Lifespan: essence users age slower; bronze-rankers can live well past a hundred, silvers double that and gold-rankers live for centuries.
Trade port: one of the important sea-trade ports on Pranay's northern coast.
Arena culture: its mirage chamber complex is the city's premier entertainment venue, with essence users facing each other or illusion challenges before a paying audience.
"There are whole essence user teams who never become adventurers"; they earn money in the arena and use monster cores to rank.
Two leagues a year in silver, bronze and iron divisions lead to grand championships. See Mirage_Chamber_Association.md.
Retirement: arena professionals stop using cores before gold, retire when silver longevity runs out and become gold-rank managers of the arena.
Layout: a flat circular arena building at the edge of the Mystic Quarter, spilling into the theatre district.
Transport: those who can afford them ride platter-sized floating discs; floating discs are sold in the Mystic Quarter.
Markets and food: the team visits its markets and finds new customs and food.
A nondescript tattoo parlour run by Tilly is where Jason gets his crest.
Ice cream: Jason remembers kulfi-like ice cream from there.
Nation: Kurdansk lies "in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil".
Celestines: "Like many of Kurdansk's celestines, she had dark skin and silver hair", and the rowhouses are narrow and wedged together.
Entertainment quarter: a former warehouse district near the Kurdan River docks, now the most viable site for large theatre halls, "a heady mix of pleasure, criminality and money".
Skyport: it has a busy skyport with towers where airships dock.
Law: Kurdansk locks criminals up for years in prisons, which a Book 12 speaker calls costly to run.
The Reaper link: Melody Jain's story begins in Kurdansk around twenty-five years before Book 9.

Indenture, not slavery: "We don't have slaves. We have indentured servants. A lot of criminals are sentenced to indenture, then their indenture is sold or auctioned to recoup the cost of their crimes".
Jason finds the system disturbing and says both his world and this one need better systems.
Captured enemies: the Ustei do not accept slavery; "their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death".

The Adventure Society agreement: a clause in the Adventure Society's agreement with Greenstone gives anyone who completes a contract the right of refusal on anyone sentenced to indenture as a result of it.
Hearings: indenture hearings are a normal legal event; the Greenstone court "was less like an American legal p[roceeding]".
House guards: in Cyrion, house guards are "technically a form of indentured servitude" and the laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families".
Jason's argument: if a family used "draconian measures" to hold people to cheap work, nothing would stop them.
The System's withdrawal: the System will withdraw access "in regions of Pallimustus currently operating with slavery, indentured servitude or similar legal systems".
"The Queen of Estercost and several other interested parties" ask for arbitration over the withdrawal.
Slave markets: Jason's friend scouts Sadi Andali's slave markets, and Ben asks whether "the destruction of the Sadi Andali slave trade" is Jason's price.

The name: Jason names Nik from the word "Lehenik", "in a language from the world where I was born, it roughly translates first or firstly. The first instance", and says that is what he wants to call Nik's people "once you're a species and not a unique being: Lehenik. The first people to belong in this place".
Belonging: he explains that everything else in his soul realm "either doesn't belong or is an extension of me. Except for you. You came from me, but you belong to no one but yourself".
A promise: Nik asks "You're going to make more like me?" and Jason answers "Yes. I believe I know how".
Not yet a species: in Book 12 Jason says he cannot "make more of your kind, turn you into a species proper, until I reach the fullness of my power".
He jokes about making a female lehenik and Nik rejects the idea.

Others like them: Raythe tells Jason that astral kings cannot ordinarily use planets in their astral realms to birth messengers, "but you are not the first original to do so. Or to birth more than messengers. There are others like your lehenik to be found amongst the countless worlds".

Strength and stamina: "Members of his leonid race are stronger and faster than us, and that's only the beginning of what leonids can do"; a leonid needs far more exertion than others to tire, another racial gift.
Appearance: a huge "lion man" whose voice is growly by default; Gary is "so huge he made bodybuilders look like they w[ere small]". He is covered in fur.
Size: draconians are larger even than male leonids.
Mixed company: a leonid, an elf and a celestine are among the eleven people who emerge from Dawn's cottage in Book 7.
Notable leonids: Gary Xandier, a Vitesse adventurer, and Gary Sharpton in Book 12, who designs the flying vehicle the group travels in and has spent most of his life in an astral space.
Only reference: Emir answers a joke about someone's partner ("Man, woman or fish?") with "Merfolk are not fish. They happen to be very sensual people".
A joke, not a sighting: in Book 12 Travis asks "Is that some kind of merman?" of a passer-by with webbed hands and feet, and Jason answers that he is the actor Patrick Duffy.
Searched: a scan of the chapter files for merfolk, mermaid, merman and merrow finds no other mention (a "siren" simile at is a comparison, not a species).
Origin: messengers are "budded, not born", and Jason says they are "actually plants, which is kind of crazy".
They are gestalt beings whose body and soul are one (see the 02 file).
Appearance: a messenger in Book 9 "looked like a celestine with alabaster skin and long hair of spun gold", with solid gold eyes, standing some eight feet high with a pair of wings.
A messenger's alabaster skin dulls when drained of mana.
Hierarchy: masters hold servant races, and a master "was free to treat the servant races however he pleased, so long as it did not impinge upon the interests of other messengers".
Fal Vin Garath, a silver-rank messenger, is Benella's abusive master.
Boris Ket Lundi is also named in this pattern (first appearances: and L19;;).
Belief: Dawn tells Jason that astral kings rule through messengers, whose message is "Kneel" (see Astral_Kings_and_Messengers.md. Hess confesses to feeling the instinct to kneel.
Rank limits: rank limits are a function of the brand, which did not exist when messengers first came into being (Boris).
Resurrection: does not work on messengers.
Among humans: Boris and his messengers constantly deal with people who believe them to be angels of the Lord despite his denials.
Fifteen years after the revelation, many Cabal members are relaxed about masking their nature (see The_Cabal.md).

Nature: "the diminutive but influential Kingdom of Mirrors. Small, affluent and geographically blessed, it had neither expanded its borders nor been had its borders encroached upon in more than eight centuries".

The king: the diamond-ranker known as the Mirror King founded the kingdom and rules it still; he has had "a series of queens, reportedly doting on each, even as they grew old and died beside him", and Valdis is one of the current queen consort's sons.
Court manners: kneeling is expected before the king; his protocol officer Hastor tells Jason "You should kneel", and the king says Hastor "starts getting snippy" without a seating chart by rank.
Valdis's team drops to one knee on the king's arrival.
The king is amused, warm and teasing with his son.
Teams built around princes: Valdis's team was built around him, "the shaft to his spearhead".
The kingdom has its own battles with the Builder cult.
The king's aura: Jason, an iron-ranker, finds the king's aura felt like part of the world, "in perfect symbiosis with the world", and it later inspires his own aura control.
Portals: the king has his own portal specialist, Hastor, who calls up a glass-like portal.
A surplus of royals: Valdis says his father is "so horny and immortal" that "the kingdom's thick with princes and princesses" and he will take a good adventurer over any of his kids.
Valdis's administrative prowess assembles an arena event in under two days.

A Book 13 line places a relic "in the Mirror Kingdom. A wild place, so far north that the ice never thaws", which does not match the "small, affluent and geographically blessed" kingdom of. Both are recorded.

Definition: Clive: "An outworlder is someone whose soul has re-entered a physical reality, reflexively manifesting a body for itself"; the body is "akin to that of a monster, or a summoned familiar", physical substance forged from raw magic, between the astral and the physical.
How it happens: natural magical phenomena connecting two realities drag someone through; their body is annihilated in the astral and their soul reconstitutes one.
Advantages: Farrah says outworlders "might have their advantages", and Jason's abilities (map, interface, astral affinity) are outworlder abilities.
Children: an outworlder with another species produces offspring of that species; two outworlders produce a celestine.
Arrivals: a hundred and nineteen outworlders arrive at once in Book 7; two outworlders among the eleven people in Dawn's cottage are bronze rank.
Jason: his character screen lists him as a formerly human outworlder until Book 12.
Geography: Pranay is this world's equivalent of Sri Lanka, "larger and further south", a huge landmass in the Indian Ocean.
Its northern coast has several important sea-trade connections in a world without the Arabian Peninsula.
Jayapura: Hester's birth city; personal transport for those who can afford it is a platter-sized floating disc ridden by shifting weight.

Mirage chambers: Jayapura has a vast mirage chamber complex, more sophisticated than the Gellers' private chamber in Greenstone because the higher magic allows potent dimensional magic and concurrent chambers.
Massive city: Jason's team visited Pranay's urban centre after their first Reaper astral space and saw only familiars as magical beasts.
Portal stopover: in Book 11 it is a portal stopover on the way to Estercost, "the last of the isolated city-states they would visit for a while".
Temple districts: temples line the road to the Island's Divine Square and "gods had hierarchies of their own": the Temple of Roads sits behind the larger Temple of Journeys.
The square is crowded with booths selling religious paraphernalia and people proselytising.
Dominion: "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles. It is he who determines who rules, and who serves".

The Healer: Neil makes a stand in the Temple of the Healer; ex-clergy who offended their gods and were stripped of divinely gifted essences suffer a debilitating imbalance in body and soul; the notes make the Healer the god who does this.
tags: notes, Book 1; the Healer is not named in that line

claim: Knowledge's temple: in Rimaros it is "an important resource for the many magical researchers" with a symbiotic relationship with the Magic Society branch; the temple is mostly a vast library covering multiple wings.
Churches and research: churches, especially Knowledge's, help fund the Magical Research Association.
Death's paperwork: the Church of Death issues certification of how many times a person has died.
Limits on gods: a god's favour does not mean intervention; a goddess says she cannot see into the astral space where Jason holds prisoners; the gods are "bound by convoluted limitations".
The Hierophant: the Hierophant of the World-Phoenix is allowed to intervene in Pallimustus a single time.
Appearance: "short and stocky, with skin of such a deep blue it was almost black", no hair and covered in faintly glowing, tattoo-like markings that are natural to the race.
Rarity: they are "a rarity in Greenstone"; a runic barman in Old City is stocky and hairless with blue-black skin and glowing runes.
Bones: the runes show faintly on their bones; a short, broad skeleton in the desert astral space is identified as a runic by them.
Notable: Arash, a runic Jason meets in the temple district, explains Dominion's role: "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles".
Part of the civilisation-building species: the list of species that build civilisations is "humans, elves and leonids, celestines, runic, smoulder and draconians".
Common in Old City: a runic works as a barman, and a runic man appears at Jory's clinic.
Inherent markings: the glowing runes "looked like magic tattoos but were an inherent trait".
Spellcasters: "Elves and runics were the most common affliction wielders, as their predilection for spells made a ranged power set much more likely".
Earth zones: when zones turn Earth people into other species, Jason, Farrah and Dawn spot elves and "the dark-skinned runic people".
A runic woman appears with Rick Mercer's team.
Kinship with smoulders: "Smoulders and the runic were quite similar, with their dark skin and glowing features" (see Smoulder_and_Brighthearts.md).
Setting: a captive's guess of "Eastern desert?" is answered "Obviously, ever hear of a little dirtball country called Sadi Andali?". Its cells are mud brick.
Law: "famous for being almost lawless"; the Adventure Society has no branch there and only sends people in to sweep for illegal research and restricted essences, finding plenty of both.
Slave markets: unusual products move through them; Ben asks whether destroying its slave trade is Jason's price.
Reach: events "all across Sadi Andali" are set against the great houses of Cyrion.
Effect on visitors: Percival Headingway thinks Garret's time there may have "knocked some sense" into him.
Smoulder: "They have natural affinities for earth and fire"; a smoulder friend of Humphrey's parents has the wind essence and his earth affinity evolved into an air affinity.
Niko, a member of Beth's team, has dark skin, glowing red eyes and jet-black hair.
Brighthearts: in Book 10 fewer than ten thousand of the brightheart smoulder survive, crammed in the citadel cavern.
Marla is a fire aspect with skin markings, eyes and hair the yellow-orange of steel in a forge; Lorenn, an ash aspect, has smoky greys.
War form: Beaufort prefers his fifteen-foot metal skeleton "war form" but must meet the brightheart smoulders in a form they will accept.
Home: the largest chamber of the underground realm was home to most brightheart smoulders.
Extent: "It rules the Sea of Storms, all the islands on it and all the coastal regions that surround it"; the capital is Rimaros.

Sky islands: reserved for "the cream of society": big-name adventurers, long-standing adventuring families and aristocrats; a family known for producing good adventurers is mostly inducted into the nobility, and a house without good adventurers sinks into obscurity.

Monarchy: the Storm King is a gold-ranker, which one must be to take the throne; royals are not raised on cores as in most nations, since that disqualifies them here, and potential heirs from every branch are adventurers proving themselves in monster fighting and statecraft in a decades-long contest until the monarch chooses an heir.

Titles: the firstborn daughter of the Storm King, if competing, is the Hurricane Princess and the firstborn son the Storm Prince; many royals bow out, often adopting into their non-royal parent's family.

Palindromic names: first and last names that are palindromes are assigned in adulthood and mark important family members; the more prominent the family, the rarer the practice, and the royal family shares a name with the capital.
Royal looks: the royal family's iconic feature is sapphire hair and eyes.
Royal guard: the Sapphire Crown is one of the most powerful guilds, backed by the royal family, and its non-royal members must periodically serve in the royal guard.
Public islands: Livaros, Arnote and Provo lie in an east-west line.
Arnote is mostly residential, home to successful merchants and retired adventurers, with a relaxed lifestyle that is part of Rimaros's cultural identity, and a minor royal branch lives there.
Livaros is the "adventurer island", with the Adventure Society campus and most adventurer services.
Rivalry with Estercost: friendly rivals whose distance gives little cause for conflict.
Politics later: by Book 12 Zara's brother is the new Storm King, and she remains adopted into House Nareen rather than on the outs with the royals.
Who they are: the "sand pirates" are actually the Ustei Tribe, nomads from a region to the north; Humphrey identifies them as northerners from their hair and clothes.
The raids: an expedition is formed to find out why they are so far south and stop them raiding spirit coin shipments.
The response: the best outcome is a peaceful return north or an agreement not to attack convoys; failing that, they are to be captured and interrogated.
Vincent expects them to talk if shown strength.
Captives: "Their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death".
Later: by Book 12 the Ustei who came south are said to predate the Earth arrivals by about three years.
The homeland: a region to the north of the Greenstone desert, whose oases are connected to the astral space that supplies the desert.
When the astral space's water supply failed, the oases "were no longer able to support all the nomad tribes".
Travel: the entire tribe lives on a war barge, "easily the equal of a passenger liner", built on giant bones with multiple decks.
Warriors and ranks: only a fraction of the warriors are iron-rankers, most have one or two essences; bronze-rank captains lead them, and a silver-rank tribal chief commands the tribe.
Dress: Humphrey identifies them as northerners "from the hair and clothes".
Women, children and slaves: the tribe's women and children were locked away in conditions like slaves, and actual slaves were found in the same conditions.
Someone floated the idea of taking the Ustei men as slaves, "which would at least be something they understood".
Law of surrender: "Their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death".
After defeat, they claim the barge and everything in it, including the women, children and slaves, belongs to the victor; "the idea is that now they have to go raiding for more women".
After the surrender: the Adventure Society plans to relocate them north and investigate the astral space.
Jason's regret: in Book 4 he regrets his part in the battle and wonders whether a peaceful solution was tried.
A later note: the Ustei who came south predate the arrival of the Earth people by about three years.
Origin: Jason had only seen valash when Earth's transformation zones turned humans into them; they are "a skinny sapient species not native to Pallimustus".
Appearance: "skinny bodies and Chihuahua-like heads", shorter than Jason.
Outworlders: the valash Jason meets in Yaresh is an outworlder with a silver-rank aura and no sign of core use.
Fashion: his fitted white suit is not in the local style and "would have been more at home in a Miami nightclub in the eighties".
Zolit Kreen: the valash outworlder introduces himself as "Zolit. Zolit Kreen".
He was originally a valash, "attention-grabbing" for being an outworlder and a chihuahua-headed species, and "had spent years working very hard to undo that damage".
A niche: he ranked to silver while staying as unremarkable as possible, then retired to be a fight promoter, where "everyone was a little bit strange" and "being a valash outworlder was his" gimmick.
Prison: Adventure Society enforcers lock him up after he meets another outworlder, asking about his assistant Benella and messengers.
Social standing: despite his small stature he is "not pushed, shoved, or disrespected" in a crowd, with a silver-rank aura.

The city of flowers: it is "known as the city of flowers", in what Jason would know as the French Riviera, with garden towers that have every third or fourth floor given to gardens "using water, light and plant magic to create lush refuges of peace".
The towers house the wealthy elite, aristocrats and adventurers, and the headquarters of key organisations.
Standing of the great families: the Remore family has no aristocratic title and the Gellers only a small provincial one, and neither is begrudged residences in premier towers.
Adventuring: iron-rankers there may not hunt alone, because of the high magic.

Adventuring capital: many consider it the adventuring capital of the continent; high magic makes monster manifestations powerful and frequent across the region, which matters because Estercost is full of towns, villages and smaller cities.
Detection: the local Adventure Society intercepts monster appearances with a network of towers, something like the Earth grid, instead of leaving notes for wandering adventurers.

A prosperous city: Jason finds "trees lined every street, heavy with blossoms" and "social programs and labour laws meant that even the poorest sections of the city were safe and relatively prosperous", from an economy thriving in multiple sectors.

Lucrative adventuring: a steady stream of silver- and gold-rank monsters with efficient looting protocols; Vitesse adventurers are in demand around the world, and the Magic Society offers portal travel and airship construction.
Safe and gossipy: with so many powerful adventurers, "if some crazy monster or lunatic cult showed up, he could relax and hear about it all later, just like everyone else".
The Academy and the guild: Remore Academy and Burning Violet face each other, and the Remore family's control of the guild is contested.
Size and design: only a few tens of thousands live there, but the design accommodates the environment so that the city has the footprint of a much larger centre.
Walls and gates: its walls are a line of massive trees with glossy black stone filling the gaps, tunnels pass through the trunks, and vehicles queue at a gate for inspection.
Streets: alleys are nicer than the norm and resemble gardens, with gravel paths through long grass.
Government: "In Yaresh, the civic administration is considerably weaker than the churches and the major societies", because one group undermines the Duke for its own ends.
The Aristocratic Faction: wealthy aristocrats and a few merchant barons who own most of the land and provide most of the jobs, and who use that power to shape their tenants' ideology.
They have no adventurers or researchers behind them, just money and political influence.

Diamond-rankers: Allayeth and Charist, both elves; Yaresh has "not just one but two resident diamond-rankers", with Charist the more social and Allayeth the more reclusive, who raised the all-woman team Moon's Edge, led by Miriam Vance.
Reunion: in Book 12 much of the reunion group has already left Yaresh to make preparations for the expedition to Earth.
Setting: "a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines".
Celestine community: Gary says "Zartos has a large celestine community"; Rufus has not been, though his brother recommended it. See Celestines.md for the people.
Craft: Virid keeps a personal smithy there, "the best place to forge a great work".
Gary and Virid forge while the team rests.

Power versus money: the Aristocratic Faction of Yaresh is described as having "focused on power structures completely divorced from personal power": no adventurers or researchers, only money and influence.
Its insignia is a sword and rod crossed over a shield, stitched on its staff's clothing and embossed on its badges.

Application: the applicant fills in personal details and undergoes a magical scan of their body and essences with an Adventure Society official, a Magic Society clerk (Russell, with a clipboard) and an acolyte of Knowledge, Gabrielle Pellin, who holds up a crystal orb as an aura reader; the essences she reads are written down.
Jason had already checked his combination against the restricted list.

Rufus tells Jason that it is impossible to become a member with a restricted essence; Death is restricted by itself and other restrictions are mostly combinations, because the confluence is usually the dangerous essence.
Field assessment: an instructor takes a group of candidates out for a week, during which they must complete postings from the adventure boards of delta towns and villages.
Field testing takes place at the start of every month and candidates sign up at the administration desk.
Vincent Trenslow and Guy Spalding both act as instructors ("Instructor Trenslow" and "Instructor Spalding"); Spalding is also Albert Bertinelli's supervisor.
Adventurers also patrol outlying villages on a monthly rota, an unpopular punishment duty that means a month away from the city.
Badge: a circular iron medallion embossed with the sword-and-rod-over-shield emblem, carried in a leather wallet.

It serves as identification, lets the holder copy a notice by touching the medallion to it and then to a blank sheet, and is paired with a tracking stone: "It tells us if you're alive or dead, and lets us find you if you go missing or die".
The Magic Society makes badges, taking an aura imprint in a magic circle; Jason's tracking stone cannot track him because of his Mysterious Stranger gift. Rufus's is bronze for his rank.

Stars show the Society's confidence in judgement, not power (Vincent): two stars mean some unsupervised responsibility and different kinds of contract; three stars are "much the same as two, but more so".

The notes add that stars drop when rank rises; Lucian tells Pochard to put up the contract on an off-the-books spirit coin farm as a three-star contract so that "someone who'll actually do the work" takes it, and Pochard answers that "if it involves the spirit coin farms, the Adventure Society will make it three-star"; and Jason is later given a gold badge with a diamond symbol where one, two or three stars would normally be.
Stones for kills: no awakening stones are awarded for killing monsters above the killer's rank (Vincent).
Notices are posted on boards or issued directly; a notice carries "the name of the monster, or a description", the number of monsters and the approximate location.
Orders and quotas: during a monster surge every adventurer has an action quota assigned at the jobs hall.
Guilds receive about sixty percent of the quotas; in a city like Livaros about three in ten adventurers are in a guild and one in ten in a high-end guild (Rufus).
Builder-response team: an official refers Jason to this team for assessment as a potential threat before assigning a quota.
Branch: a director and deputy; in Greenstone the director is Elspeth Arella, the deputy Genevieve Picot, and officials include Vincent Trenslow and Albert Bertinelli.
In Book 2 an inquiry team from the council audits the Greenstone branch after the desert expedition disaster; its leader Tabitha Gert wears a black Adventure Society pin.
The Africa-like continent's council sits at Rakesh.
Directors as politics: the Cyrion branch director Jacinta Adeline holds one of the most political appointments in the organisation.
Envoys: in Book 10 the council deploys Marcus Hargrave Xenoria to Yaresh to deal with complaints about the local administration.
Restricted essences: Rufus says Death is restricted by itself, and the Magic Society's living document shows one restricted combination, the Succubus essence, which takes two insanely rare essences.

A corrupt essence is on the list: a Magic-Society-bound adventurer hands one looted from an elemental to the Adventure Society "since it was on the restricted list"; the Society offers good trades for restricted essences.
Neutrality: the Society is described as neutral in disputes between nations.

Corruption and reform: Rufus says there "may be some level of corruption in this branch" in Book 1; a later corruption enquiry at the Greenstone branch led to blanket demotions of two- and three-star members, who were bumped back up afterwards (the notes for Book 12 describe the Society "getting cleaned up alongside Old City").
Exact meaning of the gold badge with a diamond symbol (the text does not explain it).
(Resolved) The Society and the Magic Society do take part jointly in the application scan.
Branding: a tin of salve Jason buys in Book 1 is labelled "Greenstone Alchemy Association".
Membership: Jory is "a member of the Adventure Society and the Alchemist Association".
Belinda says the same of another person, "in the Alchemy Association and the Adventure Society". Dual membership is ordinary.

Standing: in Greenstone's guild district the Forge Society and the Alchemist Association are "clearly second to the Adventure and Magic Societies, but still occupied impressive chunks of real estate".
Assistants: Jason is told he could get assistants from the Association.
Interest in recipes: the Association has been "hounding" Neil for the miracle potion recipe.
Benefits: organisational benefits from the Adventure Society, Magic Society, Alchemy Association "and the like" are what the top guilds care about, not material rewards.
Brokered supply: a lord brokered the sale of a crate of potions through the Association, and stock runs short until people get their next batches from the vats.

Yaresh: the Association's main research centre stands across the road from the Magical Research Association's campus, in a district the urban planners chose for places prone to "unexpected explosions, inadvertent poison fog and accidental fire titan summoning".
Directors: the Association has a director who attends Greenstone's great gatherings with those of the Magic Society and the Adventure Society.
The Artifice Association is mentioned only as a source of kitchen equipment and as a workshop where Travis works and the Irios family are "deeply involved" in it in Rimaros.
What it was: an ancient cult of assassins who venerated the Reaper, "the finality of death".
Emir says they were "scoured from this world, root and branch, by a coalition of churches".

Shade explains that the churches, locked out of the sealed astral space, made a second bargain with the vorger, deep-astral entities that can violate dimensional boundaries; the vorger have no physical substance, appear in swarms and warp the bodies of those they affect until the city gains another flesh abomination.

Shade says the Order served as royal assassins ("a knife in the dark can be the deliverance of nations"), was accepted by the nations, the Adventure Society, the Magic Society and most churches, and was also a hunter of the undead: "more necromancers fell to the Order than princes or kings"; the church of the Unliving and another church formed "an unholy compact" to remove it.

The last grandmaster: when the churches found the training facilities beneath Sky Scar Lake, the last grandmaster sent the initiates into a sealed astral space (the City of Fallen Echoes) and scattered the keys, so that someone worthy might one day reclaim what was left.

Shade tells Jason the Order "does not maintain a roster of assassins at all" but makes "connections. Quiet allies", matching jobs to people who think them worthwhile, a "volunteer network" whose tests find agents with the right principles.

Beliefs and methods: the Builder recruits cults with gifts of power, uses star seeds, constructs such as golems and clockwork animals, and Clockwork Kings, whose cores convert essence users (notes, Book 8: clockwork cores alter and take over bodies, so converts cannot use essence abilities because the cores cannot violate the soul).
Cult leaders: Zato, the last silver-ranker left in the cult's local forces, leads the evacuation of the island stronghold and decamps to the Vane Estate; Timos is an embedded cultist in Greenstone.
The cult's attempt to summon a clockwork king failed and instead "summoned some outworlder lunatic".
The Builder possesses Dougall's body, which breaks down if it uses more than silver-rank power, and later Thadwick Mercer's.

In Book 10 Beaufort heads the Cult of the Builder's forces in Cardinas and is Lorenn's uneasy ally: a gold-ranker who has given up his essence powers and is "some manner of semi-artificial monstrosity", though he looks like a beautiful blond elven man.
Church relation: Purity's church works with the cult and is placed under inquiry by an ecumenical council of the other churches (Disguise's role is covered in Gods_and_Churches.md).
Origin and nature: created by Disguise, masquerading as Purity; the Flames of Redemption are an extreme modification of lesser vampirism.
Effects and tools: the flames leave members with a distinct lack of imagination and a trend toward linear thinking.

Operations: massacres of isolated fortress towns disguised as monster attacks while adventurers are busy; recruitment of volunteers; the capture of Gibson Amouz, a cousin of Liara's husband, whom the Church of the Healer later recovers.

People: Melody Jain is the overall leader of the order's local operations, with her second Sendira and church adviser Laront (a Purity priest who never passed through the flames, so he can safely visit cities).
Hana Shavar says the church lies dormant for generations and, when it finally acts, it is like its god has saved up his chances to intervene; expect "dark miracles".

In Cardinas its priests turn the dead into undead; its priests are led by Garth Larosse, a priest of Undeath and a zemravore (an undead that steals living hearts;: his power is the ability to kill his own aura, rendering him invisible to aura senses).
Departments of Supernatural Affairs: the US Network "ultimately morphed" into the US Department of Supernatural Affairs.
Other states have ministries of the same kind: the United Kingdom has a Ministry of Supernatural Affairs, and the US has a Secretary of Supernatural Affairs. Australia has one too.
The UN Office of Supernatural Affairs: Annabeth (Anna) Tilden, the former Sydney Network branch director, is its Under-Secretary-General. Holly Macrossan is her successor.
After losing the UN post she becomes Australia's Liaison to the Multinational Supernatural Response Taskforce.

The summit site: after the refugee handover negotiations, Asano Village and the surrounding area are made a special-interest territory, a neutral site for formal summits between governments and magical factions, managed by a multinational organisation under Lenora Coleman.
Coleman is a bureaucrat and a core-user; most of the world's gold-rankers belong to the United States and China.
The taskforce: the "yet-unnamed multinational taskforce" at Asano Village is run by Coleman and is also called the Multinational Supernatural Response Taskforce. Its members attend by hologram.
The proposal: Jason offers the participants unfiltered access to the magical knowledge of his people, a training centre and a share in the reverse engineering of the dimensional vessel he seized.
He admits it comes with "a level of control that some might call tyrannical".
The two principles: everything developed from the information he provides must be open source, with no proprietary data, designs or patents, and published by an agreed deadline.
The second principle is that the use of what is developed is subject to terms he enforces, and "the final word is mine".

Third-world debt: he states he will focus on nations where Cabal social programs have been advancing economies, and wants third-world debt forgiven, saying he will give the nations enough spirit coins to pay it off if not.
The Saint-Étienne Summit Accords: they set up exchange programs that "raised the bar for nations around the world".
Research must be shared "in a controlled manner", though not freely disseminated to all.
The Accords' secrecy feeds conspiracy theories about a shadow government, and their terms require all research to be shared "fully and in timely fashion".

China and Russia demanded more influence in the negotiations, and the United States nearly derailed it over the spelling of "defense"; the name was changed from Earth Joint Defence Initiative to Earth Defence Joint Initiative as a face-saving compromise, and troops pronounce it "edgy".
The Asano clan dominated the essence-user landscape, with a whole generation trained by Rufus Remore and its training regimens eclipsing the elite US ones.
The clan makes it available only to nations that join the EDJI.
Intelligence agencies that tried to steal the secrets were stopped swiftly and permanently.
Forces: augmented soldiers, not essence users, are the backbone of EDJI forces, with essence users as elite specialists.
The exosuit is a magitech exoskeleton that only enhanced individuals can use.
EDJI uniforms carry the markings of the national army.
Its forces mobilise across Europe against the vampires, with flying ships of essence users and Cabal forces alongside.
People: General Michael Mills is selected as spokesperson for the EDJI member states.
Natalie Park, now Natalie Ladiv, left ASIS for the EDJI.
Its formation multiplied Anna's workload.

sec: 5. The Joint Magitech Weapons Research Institute
claim: It is headed by Miriam Coyle with Travis Noble as lead researcher; in two years it "revolutionised" weapons used against the vampires.

sec: 5. The Joint Magitech Weapons Research Institute
claim: He was recruited to the Asano clan, taken to the other universe for years of research, and returned with weapons "unrivalled in two worlds".

sec: 5. The Joint Magitech Weapons Research Institute
claim: New lightning guns are expected in general deployment within forty days.

sec: 6. The Asano clan as an organisation
claim: Yumi Asano: Jason's paternal grandmother, the clan matriarch, who looks a third of her age and forbids members to go that far out.

sec: 6. The Asano clan as an organisation
claim: Her recruitment priority is researchers, drawn by the astral cities' technology.

sec: 6. The Asano clan as an organisation
claim: Ketevan Arziani: the former Australian Network branch director, taken on by Yumi after the branch was broken up; she is the clan's administrator.

sec: 6. The Asano clan as an organisation
claim: She says the government sided with her clan in the schism of the major secret society and gave her the land of the "upstart clan".

sec: 6. The Asano clan as an organisation
claim: Standing: the clan is the world's centre of essence training and magitech.
Origins (Craig Vermillion): "some five centuries ago, a new kind of magic appeared."

Book 13 calls the Network's founder Jason's "outworlder predecessor", whose schemes continue to play out unseen; his familiar was Mr North, a rune spider (North says in Book 5 that he "was a rune spider, originally"), and Boris worked with that familiar to betray the founder to the early magic societies that became the Network.

Jason's account in Book 13 adds that the founder, an outworlder brought into the fake Purity's church, returned to Earth with magic Knowledge had bargained from the messengers, built the web of secret societies and the Grid as a pressure-release valve for the rising magic, and was betrayed by his familiar Noreth, born on Pallimustus, who handed him to the US secret societies at a time Jason guesses was around the War of Independence; Noreth is Mr North, leader of the Engineers of Ascension; the wiki calls him the original creator of the Grid and the Network's founder.
Ranks: tiers or categories zero to five match the ranks on Pallimustus (Vermillion).
Going public: known to the public as the Global Defense Network (GDN) in the weeks after the monster waves began.
Fracture: by Book 12 the Network has "fractured"; a nine-person tactical unit led by Nigel Thornton stays together through the upheavals.

At the Nitra dome in Book 6 the Network has split into four blocs: the US branches, the Chinese branches, the True Network (the former International Committee, which kept many of the government links) and the Global Defence Network, made up of rank and file and ex-EOA and Cabal members; the Cabal has split between those serving the vampires and those siding with humanity, and the EOA is splintering.

Marie Finnegan, the recently expelled director of the Zurich Network branch, lives in a chalet in Zermatt, Switzerland, and is allied with the vampire queen Elizabeth and the scientist Simon McKean (head of the Earth researchers in the old workgroup) in the Book 13 plot; a dimensional bag holds seven reality cores.
Book 13 also says her backers call using Elizabeth "the smart choice" even after miscalculations.
Methods: tactical teams answer incursions with "hammer-blow tactics" that Jason tells Nigel will not hold against stronger monsters.
Lyon's branch concealed the Dimensional Fortress at Saint-Étienne for seventy years by faking the Grid.
Vermillion, the Cabal's front man in Sydney in Book 4, says "the Cabal is everywhere".

Vermillion describes the Cabal as the oldest of Earth's three dominant magical forces, tied to the "old magic" of vampires and things older than history, with "a tight grip on old money literally since the invention of money" (the three dominant forces); its tier-four members have entered hibernation.
Messengers hid among its leaders: "even many amongst the Cabal had considered the angelic founders of their collective a myth".

By Book 11 Elizabeth has taken over Venice and rules it among the vampire lords, who resent her policy of treating humans better and her warnings; in Book 6 she keeps the peace among the vampire lords Wassily and Klaus and questions Jason about the changes; Anna describes a new leader among the vampires who has separated from the Cabal, and Jason answers "I've met Elizabeth" (to L28).
Later the Cabal is said to have unambiguously split from the vampire lords and those who followed them.
Vermillion has been a vampire for seventy years, which has brought him to the second tier (the seventy years is not yet located).
In Book 11 the Cabal holds some of the UK and Scandinavia and displaces Network factions in areas such as Russia, Africa, Sulawesi and Papua.
Structure: four Cardinals: Mr North, Mrs South, Mr East and Mrs West.
A "former Mrs South" gave the Network information about the necromancer, so she left the EOA.
Adrien Barbou becomes Mr East: "the previous Mr East" is "the late Mr East", and Barbou is "now going by Mr East" beside Mr North, "the new Mr East" with a new Mrs South.
Methods and plans: North reports that disabling the Grid is "proving more difficult than anticipated" and that they have shut off only localised areas.

In Book 13 Jason says Plan A was to wreck the Grid, forcing the World-Phoenix to step in; Plan B was an army of super-soldiers to fight Knowledge's forces, a project that the Asano clan took up and perfected.
Reach: took Perth, then Melbourne, then moved on Sydney.
Mr North (Noreth) is the true leader, very old and not fully human; he was a rune spider and the Founder's familiar.
Matriarch Yumi (his paternal grandmother) looks a third of her age through flesh-shaping essences and forbids members to leave the domain.

Governments run the artefact site, create the Multinational Supernatural Response Taskforce, in which Lenora Coleman is the designated liaison to Jason, and employ officials such as Holly Macrossan, who succeeds Annabeth Tilden as Under-Secretary-General of the UN Office of Supernatural Affairs and later takes an Australian government post as Liaison to the Multinational Supernatural Response Taskforce.
Annabeth Tilden is the UN contact earlier.

Outsiders joined together: it is "largely made up of those who came to magic from outside the normal channels", formed by the strongest of the smaller groups "looking for strength in numbers", and its magic is "a hodgepodge, cobbled together from what they could beg, borrow, or steal".
Decentralised: it operates in clusters, which makes it flexible but without cohesion, and "less likely to retaliate against the loss of individual members".
Engineering themselves: it chooses its own path "into areas the hegemonic powers won't touch" and its name means they are trying to engineer themselves to a higher state.
It does not itself reveal magic, and plays along with secrecy while expecting the truth to come out.
It expects magic to become as valuable as money or political influence, and has been inducting influential private groups and individuals where the Network took the political ones.
Products: longevity treatments with few side effects, and more radical body modification.
Its "alchemically juiced-up thugs" are the foot soldiers.
Reach: it seizes control of Perth and Melbourne and pushes into Sydney.
Hiro Asano's interests are bought out to get him out of its path.
Conflict with the Cabal: its blood-servant research causes conflicts with Vermillion's organisation. Compare The_Cabal.md.
Structure: four Cardinals sit around a square table: Mr North, Mrs South, Mr East and Mrs West, each with subordinates. Mr North is "the first among equals".
Book 13 explains the names are the cardinal directions.
Adrien Barbou: he starts as one of Mrs West's flunkies and proposes helping Asano rather than hammering him.
He becomes the new Mr East after his predecessor dies, and shows the previous Mr East had stalled the plan to give Cabal factions time to prepare.
Mr North poaches him from Mrs West's circle.
The self-repair function makes a wide-scale blackout difficult.
Barbou warns that the Grid will be down for months, not two weeks, which is an apocalypse.
Mr North decides to go ahead within a week.
Mrs South's refusal: the first Mrs South, Audrey, says the EOA's original goal was "to democratise magic", that they became what they fought, and that she will not burn the world down.
Mrs West tells her she will not leave the room, and she answers "I'll die clean". A new Mrs South is installed.
Mr North: not human, a former rune spider and the Network founder's familiar.
He tells Jason his minions were disappointing "before Adrien Barbou came along". See Mr_North.md.
Barbou's later conduct: Gerling grabs him from the US.
He tells Gerling that he is "a vessel subject to the prevailing winds" and would change sides, and that Mr North knew the founder well.
Public campaign: the EOA tries to swing public opinion enough to demand a seat at the table.
In the lead-up to the reveal it works to turn Jason into an urban legend, to pave the way for its superheroes.
Network opponents: Jack Gerling, a category-four Network essence user with the Onslaught essence, is sent to fight the vampires and later to fetch Barbou.
Farrah Hurin, whom Barbou once held, is the key to the Network recovering the Grid. See the Gerling and Farrah files.
Its strongest members are modified humans who dose themselves with magical drugs and pose as superheroes.
They drop the superhero gimmick and operate more like a superhuman paramilitary.
Former members who did not know what they had joined are absorbed by the Global Defence Network.
Noreth's failure: Noreth was an unstable element whose isolationism was "disastrous". Boris refused to take part.
His drastic disabling of the Grid created the transformation-zone crisis and spiked Earth's magic.
Plan B was an army of super-soldiers to fight Knowledge's forces, but North's "shortcuts and fumbling, inhumane experiments led only to abominations and madness" until the Asano clan perfected it.
The program: it had massive death rates and damaged alien implants, and the leader was "secretly being some kind of spider".
The superhuman products are a haunted lot, many dying.
The end: the sabotage "was ultimately the action that spelled the end of their organisation".
By the later years, the EOA no longer exists.
Their research on the Grid is "a dead end", but Jason has the complete records.
She ran a joint magitech program with the Cabal and the Network and was the buffer between North's ambitions and his paranoia.
North's vault: he leaves a vault of his centuries of research to Jason, which becomes the basis for the clan's magitech and the EOA's research.
North never fully trusted Boris, who supplied him with spirit coins.
The legacy: the superhero branding "stuck in the public imagination", and most major cities keep their own cadre of masked heroes.
Where and what: an elite guild whose house is a large but unassuming building directly across from Remore Academy in Vitesse.
It moved there after Roland Remore, a diamond-ranker, took over the guild long ago; he no longer manages it but his presence looms large.
Relationship to the Academy: after Rufus's grandfather became guild leader it became more associated with the Remore Academy.
Farrah introduces herself in Rimaros as Burning Violet out of Vitesse.
Standards: "elite amongst elites", yet not prejudicial about background; large enough to need head-breakers as well as politicians and ritualists.

Application: the chief membership officer, Neiman Bassingthwaite, tells Jason his membership "threatens to be the flashpoint that could set the whole guild ablaze": people opposed to the Remore family's control of the guild see Roland looming over it, and Jason's closeness to the family and the Adventure Society's treatment of him as a diamond-ranker would inflame them.
The royal family's guild in Rimaros.
The pre-eminent producer of defensive engineering in the Storm Kingdom: the defences of many cities and fortress towns, including Rimaros, are designed and maintained by the house.
Zara was matched with a member of the family (the cause of the scandal in). See 06_Places/Rimaros.md.
A school in Vitesse run by Roland Remore, the diamond arch-chancellor, who is rarely seen on campus but whose presence is felt.
Rufus, Farrah and others are graduates; connections only open the door to the prestigious guilds, and the Academy gives its graduates the skills to walk through it.
Allayeth explains in Book 10: a collection of wealthy aristocrats and a few very wealthy merchant barons who own most of the land in the region and provide most of the jobs.
In his own thoughts he has concluded that the faction is weak, foolish and oblivious to its path to self-destruction and that the ship must be drydocked and burned to ashes so a new one can be built.
The living document: a marble-and-gold tablet, connected to a central record, that updates as the record changes and holds the full list of every essence and essence combination known to the Society.
Water link: the Society's chambers allow conversation at a distance (Belinda says in Book 10 that the chambers have been closed to the public since the attack on Yaresh).
Spirit coin farms: registered farms exist (Clive,: a spirit coin that did not come from "a registered spirit coin farm" implies an unregistered one that "needs to be found and shut down").

Greenstone branch: directed by Lucian Lamprey (corrupt), who uses the Fortress as his office; his deputy director Pochard Finn is an elf and a local who runs the city campus and is "the de facto director of Greenstone's Magic Society". Pochard is Clive's boss.
By Book 11 Pochard has become director: "It's Director now, Standish. I haven't been deputy director for several years".
Rakesh campus: the largest Magic Society and Adventure Society strongholds on the continent share a campus at Rakesh on the north coast. Portals work only in designated zones.
Behaviour: the Society leverages its research and secrets for political power; many prominent academics stay with it for personal gain.
The Alchemy Association has been hounding Neil for the miracle potion recipe; Jason jokes about complaining to the Artifice Association about shoddy standards. Their internal structure is unchecked.
In Greenstone's guild district the Forge Society and the Alchemist Association are "clearly second to the Adventure and Magic Societies, but still occupied impressive chunks of real estate".
Founding and role: Clive Standish builds a rival to the Magic Society.

Funding and protection: government authorities, the Adventure Society and a variety of churches, especially the Church of Knowledge, contribute, and shield it from the Magic Society's attempts to crush it.

Projects: the new sky communication network and a rumoured transportation network (the "portal network project" in Grantham's report), the result of years of study into the network Clive had tracked earlier.
Leadership: Clive is Archchancellor.

Lorelei Grantham is Vice Chancellor: she first appears in Book 3 as a researcher assigned to work with the Adventure Society's Continental Council, and in Book 6 she is an administrator in the Magic Society's astral magic research wing in Rakesh, where Clive is held.
She runs the MRA in Clive's absence and has a portal network project.
Founding and growth: "In just a handful of years since its inception, the Magical Research Association had exploded into prominence".
Clive has gone from silver-rank team member to the head of "a rival to the Magic Society".
Many prominent academics stayed with the Society for personal gain; the MRA is "a bastion for young, bold and innovative researchers".
Government authorities, the Adventure Society and several churches, especially Knowledge, contribute, and also act as a shield against the Magic Society's attempts to crush it.
Projects: it is closely associated with the new sky communication network, and rumoured to be researching a transportation network, from years of study into the network Clive tracked earlier.
Satellites solved the problem of monsters attacking relay towers.
Its portal network project is reported to Clive by Vice Chancellor Grantham.
Leadership: Clive is Archchancellor; Lorelei Grantham is Vice Chancellor.
Staff address Clive as "Archchancellor" throughout.
Security and spies: the Security Director finds a spy for the Magic Society and Clive throws him through the ceiling; staff are afraid of being thrown through the ceiling.
Campuses: the Yaresh campus stands across the road from the Alchemy Association's research centre.

Yaresh was one of the first branches, with an outdoor testing facility whose site Clive chose, between a river and a major road, so that the city's guards protect it while the Society is kept from undermining the association.
The Vitesse branch is a modest campus beside the older Magic Society's.
The Magic Society's hostility: the courts were "quite punitive" after the Magic Society was proven to be behind most of the vandalism of the Vitesse campus.
The Society has controlled long-distance communication through the water link for centuries and is working to replicate Travis's satellites.
Fame: Clive is famous as much for the Magic Society's hatred of him as for his organisation's success.
The effect: a chamber projects things from platforms along its walls.
Those inside feel everything as real, including the impact of blows, while their bodies lie unharmed in the control room.
Illusions can only affect, and be affected by, other illusions the chamber creates.
Control: a stone block under the control room window carries runes and diagrams; Rufus edits its monster imprints.
Clive knows older stone-slab controls and has helped rebuild chambers in Boko and Hornis.
Limits: low magical density restricts the Geller chamber to bronze-rank level for limited periods. No chamber can simulate a whole world.
Higher magical density allows dimensional magic to replicate vast spaces and run several chambers at once.
Business: it hires out training space and is the city's premier entertainment venue, with essence users facing each other or illusory challenges before a paying audience.
Standing: the Association "had close ties with the Magic Society, Adventure Society and local government" and enjoys significant power and influence in Jayapura.
Setting: it is a flat circular building at the edge of the Mystic Quarter, spilling into the theatre district.
Leagues: two leagues a year in silver, bronze and iron divisions, leading to the grand championships; there is no gold division because the professionals stop using cores before gold.
Management: the place is run by former participants, now gold rank.
The Greenstone chamber belongs to the Geller family.
Emir says they were "scoured from this world, root and branch, by a coalition of churches".
The church of the Unliving and another church formed "an unholy compact" to remove it.

The last grandmaster: when the churches found the training facilities beneath Sky Scar Lake, the last grandmaster sent the initiates into a sealed astral space and scattered the keys, so that someone worthy might one day reclaim what was left.
The churches, locked out, made a second bargain with the vorger, deep-astral entities that warp those they touch into flesh abominations.
Shade tells Jason the Order "does not maintain a roster of assassins at all" but a "volunteer network" of quiet allies.
Skill books: the Order's techniques are designed from the foundation to include skill-book use.
The cult: it "operates in that world, or it once did", but the Reaper does not speak to it directly, which would trespass on the local god of death.
The Church does public-facing things and the cult can be its "hidden dagger".
Cult versus order: "The Order of the Reaper is an offshoot of the cult", a faction that wanted to become more active in the world and accrue political power.
The Sky Scar Lake remnant was a faction that wanted reconciliation with the cult and was "sacrificed for it".
The cult is hard to infiltrate because it is impossible to fake long-term.
Arabelle summarises the difference: the cult follows the Reaper's principles; the order is the offshoot.
The Reaper's view: a vessel-form of the Reaper tells Jason the order "paid only lip service to my principles while using my name in the pursuit of secular power".
The Reaper says the techniques of the Way were developed by his cult and are traditionally restricted to individuals raised within the cult and trained for decades.
Shade's contact: before returning to Earth, the World-Phoenix's avatar contacted the cult's counterpart and persuaded him to let Shade, a shadow of the Reaper, act as a vessel.
The long plan: the order is bringing "centuries of planning" to fruition around twenty-five years before.
It faked the demise of its entire order as part of a plan "more than half a millennium in the making".
Method: it infiltrates other organisations, including low-level administrative staff of churches, where deep faith is not required.
Its aim is to return to being an open secret "playing tool to those in power while pulling the levers of power themselves"; the first time, it was "too crude and got crushed".
Strikes against threats: it made critical strikes against the Church of Purity, the Cult of the Builder and other threats, having infiltrated them and let them grow dangerous first.
The cult suspects it also knew about the messengers.
She hid a husband and daughter, Sophie, and was discovered when Sophie was small.
Marta Fries: Melody's best friend in the order, who warned her and helped smuggle the husband and Sophie out.
Fries is under scrutiny after Melody's defection, and later helps trace Melody.
They investigated the order together for years, but the cult never truly accepted her. He is in love with her.

The search: Callum steered Emir and a diamond-rank historian friendly to the cult towards collecting Way of the Reaper skill books, hoping a stray user of the techniques would turn up Melody's husband.
That is how Sophie and Emir came to Marta Fries.
The Purity infiltration: the cult required Melody to infiltrate the Order of Redeeming Light as a momentous gesture before it would accept her, over Callum's objection.
She was "cleansed" and became an artificial zealot, and Callum lost track of her.
Melody and Jason: she fights Jason using the Way of the Reaper and says she was trained in it before he was born.
Her therapy and the Flames' damage are covered in Melody_Jain.md and.

A joint force of churches: Jason's account of events on Pallimustus says the original order was "eliminated by a joint force of churches" in an event engineered with Knowledge's help, which also killed priests who would have troubled the fake Purity.
Shade's brother: Umber says he has "been building up their numbers" while preparing for Shade's escape.
Jason says Umber created whatever Thadwick Mercer has become and has turned the order into more of the same.
A bigger conflict: Shade tells Jason he believes the events of the treasure hunt were part of "a much larger and longer conflict".
The old magic: "The Cabal represents the old magic of this world. Things older than history that dwell in the dark places".
It is one of the three dominant forces beside the Network and the EOA, with a tight grip on old money.
A loose collection: it "was always a loose collection of factions".

Its members are creatures of many kinds: a troll-blooded fae who shapeshifts to pass for human in rural pubs, and contingents that include a thirteen-foot fur-covered humanoid with a mane of mossy hair.
Concealment: Dawn says the Cabal's members "have become experts at hiding their presence over the centuries".
Many believed the angelic founders were a myth.
Its official line on Jason: Vermillion says it is the Cabal's position that Jason's liberty and independence be respected.
Rivalry with the EOA: the EOA's research into blood servants causes conflicts with the Cabal, which dislikes having its people kidnapped as research materials.
Help in the monster waves: individual factions help in places such as Siberia and the South Pacific where the Network is thin.
Stronger in the zones: transformation zones make Cabal members stronger, since many had hit a ceiling in a world not magical enough, and the Cabal starts to approach parity with the Network.
They rush to wake their ancient ones, and the rest of the Cabal "reluctantly went along due to the need to compete with the Network".
Lord Willoughby has been hibernating in a sarcophagus since 1794.
The attack on Sydney: the Cabal makes an open assault on the Network building in the Sydney CBD, after which authorities cordon off the area.
Splinters: Craig Vermillion leads a splinter faction that does not work with the old vampires, and by Book 6 the Cabal has fragmented.
Some have formed a non-vampiric new Cabal and others have joined the Global Defence Network.

The Arisen: William Spencer, an ancient vampire and one of the Arisen (the vampires' own name), says not all of them want global dominion, and some are looking to carve out a place for themselves after the vampires lose.
Boris's claim: Boris tells Jason's team "We founded the Cabal".
Jason's briefing says the magical elements hidden on Earth "ultimately formed the Cabal to keep their secrets".
"The whole mess caused a schism in the Cabal and cleaning house was ugly. We cast out any vampires that sided with the risen lords willingly".
The vampires seized a lot of power in the Cabal, which cost Boris's quiet influence.
Territory: the Cabal holds some of the UK and Scandinavia, and displaces Network factions in areas such as Russia and Africa.
It has "unambiguously split" from the lords and those who followed them.
Safe zones: safe zones for vampires who are not with the lords exist mostly where the Cabal holds sway.
Hierarchy: Boris stands at the top; a member says to him "you're at least five steps above me in the Cabal hierarchy".

Under Boris: openly led by Boris Ketland, the Cabal is "highly aggressive with their economic and social programs": he "toppled governments and cut some of the world's most exploitative business practices off at the knees".
Its humanitarian work since going public is far ahead of the UN team's.
The vampire lords: besides Elizabeth, who rules Venice, the books name Wassily, Klaus and Georges and Magdalyn, one of the strongest surviving vampire lords.

A federation, not a hierarchy: "the Network isn't one large hierarchy. It's an organisation of old secret societies and the International Committee is more like a United Nations than an overlord. The branches are members, not subordinates".
The International Committee (IC): it holds local offices, such as the Canberra office, and global executives; Asya represents it in Sydney.
Only the agreement of a majority of member branches can act punitively against a branch; the IC itself has no such authority.
Branches: the books name Sydney, Lyon, Fiji (as a joke about living on a beach) and Berlin, where Cleary and Gerling work at the branch with its own grid monitoring station and Steering Committee.
The IC also has offices in Brussels, Shanghai, New York, Johannesburg and Cairo.
Steering committees: each branch has one, which directs the agenda and takes high-level decisions; the Sydney committee has eight members and Anna is promoted into it.
Divisions: a branch has an Operations Director (Adrien Barbou in Lyon), a Director of Tactical Operations (Koen in Sydney), and a Harvest Division headed by Eustace Brown.
The Research Division has been "divorced from specific branches and brought under the umbrella of the International Committee" so that breakthroughs are shared across the Network.
Tactical teams: the Sydney tactical presence is two platoons of three nine-person sections, with five category threes.
Nigel Thornton was a section leader there before leaving.
Spirit coins: the stronger branches in the US, China and Russia are the primary source of spirit coins and resist placing tactical forces under the IC.
The Sydney branch has none of its own and depends on the IC.
Ranks: Network categories zero to five match the ranks on Pallimustus.

Who gets what: all executive-level personnel are given essences to reach category one; cores are mostly saved for lower-ranked enforcement members on the front line, and only committee members like Keith go to category two with cores.
What it is: the Grid exists to identify and monitor dimensional spaces, and every branch has access to it.
How simple it is: Farrah says it is "so basic that it doesn't seem magical at all", based on principles "so sophisticated they work back around to being simple".

A concealed sector: in 1948 the Lyon branch's committee hid an incursion space that had become permanent near Saint-Étienne by disabling the Grid in that area, and the sector has been offline for seventy years.
Its failure: the EOA's sabotage of the Grid let proto-astral spaces break down and eject monsters, the monster wave crisis.

Research: Farrah led a Network workgroup that fixed the sabotage; the people in it became the first outside Emi to be systematically trained in core magical fundamentals, but they are forbidden to pass on knowledge of the Grid.

The public name: the Network "had become known to the public as the Global Defense Network in the weeks since the monster waves began", presented as the government response through "supernatural task forces".
The EOA's campaign: the EOA tried to swing public opinion so strongly that governments would give it a seat at the table.
Anger at the IC: branches resent resources being allocated to fighting alongside the Americans, and Berlin is furious at losing people to the IC's order.

Four blocs: by Book 6 the Network is split into the US branches and the old leadership faction (still calling themselves the Network), the Chinese branches, the True Network (the former IC, which keeps many government links and powerful members), and the Global Defence Network (rank and file with ex-EOA and Cabal members).
The US branches staged a secret coup of the US government.
The Chinese and US governments absorbed or were absorbed by their branches, and the largest faction was born from the leadership of the other branches.
Certification: before Jason registers with the Magic Society, he is told to visit the Temple of Death for formal confirmation that he is who he claims, "returned from death".
The paperwork helps with the Magic Society and a certification from the Church of Death serves as identification.
The certificate: Jason's certification says he has died four times, "so far".
The temple: it looks like a memorial centre, with white stone, manicured gardens and clergy in white robes.
Verification of deaths: it is needed to confirm that neither of two missing adventurers had made a miraculous last-minute escape.
Watching for undead: "The Adventure Society and the Church of Death especially" do not give the Church of Undeath the chance to act, so it lies dormant for generations.
The cult: "The cult often works with the Church of Death... as they are closely aligned. The church does more public-facing things for the cult, while the cult can be the church's hidden dagger".
Temple: in Greenstone it is "the strange temple" on the Divine Square, called the temple of Dominion.
Control of clergy: other churches make little call on adventuring clergy; Dominion's is the most prominent outlier in keeping low-ranking essence users under its thumb.
Absent priests: a character thought power and control were the church's remit, but has "never even met a priest of Dominion".
The god's description: Dominion tells Jason he is "oppression-friendly", not an oppressor.
The church does not venerate power itself, "but the establishment of power over others. Rulership. The exercising of authority".
He calls slavery "a petty tyranny" compared to what the god looks to.
Priests: Gwydion Remore, Rufus's older brother, is a priest of Hero.
Relics: the church has collected the relics of dead demigods for millennia.
The temple: a sculpture of a leonid in bronze, silver and gold with dark iron stands in the middle of the boulevard before the temple of Hero in the Worship Ring of Outer Rexion.
Assessors: the Adventure Society's assessments are checked by a priest of the church of Knowledge: "Don't try to slip anything past them, because there isn't any point".
Temple: in Greenstone the Temple of Knowledge is the plain, blocky building on the Divine Square.
The temple library is used by researchers and the goddess "always welcomes seekers of truth".
Acolytes and dress: its members wear recognisable regalia.
Answer room: the Vitesse temple has an "answer room" where the goddess manifests.

Rimaros: the main Temple of Knowledge there stands on a sky island apart from the temple district and has a "symbiotic relationship" with the Magic Society branch, with a chamber for incoming portals.
Authentication: it is reluctant to hire out clergy to authenticate valuables.
Education: it "does what it can" for education, but meets pushback from nobility.
Quiet muster: "The Church of Knowledge has been building up fighting forces around the globe. Slowly but steadily, over the last fifteen years or so"; no one knows why, even its own people.
Cover blown: the force is mobilised on a single day, after which it no longer cared about being noticed. The god War alone knew its scale.
Reaching out: a priest of Knowledge contacts Jason's team because of Jason's relationship with the goddess.
Representatives: Gabrielle Pellin, a young priestess, is assigned to Travis as a shadow and representative and is a priestess of the Church of Knowledge.
Funding: it is one of the churches that funds and shields the Magical Research Association.
Annexation: it annexes the island that anchors the bridge on the Pallimustus side.
Plan: in Jason's account Knowledge helped Disguise pose as Purity, and in return Disguise brought the Network founder into his church.
Healers and cleansers: the church sends a healer, a girl from the Lasalle family, with Rufus's party. Anisa Lasalle is a priestess of Purity.
Contracts: it makes noise about the completion bonus after Anisa leaves, but the contract was through the Adventure Society and was paid.

Rituals: the archbishop prepares a ritual circle of silver-rank spirit coins and orbs; such rituals "draw on the power of ambient magic but are infused with the glorious might of the divine. My god's will moves the magic and not the other way around".
He is emotionless and cold at the death of Jonah Geller.
Star seeds: the church first developed the extraction techniques and the archbishop holds its records on them.
