The archbishop: the book calls him Nicolas Hendren but also "Herston, the archbishop of Purity" in one scene, and Book 3 spells it "Hedron" once.

sec: 3. The fall of the Greenstone leadership
claim: Vanishing: following the revelation of Purity's apparent involvement with the Builder cult, the archbishop vanishes along with other key members on "previously scheduled sabbaticals".

sec: 3. The fall of the Greenstone leadership
claim: The Healer's new Chief Priest takes his seat at the war council.

sec: 3. The fall of the Greenstone leadership
claim: The Lasalle family: Anisa and "much of the Lasalle family" vanish with the archbishop (see Anisa_Lasalle.md).

sec: 4. The ecumenical council and the false god
claim: Council: the churches convene an ecumenical council to judge the church's behaviour; it finds the church "had been operating well outside its dictates for some time".

sec: 4. The ecumenical council and the false god
claim: People from the church are detained under its authority.
The Order of Redeeming Light is a creation of Disguise masquerading as Purity; its "Flames of Redemption" are an extreme modification of lesser vampirism.
It takes in people from outside the faithful. See Cults_and_Orders.md.
Jason's account says Disguise took over Purity's position and had Knowledge's help in removing Purity's loyal priests, including through the destruction of the Order of the Reaper.
A past plague: a zombie plague had "a Temple of Undeath at the heart of it all", with the local mayor as high priest.
Why it is stamped out: those who fall to the undead become undead servants, allies and enemies alike, "why they are so thoroughly stamped out whenever and wherever they are found".
Dormancy: "The Church of Undeath does not act frequently. We don't give them the chance".
It is one of the few reliable allies of the Church of Destruction.
Opportunity: a place of magic gone wrong and a hidden location is "a veritable wish list" for it.
Priests: dozens of priests of Undeath, gold and silver rank, lead the army.
They use their god's power to feed on elemental magic and make more powerful undead.
Leadership: Garth Larosse is the High Priest, himself an unliving thing nine feet tall, in a dark green cloak. He leads the priests.
Claiming: the high priest "could not himself" hold claim over the unliving's unified territories, which an avatar then does.
A holy war: an undead army led by priests of Undeath is raised as a question of whether it counts as a holy war.
Rexion: the Undeath priesthood overran the domains of the gods in the old brightheart city.
Jason says building a temple of Undeath would be repugnant, as a drastic act.

Healing service: "Most healing was done through the church of the Healer"; the god supplies the essences and awakening stones; its priests can be sought out for a fee and send people to other healers.
Local reach: it is "really important in isolated areas", though "more than one church leader has been known to go a bit power mad".
Members are found in multiple towns and villages on the road to Greenstone.
Hierarchy: the Greenstone temple stands on the Divine Square, led by a Chief Priest who arrives with bronze-rankers, iron-rankers and lesser clergy behind.
The basic robe is simple brown, though the Greenstone group wore white-and-gold silks with brown embellishments.
High Priestess is the title at city level.
Adventuring clergy: like most faiths, the church makes little call on the time of adventuring clergy. Neil Davone is a long-time churchman.
A replacement priest, Donal Lange, arrives through a portal the Healer creates.
Priests then stop charging for services.
The new Chief Priest: after Purity's Greenstone leaders vanish, the new Chief Priest of the Healer takes the vanished archbishop's place at the war council.
Sanctuary: the Healer makes Jory's clinic sanctified ground, which stops others breaking in for the formula.
Star-seed work: "The church of the Healer has taken over from Purity in dealing with the star seeds"; the Healer provided the rituals.
Carlos Quilido, a gold-rank priest, is the specialist.
Mental health: Arabelle Remore is a member specialising in mental health and trauma recovery.
Mandate: the church gives Jory a mandate and funding to spread his methods around the world. It has its own skyships.
Summons: it can call away members such as Jory.
Yaresh: Hana Shavar is High Priestess of the Healer in Yaresh and takes personal charge of refugees.
At the front: the Healer clergy at the war council are Arabelle, Neil, Carlos and Hana, and the Healer priestess runs a hospital in Jason's palace.
Origin and links: "an old guild, but after Rufus' grandfather became guild leader, it became more and more associated with the Remore Academy".
Its membership is Rufus's family plus allies such as Gary and Farrah.
Members: most big-family graduates of the Academy do not join, so it is mostly graduates who do not come from power or money.
The Academy's scouting programme gives scholarships to people with potential.
Symbol: purple flames in the shape of a flower on a belt buckle.
Farrah introduces herself as "Burning Violet guild, although I don't have a guild pin on me".
Induction: Miles Cotezee says Jason's team has been "inducted into the Burning Violet".
By Book 11 all of Team Biscuit are members except Jason and Taika.
It moved there when Roland Remore took over the guild long ago; he no longer manages it, but his presence loomed large.
It has four sets of double doors and a cavernous lobby.
Standing: Burning Violet members "are elite amongst elites".
The guild is exclusive but big, with room for "head-breakers" as well as politicians and ritualists.
The guild is "not prejudicial as to the background of our members", so its roster is eclectic.
The contention: two factions in the executive, one wanting the guild free of the Remore family's influence and one opposed.
Jason's membership "threatens to be the flashpoint that could set the whole guild ablaze".
Outcome: Team Biscuit withdraws from the guild.
Action quotas: after clearance an adventurer is "assigned an action quota" and must report regularly to the jobs hall for contracts.
"Action quotas are the minimum requirements every adventurer has to fulfil during the monster surge".
The contribution board: contracts taken beyond the quota carry contribution point values, tallied on weekly and overall leaderboards, with rewards each week and major rewards at the end of the surge.
A large leaderboard in the jobs hall shows the top hundred contributors by action quota.

Who pays for the rewards: societies, associations and governments give out hefty rewards; in return the Adventure Society "assigns high contribution point values to the contracts that provide that protection".

What guilds want: the big guilds monopolise the top of the board, but want "access to civic services" and organisational benefits from the Adventure Society, Magic Society and Alchemy Association, not material rewards.
Material rewards are the lower-rung prizes, which small guilds and independents can reach.
The numbers: Rufus says that in the city (Rimaros) about three in ten adventurers are in a guild and one in ten in a high-end one, yet "guilds are given sixty percent of the quotas to fill".
Guilds have the highest quotas to beat before they reach the boards.
The Society handles their large quotas through liaison officers, "a test for the guilds to prove they deserved the privileges they enjoyed".
Not shielded: the royal family does not shield the Sapphire Crown from the quotas.
Rules: normal rewards are suspended in a surge and handed out weekly on the leaderboard; some contracts do not count towards the quota or leaderboard.
Escalation: after losses minimum action quotas are raised and safety standards lowered.
Purpose: in many places the role of guard had become ceremonial; "in Rimaros, the solution came in the form of a guild".

Royal support: it is one of the most powerful guilds in Rimaros because of the support of the royal family, many of whom are among its most capable members; in return all non-royal members "were required to periodically serve within the royal guard".
All members are examined quarterly, rising to monthly or weekly while serving in the guard.
Trenchant Moore, a human gold-ranker in a guild of celestines, carries a good portion.
Liberty: even its gold-rankers have "a rich amount of liberty", an exception to the usual monitoring of gold-rankers.
Standing: Liara is "a figure of accomplishment and respect in the Sapphire Crown", where power, not legacy, is the ultimate authority.
Operations: it joins Amouz family members in sweeping the Builder cult's hideouts, watches over a familiar ritual, and uses the duelling arena as a training hall.
Royal guards: a speaker recalls being one of the iron-rankers from the guild assigned as royal guards, with no camaraderie; a character is asked whether she has considered switching to it.
Duty and power: Arabelle notes it has "more personal power than the royal family, but they've been instilled with ideals of duty".
At the outpost: it has been present at the Storm Kingdom outpost since its early days, with a full contingent led by Trenchant Moore.
Origin: Jason says Valdis, "Prince of the Mirror Kingdom", is "the reason their team exists".
Humphrey says its members "were being prepared for Valdis's team before any of them ever received an essence".
Structure: "their team is built around their healer, Sigrid. She facilitates and directs strategy"; the strategic core is Sigrid and the political core is Valdis.
The match: in the mirage chamber fight Jason's team defeats it by going for Sigrid while feinting at Valdis.
Team Biscuit's friends: Team Shining Scabbard came through the Reaper trials and trained with Jason's team at iron rank, and Sigrid is Valdis's wife.

Royal backing: the Mirror King's own portal specialist portals the team to Yaresh, and Valdis says "the kingdom's thick with princes and princesses", so the King will take a good adventurer over any of his children.
The team has royalty in the group, "less impressive with the Mirror Kingdom's surplus of princes and princesses".
Administration: Valdis assembles the arena event in under two days, admired by the duke.
Business: House Amouz "controls or has an interest in more than half of the mining operations in the Sea of Storms, including the bulk of high-rank mineral acquisition".
Ties to the royals: Liara's husband married out of House Amouz into the royal family, but remains a high-level manager in the family's business interests.
Heir: Gibson Amouz is "son of Lord Cassin Amouz and heir to the seat of House Amouz".
He is captured by the cult, which wants the family's secrets.
Lord Cassin: a gold-ranker with a goatee, who confronts Liara over his son's capture.
Liara suspects the son was targeted because of what he would be told on becoming gold rank and ready to assume his seat.
Volunteers: the Amouz family volunteers in numbers that surprise even Liara in the sweep of the hideouts.
Mercer ties: "the Davone and Kettering families, with their close ties to the Mercers" sent their boys to the Mercer compound, where Neil spent time as a boy.
Teaming: the Davone and Mercer families "colluded to team him with Thadwick Mercer at a young age".
Servants to the Mercers: Neil's family had been "stuck as what amounts to servants to the Mercers for years" but now the most powerful people in the city must show them respect.
House Davone: in Book 12 Neil escorts three of House Davone's young scions, his nieces and nephews.
The estate: the Geller family estate sits behind a thick high wall, so vast that monsters are as likely to be inside as out; household guards are iron-rank essence users.
The seat is "a sprawling estate in the delta", landscaped on secure ground with artful waterways and decades of defences.
Standing: "The Geller family stood at the peak of Greenstone society, and their local power was just a fragment of their world-spanning influence".
The family "sprawled across continents", and branch families exist: one patriarch leads a branch family.
Training: Geller family tradition is to supply scions with enough awakening stones to get started, while the rest must be earned.
The family trains its young at "the south end of nowhere" so they can make their own mistakes, with facilities including a mirage chamber and arena.
Why Greenstone: other Greenstone families envy the influence the Gellers hold elsewhere and want outside connections.
Some families "simply wanted the next adventure", as the Gellers do.
The academy annex: the Remore Academy's Greenstone annex is a joint venture with the Gellers, with an internal Geller faction opposed to the agreement.
No title but one: the Gellers hold only the title linked to their small provincial city of origin, refusing all others.
They are "technically aristocracy in some inconsequential city-state somewhere" and their prestige is as an adventuring dynasty.
Everywhere: "There are Gellers everywhere, Mr Asano. You'd have to ask the Church of Fertility about that".
Branches have towers in Cyrion and estates in Rimaros.
The seat in Greenstone: the family kept Greenstone as its seat even as its power spread, for the experience it gives the young.
Training methodology: "you don't understand just how deep Geller family training goes", and people scramble to be on a team with a Geller who went through the Greenstone programme.
Wealth and politics: "The Gellers have more money than any other family in Greenstone", and mostly keep to their compound and stay out of local politics.
Its most elite training programme is in Greenstone, entered on Danielle's introduction.
Standing: Garret Headingway is "an upper-echelon member of House Headingway, one of Estercost's pre-eminent families".

Percival Headingway is the patriarch and Duke, "holder of the family's highest title", which "came from Cyrion", unlike the claimed titles of rural city-state aristocrats; he serves under the throne but his power "dwarfed even the most prestigious of theirs".
Power: "the true power of House Headingway came from their adventurers"; adventurer training had been mandatory in the family when Percival was young.
Ben: Benjamin Headingway is the family's top gold-ranker and represents the noble houses of Cyrion when they ask to speak to Jason.
Factions: one faction, "the pure politicians", wants a proportional political reply; Percival knows they are wrong.
Mariska Headingway manages business affairs.
Pressure: the Sky Link Company decides whether "continuing a relationship with House Headingway is appropriate".
The affair: the Dominion church keeps the captured family members from genuine danger.
Mercer ties: the Davone and Kettering families have "close ties to the Mercers" and send their boys to Thadwick.
Adventurers: Hudson Kettering is on Beth Cavendish's team.
Dustin Kettering, a local, takes Jonah's defender role in Rick's team.
Old City: "The Ketterings have people in Old City"; Danielle coordinates with the Kettering family to mobilise them.
Dustin: a friend of Neil's from Thadwick's team.
His family obliged him to work with the Mercers.
The family ranks above many others, especially those without aristocratic title.
Residence: their main residence is a manor on the Island, five towers set in a ring connected by glass walkways, "a feat of magical engineering".
Numbers: no family can match the Gellers' numbers, but the Mercers "still made an impressive showing".
Farms: Humphrey says most of the spirit coin farms are operated by his family or the Mercers, under Magic Society regulation.
The Mercers do not offer part ownership as the Gellers do.
Household: the household staff are "raked over the coals" when Thadwick is provoked.
Patronage: "Thadwick had needed friends his own age and the Davone and Kettering families, with their close ties to the Mercers, had frequently sent their own boys over".
Neil Davone grew up at the Mercer compound.
Obligation: Neil and Dustin were forced to train and work with Thadwick through their families' obligation to the Mercers.
The Mercer family gave Neil training, facilities and resources "that only the Gellers could match".
The Mercer family is large and Thadwick was raised mainly by his father.
The Academy: the family "operates the Remore Academy, which is a big deal everywhere, not just Vitesse".
It runs a Greenstone training annex built with the Gellers.
Roland: "Although Roland Remore was rarely spotted on the Remore Academy campus, the presence of the diamond-rank arch-chancellor was always felt".
Rufus as heir: Rufus "was the prince of Remore Academy, the talented heir-apparent to the power and prestige of his family legacy".
Graduates: an academy graduate should have better control of her aura, so students have standing among adventurers.
No title: the Remore family has no aristocratic title; the family's prestige comes from "generations of accomplishment", not their name.
Like other prestige families they are offered titles and refuse.
Scholarships: Rufus's grandfather set up a scouting programme for people with potential, with scholarships and dormitories.
Students: scions of international mercantile guilds, adventuring families, aristocrats and royalty, taught by methodology studied from across the globe.
The family nurtured Rufus's talent with carefully engineered opportunities.
Guild influence: some in the Burning Violet guild think the Academy has too much influence over guild affairs.
Gold-rankers: the Academy is famous for recruiting adventurers near or at gold rank as faculty.
The control of the guild: the Remore family's control of Burning Violet is contested by one faction in the executive (see Burning_Violet.md).
Teaching: Remore teaching is "built around the concept of individualised outcomes", with the most effort for those who show drive.
Allies: they are known allies of Jason: "The son of the Remores is on his team".
The guild: the royal family supports the Sapphire Crown, and many of its own are among its most capable members. See Sapphire_Crown.md.
The union would have created political stability before the surge.
Liara's husband was born into House Amouz.
Family traits: Zareen has "the royal family's sapphire hair and eyes".
Liara: a gold-rank member of the royal house, in charge of screening adventurers for Builder cultists (see Liara_Rimaros.md).
Zara: although she left the royal family for political reasons, "the Storm King did not stop caring for his daughter".

sec: 1. How to use the Places files
claim: The Great Southern Continent is named only once, as a stop on the team's route south in Book 9, and has no file.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Greenstone, a delta city in the low-magic far south of the Africa-like continent, is a colony settled from Estercost a few centuries ago (calls Estercost the land from which Greenstone was colonised; says most Greenstoners descend from Estercost immigrants).

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Kazlahk is a city of sandstone, palm trees and money on Estercost's eastern coast, surrounded by desert and valuable for higher-magic spirit coin farms.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Its notable institution is the Kazlahk University of Medicine.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Yaresh: a rainforest city of a few tens of thousands with a natural array beneath it.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Boko: a desert academic city north of Greenstone, destroyed in Book 12 when the blast containment zone gave out after the System Administrator's assassination; most of its ninety thousand people were evacuated by Jason's aura before the blast, and the floating temples shielded by their gods remained.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: The survivors were housed in New Water, an oasis city Jason named in his astral kingdom, where the Duke of Boko still holds management meetings.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Zartos: a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines; it is the home of the diamond-rank smith Virid Martine and his smithy, where Gary and Virid reforge Dread Salvation.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Rakesh on the north coast hosts a Magic Society campus that blocks portals outside designated zones; Hornis is a port to the south, reached from Greenstone across the delta and the Veldt.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Book 6 places the continental council of the Africa-like continent at Rakesh, and a different passage places an Adventure Society continental council in Cyrion, so there appears to be one council per continent; Book 6 also puts the Adventure Society's continental council in Vitesse rather than Cyrion, a conflict left open.

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Foreign lands named at a distance: Kurdansk (in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil; Sophie's birthplace), Pranay (the Sri Lanka equivalent; its port city Jayapura, Hester's birthplace, has a vast mirage chamber complex,; the island is larger and further south than Earth's, in the middle of the Indian Ocean equivalent; a portal stopover and one of the isolated city-states on the way to Estercost), Girlano (an inland nation south of the Storm Kingdom's coast, a kingdom in name but controlled by cartels; its border city is Casallini), Sadi Andali (a country whose slave markets are named in, where Jason's price is their destruction), Segurado (a small city-state in what would be Uruguay; messengers attack it in Book 12), Jorganis (a small island in the Pacific equivalent, almost entirely covered by a grimy city outside any society's or government's authority) and the Dragon Lands (the Antarctica equivalent, home of the draconians, named for subterranean apertures to a realm of fire that make volcanoes, hot springs and "dragon mouth" geysers; its farm exports pass through Greenstone's port).

sec: 2.1 The nations and cities named in the books
claim: Ruins and sites: Cartise (a river city destroyed when the Builder cult claimed a nearby astral space), Isart (a city on Jason's procession south that Emir asks him to reach), Arcazitlan (a fortress town attacked by bone feasters).
Clive rates Greenstone's density as about mid-iron, "which is very low".
The books give no numeric figure for Vitesse but place it a band higher: typical monsters are silver-rank, with frequent gold and occasional diamond (see Vitesse.md).
Vitesse (spoiler level 0): Vitesse, in the kingdom of Estercost, is the City of Flowers, "located in what Jason Asano would know as the French Riviera" (Book 1,...
Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom (spoiler level 2): Jason's personal space grows over the series: a dimensional inventory that only he can physically enter (: "others cannot be invited or...
Dimensional Artefact Site One (Australia) (spoiler level 3): Dimensional Artefact Site One, called the artefact city, is "a small city" in outback Australia, with "nine thousand or so workers"...
Casselton and Asano Village (spoiler level 1): Casselton Beach is Jason's hometown, a tourist beach town on the Mid-North Coast of New South Wales where he was born.
Hornis (spoiler level 1): Hornis is a port city on the coast south and around from Greenstone, reached overland through the delta, the veldt and then south (Book...
Jayapura (spoiler level 1): Jayapura is a port on the northern coast of Pranay, the large southern land equivalent to Sri Lanka, and the birthplace of Hester.
Kurdansk (spoiler level 2): Kurdansk is a river city in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil and Sophie Wexler's birthplace.
Leust (spoiler level 1): Leust is one of the largest and richest towns in the delta, with paved roads and stone buildings instead of mud brick.
The Storm Kingdom's Islands (spoiler level 2): The Storm Kingdom is a nation of islands in the Sea of Storms, the Caribbean analogue, founded by Soramir Rimaros.
From the air it stretches to the horizon in every direction; "Cyrion looked like Tokyo by way of the Emerald City of Oz" from the air, with massive lakes and whole forests inside the urban sprawl.
Book 7 calls it home to the Adventure Society's continental council, though Book 6 puts that council in Vitesse.

A series of concentric walls rings the city proper, with vast spans of agricultural land in between, "some of the most magical and valuable growing land on the planet" and under "impressive protection".
It is closer than Vitesse to the site of the operation that became a debacle of magical explosions, summoned messengers and unexpected outworlders.

Beyond the outermost wall lie the remains of the Builder cult's attack from before the messenger invasion: the toppled, overgrown forms of the Builder's world engineer golems, which rival diamond-rank monsters in size and look more like hills than engines of war ("almost two decades after their demise"); the messengers had made no attempt to invade Cyrion.
Seat of the Estercost crown (the monarch is a queen in; her name was not found) and the Adventure Society's continental council.

Cyrion's laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families, and house guards were technically a form of indentured servitude. Very well-paid servitude"; many noble houses use that power to keep guards from leaving.
The Queen of Estercost is not named in the chapters read.
Duke Percival Headingway, patriarch of House Headingway, holds a title from Cyrion.

Made of set-state authority. Jason's spirit domains are made of set-state authority, "the treehouse that I'm allowed to play in", and he thinks that if they broke down into potential-state authority it would kill him (see../02_Cosmology_and_Powers/Authority_and_Sanctioning.md).
A claimed zone becomes one. In a transformation zone, claiming a territory puts his influence on it; once his influence is already established, others cannot contest the claim.
Claiming a territory also claims the inhabitants in stasis in it, who are imparted with the claimant's influence.
A zone's domain covers the whole zone. At the Saint-Étienne zone he extends his senses "throughout his domain, which covered the entirety of the transformation zone".
Growth. He wants the domain to grow large enough that even his powers could be restored inside the zone.
He senses everyone inside. Jason can always sense people within his spirit domain, even from across the world, and everything inside it.
His aura senses extend across the domain.
Memory. In his domains "he saw everything"; if he wanted to watch something that happened seven years ago in a corner of Rexion, the memory came to him.
Known to others. The Australian military assumes he knows everything that happens in his territory; the protocol is not to speak restricted information aloud on Asano ground.
Farrah says his perception within his territory is "absolute" and "quite well known".
Limits. In Cardinas an avatar of Jason cannot go beyond the boundary of his domain, so he cannot rescue a blood farm kept outside it.
Sin afflictions. To act against Jason or his allies in his domain is a sin and is punished: the sin afflictions from his aura cannot be resisted.
Aura inside a sealed zone. Within a sealed zone he can use his aura within his domain, though without his aura power's effects.
Gods cannot spy. Inside his spirit domain, even gods cannot spy on him; it is like territory from which they are excluded.
Priests cut off. Church of the Healer priests are cut off from their god's influence in the spirit domain.
Gabrielle of Knowledge likewise looks as if she bit a lemon when it cuts her off from her goddess.
Portals. The spirit domain prevents portal tracking within it, but external destinations remain subject to tracking effects.
Ransacking. Outsiders who entered an earlier domain tried to ransack it, then took footpath tiles and whole trees away to examine magically; Jason sensed them throughout.
Jason says that his territories, the Asano clan lands, "function like the divine ground held by gods": mechanically they are temples of him, which matters to Knowledge's planned holy war.
He forbids anyone to make Rexion a temple.
Clan members say Jason's presence gives them a feeling of protection and belonging, which is not the experience of an outsider.
Claiming. A territory is claimed by clearing anomalies and its final boss; a single claimant must remain before a Stable Genesis Core is produced.
Uses of claimed territory. At least in a claimed territory Jason has access to his soul realm and its resources.
He can place outsiders, such as Builder cultists and brightheart survivors, in his spirit domain.
Messengers. Messengers in a claimed territory feel his aura as the incomplete but unmistakable feel of an astral king.
Spirit Vault and soul realm — Astral_Spaces/Spirit_Vault_and_Astral_Kingdom.md — Only those who trust him can enter
Astral kingdom — Astral_Spaces/Spirit_Vault_and_Astral_Kingdom.md — Appears with the Astral Throne and Gate
It was founded because its conditions suit low-end spirit coin farms: stable low magic, in a place that is also livable and close to the desert.
The Old City: "the original city of Greenstone, situated on the original harbour"; the Island was meant to be a massive breakwater.
It is built mostly from the same red and yellow stone as the desert, with a massive port along its whole shoreline, and "Old City is where the money is made, but the Island is where the money goes".
The city authorities pay little attention to it so long as the elite's interests are secure, which makes its three biggest crime lords its de facto rulers.
Districts have names from old families, such as Cavendish, whose tavern the Townhouse is the largest building there.
The Island: the affluent district built entirely of green marble.

Travel to it "was restricted without a valid reason for entry": trade and work permits admit a person to the trade lanes, and aristocrats, adventurers and residents come and go freely; a day's entry costs an iron-rank spirit coin.
Staying past sunset needs lodgings, which earn a temporary residence permit and a tracking stone.
Vehicles on the Island are magic-driven, not animal-drawn, and prices there are twice or three times Old City's.
The guild district in the north-west holds the Adventure Society campus.

The Divine Square: a huge crowded square on the Island, paved even in high-grade green stone, ringed by streets of temples that show "gods had hierarchies of their own"; booths sell religious paraphernalia, and even the flagstones are high-grade green stone.
The Temple of the Healer is one of the central temples on it and all the major temples front it.

The Fortress: a huge stone building in the grimy heart of Old City's warehouse district, "older even than the city walls", once the shelter for residents during a monster surge; now neutral ground where the Big Three divide responsibility and profit, and the best place in Old City to glimpse the Island elites.
Fights are held there in a steel cage, as Sophie's Nightingale bouts.
Transit uses loop terminals; Jason's "magic trams?" is only his guess.
The Magic Society branch is directed by Lucian Lamprey, a silver-ranker who watches Fortress fights from a viewing box.
His deputy is Pochard Finn, whose son Cassowary serves as Lucian's dogsbody.
The Big Three of the underworld: Clarissa Ventress (mansion in the canal district), Cole Silva (obsessed with Sophie) and Adris Dorgan (the "quiet one"; Elspeth Arella's father).
They keep the underworld running and avoid gang war because it draws the attention of the Island authorities.
History of the settlers: most Greenstoners descend from Estercost immigrants a few centuries ago; Boko to the north is much older, with a native population.
Adris Dorgan, once a crime lord, is mayor of Old City by Book 12; that the mayor answers to the Duke is unchecked.
Greenstone is a low-magic region where "iron-rank monsters are the norm, with a good smattering of bronze-rank".

This shapes the city: core use is nearly universal, because fighting for advancement is slow when monsters are few and weak; a bronze-rank mirage chamber can run only for short periods; there are only "forty or so silver rankers in the whole city", most semi-retired, and the narration notes that Greenstone's other silver-rankers show more of their age than Emir, Danielle and Thalia.
Almost nothing is known about the region's history before the original Greenstone Colony, as Clive observes; the Gellers' ancestors came as the region was first being settled.
Boko, the neighbouring academic city, is destroyed after Jason is assassinated there (Book 12, Ch32-33); most of its ninety thousand people are evacuated first.
The Leust lumber conspiracy plays out in autumn.
Era 7: Jason is expected "in just a few days, to great fanfare" at the Adventure Society, twenty years after he was thrown down there.
A resident says Hornis is the furthest south he has been.
Era 1: an old desert city of academics and artists with a Duke and an Adventure Society branch; Jason arrives by portal after the Ustei expedition.
Era 7: the city is destroyed in Book 12 when the blast containment zone gives out after Jason's assassination; most of its ninety thousand people are evacuated.
They shelter in Jason's astral kingdom, the crater becomes a harbour and floating temples shielded by their gods remain.
The astral city of New Water is named so that it would not be named after Boko.
Before Era 5: a river city, the major hub of trade and travel in its area.

Era 5: destroyed just before the great surge when the Builder cult claimed a nearby astral space and a diamond-rank monster overwhelmed it; ruins "like London after the Blitz" and refugees overpopulating nearby towns. Jason's team clears the ruins.
Era 5: a rainforest city of a few tens of thousands with a natural array beneath it, besieged by messengers. The Battle of Yaresh ends the siege.
Era 5-6: the Cardinas expedition descends beneath it.
Cardinas, the brightheart city, is turned into a transformation zone in Book 11.
Era 7: Yaresh remains a hub; the Valdis duel is staged in its mirage arena.
Its survivors live in Rexion, a border town in the shaft walls managed by brighthearts.
Era 4: Jason arrives in a tropical cyclone as the surge begins (Book 7, Ch5-7; see Rimaros.md); a Builder fortress-city is destroyed above Livaros in the One Day War.
Palisaros is the town where Jason settles.
Era 4 (Book 8): the Order of Redeeming Light converts towns and operates from a mountain stronghold (see Rimaros.md).
Era 7: the Storm Kingdom's ambassador Hils Jaramaris is warned against water or sky links (see Rimaros.md); Zara's brother Emiliano is Storm King.
Nitra: Era 3, a Network centre until the Kostroma-style zone forms at the end of Book 5; Jason claims it in Book 6.
Era 6-7: the clan lives in a steampunk city around a pagoda (see Nitra.md).
Saint-Étienne: Era 3, the Dimensional Fortress found in 1948, hidden for about seventy years; a second zone in Book 6 that Jason turns into a cloud city (see Saint-Etienne.md).
Era 7: a refugee city and clan centre where Erika and Ian live.

Casselton and Asano Village: Era 3, Jason's home and then the family compound, evacuated when the Grid is sabotaged; Era 6, the clan lives in Jason's astral domains in Europe (Book 11, Ch68); Era 7, seized by the Australian government in Book 12 and made a special-interest territory in Book 13 (see Casselton_and_Asano_Village.md).
Era 3-7: Vitesse is the City of Flowers on the Riviera; Cyrion's analytical office tracks Jason in Book 6 and Jason studies Clive's bridge work there in Book 12 (see Cyrion.md).
Beyond Cyrion's wall lie the toppled Builder golems from before the messenger invasion.
Era 7: the noble houses' abuse of indenture law triggers the System withdrawal (see Cyrion.md); a mob gathers outside Jason's palace after the System goes dark.
Rakesh: Era 3, Clive is recruited and imprisoned on its campus.
Kurdansk: Era 3, Sophie's birthplace searched by the team.
Dragon Lands: Era 7, seen from Jason's sky ship.
Oleyu: Era 3 only, a river border city.
Its monarch, the Storm King, must be gold-rank (and, per, royal heirs raised on cores are disqualified); the successor is chosen by the previous king after a contest.
Its royal guard is supplied by the Sapphire Crown guild, whose members are examined quarterly, and more often in the guard.
Sea of Storms: the Caribbean analogue (with Jason's map at L45).
The three public islands are Livaros, Arnote and Provo, in an east-west line.
Livaros: "the primary destination for adventurers... the adventurer island", with the Adventure Society campus and most services for essence users, and the skyport.
Havi Estos owns property there and hires people to poke at Jason's aura.

Arnote: the westernmost island, home to many wealthier citizens, with a relaxed lifestyle that is part of Rimaros's cultural identity and a minor branch of the royal family; it is the least populous and least defended.
Provo: the easternmost and most populous island, the general trade hub and home to most of the non-magical citizenry.
Jaitari: "the largest and most populous city" of the Storm Kingdom, on the largest island of the Sea of Storms.
Commander of the royal guard: Trenchant Moore, introduced as "Commander Trenchant Moore of the royal guard" and called "the siege sword".
House Irios: "the pre-eminent producer of defensive engineering" whose defences protect Rimaros and many fortress towns; the family is "known as the shield of" the kingdom.
The Magic Society holds the second-largest sky island in Rimaros, after the palace.

Soramir and Zila Rimaros, Liara and Baseph Rimaros, Dara and Zara Rimaros, Emiliano (the Storm King of Book 12, Zara's brother; adopted cousin), Trenchant Moore, Jacinda Irios, Havi Estos, Pelli (the mayor of Palisaros, in the post since before Argy's family began growing fruit), Hils Jaramaris.
Vitesse, in the kingdom of Estercost, is the City of Flowers, "located in what Jason Asano would know as the French Riviera".

Its skyline is made of the garden towers: huge towers with flowering vines spilling down the exterior, "most had every third or fourth floor dedicated to gardens using water, light and plant magic", which are residences for the wealthy elite and headquarters of key organisations.
Garden towers, most with every third or fourth floor given over to gardens.

The Adventure Society branch is in one of them, with a meeting room opening onto a balcony; the Adventure Society and Magic Society each hold an entire building, and the royal family keeps a tower as a palace.
Remore Academy and the Burning Violet guild house stand opposite each other; the guild house moved there after Roland Remore took over the guild long ago.
A tower belonging to the Geller family stands in Vitesse: on a high balcony of one of the famous flowering towers Sophie leans into Humphrey.
(Rakesh is also called the home of a continental council; the two may be councils for two continents, see Minor_Places/Rakesh.md and Open_Questions 22.)

The books disagree on where the Adventure Society's continental council sits: Book 6 says "the continental council for the Adventure Society sat in Vitesse, rather than the capital city, Cyrion", while Book 7 calls Cyrion "home to the Adventure Society's continental council".
Remore family influence is pervasive: Roland Remore, a diamond-ranker who took over Burning Violet long ago, is the Academy's arch-chancellor and Rufus's grandfather.

Farrah says the area has a higher density of magic than Greenstone's region, so monsters are stronger on average, and Gary says there "you get more silver rank monsters than anything. You see as many golds as you do bronze, and sometimes even diamond rank monsters".
Compare Clive's rating of Greenstone as about mid-iron.
A surge precursor that shows as more silver-rank monsters in Greenstone shows as more gold-rank monsters in Vitesse.

Consequences: even bronze-rankers go out with a silver escort, no adventurer below silver operates unsupervised, monster manifestations are powerful and frequent across the whole region, the Adventure Society detects them with a grid like Earth's and magical vehicles work for everyone on ambient magic.

Roland Remore (diamond archchancellor; Rufus's grandfather), Arabelle and Gabriel Remore (Rufus's parents), Neiman Bassingthwaite (the guild's chief membership officer), the receptionist Monica, plus the Gellers and the many students of Remore Academy.
Yaresh is a rainforest city with "only a few tens of thousands" of people, spread over "the footprint of a much larger centre" because its design deeply accommodates the natural environment.
Its walls are "a line of massive trees with walls of glossy black stone filling the gaps", with tunnels through the trunks.
Black land skimmers queue at the gates for inspection.
Outside the central area most buildings have living magic trees as a core, shaped and supplemented with brickwork; the heart of the city has polished metal and glass towers.
Towers stand at the heart of the city; the battle at the centre was "a dozen kilometres away" from the outskirts and the titanic figures could be seen looming over the towers.
Beneath the city: the natural array, the underground realm of Cardinas, ruled from the Citadel of Pillars and, further below, an astral space occupied by the Builder cult.

The Aristocratic Faction, a bloc of wealthy aristocrats and merchant barons who own most of the land and provide most of the jobs, is the dominant political force in the region; see 05_Organisations/Guilds_and_Houses.md.

Hana Shavar is "the High Priestess of the Church of the Healer for the city of Yaresh"; she runs relief for refugees, and after the messenger attack much of Yaresh's population is homeless and housed at Jason's cloud palace.

The array imbues elemental magic and makes messengers mutate with devolving intelligence; its changes "cause intelligence to rapidly and precipitously devolve" and cost the messengers most of their initial silver-rank force.

Book 9: messengers besiege Yaresh; a naga genesis egg (an apocalypse beast) is triggered when Argrave Mericulato, an Adventure Society functionary whose aura mask hides his seething anger, tosses an egg-like sphere at a guard (confirmed); the Battle of Yaresh ends the siege with the help of Jason's allies; Marek explains the natural array.
Rufus is with Jason's group in Book 9: "Mostly doesn't," Rufus qualified.

The dumpling-soup model: in Clive's analogy ("Dumpling Soup") worlds are dumplings and the astral is the soup, "the source of all magic"; astral spaces form attached to worlds and break down without them.
Spirit coin farms: Greenstone "was founded because it was such a perfect place for low-end spirit coin farms".
Constructs and ambushes in the Book 1 desert space, trial hazards in the Reaper's ground, and golems and Builder agents in the Book 3 vessel.
Expeditions bring healers, tracking stones for every member and a camp outside the aperture.

An astral king rules a miniature universe forged from the king's own soul: "the astral throne" and "astral gate" are "the tools of astral kings, who forged their very souls into physical universes, creating domains where their power was unassailable and all-but-unlimited".
The messengers' view is that "you're an astral king because you have an astral kingdom... because you possess an astral throne and an astral gate".
Marek notes Jason lacked "the third part of the astral throne, astral gate and soul forge trifecta".
Astral kings can bestow powers through a bond, and a messenger voice "needed to be sworn to an astral king, lest he wither and die".
Jason is an astral king from Book 8 or Book 9.

Interstice is a "city world" on a single flat plane with no sun or stars, "both the oldest and largest metropolis in existence", with "administrators in Interstice, but no rulers" and the physical reality the great astral beings use for their business.
One city-region is the island Glim, made almost entirely of rainbow-stained ice that does not chill or melt.
Book 12 describes it from Jota Withers's view.
Jason's Spirit Vault and Astral Kingdom (spoiler level 2): Jason's personal space grows over the series: a dimensional inventory that only he can physically enter (: "others cannot be invited or...
A sloth demon is a gold-rank monster with a soporific power that cripples speed; the space's overall density is not stated in the passages I checked.
Shade administers five trials in order, with a hidden sixth at the end:
The first trial: a choice between wisdom and courage that "cannot be failed"; it decides which of the two virtues is tested at the third trial.
Choosing wisdom gives a Medallion of Escape (silver-rank, uncommon; projects the aura to evacuate, works only in the city) and a Lesser Miracle Potion.
The second trial, capability: the City of Fallen Echoes itself, the longest of the five; the objective is to reach the centre (completed). Reward: a random magic item.

The third trial: those who chose courage first now face the test of wisdom; those who chose wisdom face courage, each alone behind a chosen door, where each meets a nightmare hag (diamond-rank astral entities that cannot harm directly; Jason faces an evil future self, Humphrey his family, notes).
The fourth trial, intellect: a time-limited test of calm under pressure; failure means death.
The fifth trial, resolve: the invigilator asks Jason to execute the Order's captive enemies; he refuses ("Not a chance") and the reward is an Immortal Crest. Reward: a random magic item.
The hidden trial, insight: the "ability to see beyond appearances"; reward unknown at the outset.
Participants may withdraw before each later trial through a gate.
Entered through a submerged aperture; Danielle Geller surfaces in "a turquoise lagoon, under a clear cerulean sky", mostly bounded by rocky rises with scrubby trees.
On the third island the party finds "a five-sided column, about as tall as a person and covered in magical engravings"; several are later packed away.
Boko is where the Adventure Society returns the freed Ustei slaves and women and children who wanted out of the tribe.

A construct army of "wooden puppets, awkward but numerous", stone golems two or three times human size, clockwork creatures such as a giant steel-cog tiger, and a huge steel spider carrying a robed figure, led by sandy-robed bronze and silver masters and silver-rank abominations (metal grafted into flesh, extra metal arms), attacks the expedition.

Jason's personal space grows over the series: a dimensional inventory that only he can physically enter (: "others cannot be invited or forcibly intrude") becomes the Spirit Vault, which those who trust him completely can enter, then a spirit domain, a soul realm that travels along the world link, and finally an astral kingdom once he possesses an astral throne and gate. Places inside it are described below.

Inventory (: only Jason may enter); the Spirit Vault, the enhanced inventory, which only people who implicitly trust him can enter and which he may seal against anyone; Erika, Emi, Ken and Hiro could enter, as later did Farrah, Asya and Ian; the gate to his storage space admits "those you allow"; a spirit domain; the vault as the extradimensional realm within his soul; an astral kingdom once the Astral Throne and Gate appear; consolidation of the Cardinas zone with the Soul Forge and the forest city Arbour (on the soul forge; Arbour introduces itself).
Seen first as a floating obsidian gazebo of black-and-white marbled obsidian, circular with four archways and open sides, floating in a rain-filled void.

The same passage describes a blood section of red flowers and blood-red flagstone like walking through an artery, a sin section of black, red, white and gold beds, a dark section in an underground cave with luminescent fungus and silver grass, and a doom section of trees and bushes, with a creek that runs through all of them to a waterfall and an underground fairy grotto.

In Book 8 Clive tours the same garden estate, where the essence sections intermingle, a subterranean network of fungus-lit tunnels runs under it, the sin garden is a manicured plot of black and white flowers and the doom areas are wild jungle.
Slovakia (Nitra): the territory renamed the Arrival Pagoda, whose portals connect to places in the astral space and which any non-hostile may use by default.

The arrival building is rebuilt as an octagonal pagoda; the portal area holds ten portal arches in dark crystal; the central city, about eighteen kilometres across, has a semi-industrial, steampunk feel, with a ring of about a hundred and sixty kilometres around it and roamable land about seven hundred kilometres in each direction.
After the Astral Throne and Astral Gate appear, Jason is an astral king.
The kingdom is an island "roughly thirty kilometres by fifteen, with widely differing elevations", with "a small mountain, sandy beaches and what looked to be an area sunk below sea level".

The island has a lagoon at the opposite end from the mountain with a small town along the shore, a larger city in the middle (without population) and a pagoda ten storeys tall instead of the usual five.
The flesh pit is where a sanguine horror was summoned and killed and the stone for Colin was looted, and it is now Colin's. Mana flows in creeks.

Arbour: an avatar introduces itself as "Arbour" in Book 11; the notes describe it as a tree city in Jason's astral kingdom with redwood tree mansions and light rail, with its own soul and avatar, formerly the corrupted World Tree or birthing tree; in Book 13 Jason and Emi stand on a platform in a tree mansion spanning several towering redwoods in Arbour.

New Water: the oasis city in his astral kingdom, named so that it would not be named after Boko; the Duke of Boko is holding a management meeting in its administrative centre when Jason fetches him, and addresses him as "Lord Asano".

Rexion: a city for Cardinas's brightheart survivors, led by Lorenn (confirmed as their leader); Book 12 describes a border town dug into the walls of the shaft, managed by the brighthearts with a mostly transient population, where Jason forbids anyone to make Rexion a temple. The array-powered citadel is unchecked.
A transformation zone is a sealed dome or sphere in which a place is rewritten; the Kostroma sphere extends underground and completely encapsulates the city.
She adds that "in the best case it will establish a second source of magic that will start feeding into this world".
The seal: "forty-three hours after the sphere moved into place, it vanished" at Kostroma, the first zone.
Sealing: inside a zone Jason's essence abilities are sealed while his racial powers remain; a normal transformation stays sealed about two days; the first zone message is.

Territories: each at least about a hundred kilometres across in the Cardinas zone ("a hundred kilometres across at a minimum"; the estimate puts the whole zone "somewhere between a continent and a planet" in size); claiming one requires clearing anomalies and the final boss.
Defenders have 117 minutes after a challenge, and claiming several territories causes anger and paranoia.
The zone's length is "months" (the territory is under two weeks old at; Nik is six months old at); the Tree territory is "roughly eight kilometres across" and "close to perfectly round".
Book 4 (about eighteen months after Jason left): Earth has so little magic that Jason relies on spirit coins to keep his recovery normal.
The Network has by now moved from hiding to scaling up in public view (a Book 4 explanation from Craig Vermillion,: the rising rate of threats forced it to expand beyond a hidden organisation).
A proto-astral space lasts "forty-three hours, as a baseline. Slightly longer with a more powerful ADE, but fifty-one is the record".

Book 11: Europe is mostly held by vampires, the Cabal holds some of the UK and Scandinavia and the Network has set up in Greenland, and Cabal-backed groups have openly joined or ousted governments in Scandinavia, parts of Russia and Africa, Sulawesi and Papua.

The Network (known to the public as the Global Defense Network from the early weeks of the monster waves): a coalition of local organisations using essences, founded about five centuries ago by a gold-rank outworlder, "the Founder", who struck a deal with a Pallimustus god and returned.

The founder's familiar Noreth was born on Pallimustus, loved the Earth and worked against Knowledge's plans; Boris worked with the familiar to betray the founder to the early magic societies that became the Network.

The Engineers of Ascension (EOA): a group described in Book 4 as taking over Perth "maybe two years ago", Melbourne "a year after that", and now turning to Sydney; its League of Heroes appears at Broken Hill.

Governments: multinational coalitions fund the artefact site; the Australian government seizes Asano Village in Book 12 (Gordon Truffett, the first to hold the artefact site's director post, is the Australian Prime Minister by Book 12) and in Book 13 declares it, like the standing stones, a special-interest territory under a multinational organisation.
Dimensional Artefact Site One (Australia) (spoiler level 3): Dimensional Artefact Site One, called the artefact city, is "a small city" in outback Australia, with "nine thousand or so workers"...
Casselton and Asano Village (spoiler level 1): Casselton Beach is Jason's hometown, a tourist beach town on the Mid-North Coast of New South Wales where he was born.

Dimensional Artefact Site One, called the artefact city, is "a small city" in outback Australia, with "nine thousand or so workers" before an evacuation, built around the standing stones where Jason and Farrah left Earth.

A ring of monitoring and research stations surrounds half a kilometre of open concrete with concentric metal panels, each a weapon bunker with "retractable weapons, magically enhanced howitzers and rocket batteries".
A coalition of nations "had spent the last fifteen years preparing it" as a defensive point.
Most of the workers are shop attendants, janitors, gardeners and others who keep the city operating; command runs from bunkers beneath the city.

Director of Operations: Lenora Coleman, Director of Operations for Dimensional Artefact Site One; she was a graduate stuck for two years in a monitoring station when the site was "little more than some pre-fab buildings", and is a bureaucrat and a core-user.
Deputy: Barry, "what amounted to mayor of the artefact city"; assistant Cassie; Security Commander Higgins.
Sub-Commander Keene leads a security team under Director Lenora Coleman.
The original director was Gordon Truffett, who chose the site's name and is now the Australian Prime Minister; he came to power "through fearmongering over magical gender transitions during rank-up".
Gold-rankers on the rotating roster are mostly American and Chinese, which is why Lenora does not have the command her title suggests.
A bomber attack leaves the standing stones unharmed.

The island is the one Jason and Farrah first reached years earlier, then uninhabited and ringed by the magical hurricane of the Sea of Storms, since bought and developed by the Sky Link Company; Jason names it as the Pallimustus anchor point, an uninhabited island in the Storm Kingdom and in Book 13 says the Church of Knowledge has annexed it; it is renamed Ascension's Gate.

Timing: Boris's reasoning in Book 13 says the Cosmic Throne detour gave fifteen extra years, the bridge is now set in place, and "within a decade at most, the bridge would become a true dimensional passage, no longer requiring sophisticated astral magic to cross".

Whether the island renamed Ascension's Gate is the island where Jason and Farrah first arrived and that the Sky Link Company later developed: describes that island (an uninhabited island in a magical hurricane, later a town with storm accumulators) and a chamber of standing stones beneath it; and describe the island with standing stones as the counterpart anchor point.
Casselton Beach is Jason's hometown, a tourist beach town on the Mid-North Coast of New South Wales where he was born.
Asano Village: eco-village buildings on clifftop land, a medical centre, a pub and spa, and a secret tunnel system.
The long passage ends at Jason's cloud house, which sits at the bottom of the sea about two kilometres out, reached by a hidden tram.
Earth has very little magic in Book 4: Jason uses spirit coins to normalise his recovery.
Book 4: Jason wakes in the hospital; contacts uncle Hiro through the Stone Wall bar in Sydney's Kings Cross; reveals magic to his niece Emi, then to the family.

Book 13 (2038): after negotiation the Australian government declares Asano Village and the surrounding area a special-interest territory, "similar to the standing stones", to be managed by a multinational organisation with Lenora Coleman in charge; Jason says his family built it with their own money and toil, and Prime Minister Truffett is named as the one who suggested the seizure.
Spaces are rated by category and last "forty-three hours, as a baseline".
Dorrigo National Park: the team meets silver-rank jungle trolls (confirms roaming jungle trolls, whose regeneration is shut down by fire; Nigel's team burns the bodies with bronze-rank everburn oil).
South Australia: Jason and Farrah are flown from Sydney to join the Adelaide branch's tactical team.

Inside, flat scrubland holds a herd of grotesque animals: "three gigantoads, two yowies, and a yara-ma-yha-who", with barb-tailed mantas overhead; the team's projection is that the space "might last as much as sixty hours".
Setting: Makassar, South Sulawesi, a city of one and a half million people.
Dino-men: silver-rank intelligent lizard-men lead dinosaur monsters; their king says "I, like you all, am less than two days old".
Outcome: Jason enters, dies, and takes the form of a star phoenix.

The Makassar death toll "officially crossed a hundred and fifty thousand" with bodies in piles, early estimates being one to two hundred thousand, and a necromancer later animates Makassar's victims as a zombie horde (Mr North says it looks like an extension of long-discarded experiments from his own organisation's past; Jason says the necromancer who animated them got his start in North's house, and names Todd "The Necromancer" Halverson).

A New South Wales outback town whose population had grown from fewer than twenty thousand to almost thirty-five thousand as isolated outback residents were gathered there; under Network protection with a support team and a nine-person tactical section.
Jason estimates "somewhere between ten and fifteen thousand people had died" from the bodies and his portal count, putting survivors at fewer than twenty thousand.

Sydney's Kings Cross (the Stone Wall bar), the Network's Sydney clinic where Jason secretly works as the "Starlight Angel", and the Starlight Rider episodes belong to Book 4: the media dub the figure the Starlight Rider after earlier stories of a starlight angel. They are not full place files.
Nitra, in western Slovakia, is a city that became "a major centre for the Network after the organization had been pushed out of Bratislava by vampires".
A glimmering dome several kilometres across, "a giant rainbow under glass".

Jason claims territories (Arrival Pagoda, Soul Haven, Tranquil Shadow Woods, Steamforge Circuit and others; the renamings are at;), stabilises the zone into a permanent astral space, and earns the title Reality Hegemon.
Its steam engines are driven by a mix of fire and water quintessence, not coal, in a blend of Victorian and modern technology with magic that does not respect real physics.

Discovered in 1948 when local Network operatives found "an incursion space dimensionally coterminous with an area near Saint-Étienne" with multiple apertures, as Paul Abreo of the Lyon branch Steering Committee explains.
Adrien Barbou is the Lyon Operations Director, working out of the black site; Paul Abreo confesses that many of the decisions behind it were "at least in part, mine".
Barbou holes up in the fortress having sealed the apertures from the inside, and ritual specialists try to breach the seals.

sec: 3. The transformation zone and cloud city
claim: In Book 6 Shako and Chen place a device in the aperture of the astral space, which triggers a second transformation zone (Gerling and Mr North fight beside the vampires and Jason in the zone); a nightmare hag, "a diamond-rank entity that had little direct power but could manifest people's fears", is among the foes.

sec: 3. The transformation zone and cloud city
claim: Jason claims it and stabilises it into his Saint-Étienne spirit domain; the allies he gathers there are the vampires, including Elizabeth, Mr North and Gerling, with the necromancer Todd "The Necromancer" Halverson a silver-ranker with heavy core taint.

sec: 3. The transformation zone and cloud city
claim: Fates: Noreth, the EOA leader known as Mr North, is dead before Book 7; Gerling is killed more than once but keeps returning and in Book 11 is Elizabeth's blood slave.

sec: 3. The transformation zone and cloud city
claim: By Book 12 it is a cloud city whose administration tower is "a looming edifice of renaissance architecture, the most overt divergence from the original design of the city"; the clan's city has expanded green areas and waterways with streams running through.
Vampires, ghouls and blood servants (mad after Jason's Book 12 purge: a giant eye in the sky), hostile Network factions.
Arcazitlan is a fortress town dug into the wall of a rocky gorge in jungle country, where Jason arrives alone at the start of the surge and fights bone feasters.
Setting: a fortified town "dug high into the wall of a rocky gorge", reached by adventurers because airships would be crushed against the wall by the gorge's gusts.
Interior: stone chambers and claustrophobic corridors, favouring defence over comfort; civilians sheltering from the surge are packed in.
Defences: magical sensors throughout the gorge and wind-blade runes; a military command post watches the fight below.
Roads: a well-maintained network runs through the surrounding jungles and hills.
A militia commander runs the fort. Adventurers make deliveries.

Book 7: Jason lands nearby after dropping from the sky, reaches the fort during a night attack by bone feasters (emaciated, eyeless humanoid monsters with large mouths) and helps defend it; he leaves by road with Shade as a land skimmer.
Surge monsters in the gorge and jungle; the fort's inaccessibility is both defence and difficulty.
Boko is an old desert city of academics and artists to the north of Greenstone, with a native population, a Duke, an Adventure Society branch and a Magic Society presence.
Setting: "A city to the north of here. A lot older than Greenstone, with a population native to the area".
Hester's portal range limits mean Boko is about an hour's recovery from Greenstone by portal.
Look: desert stone like Old City, with drier air.
Coast: Boko was a coastal city but never a port like Greenstone, with no natural harbour.
Gardens and universities: beautiful architecture and gardens; a warehouse district far from the gardens and universities.
Temples: floating temples shielded by their gods survived the destruction.
The scholars: "Scholars of the arts. Painting, poetry, sculpture, dance"; people travel from across the continent to visit its theatres.
People: almost entirely human and very dark-skinned, with local fashion loose and breathable, calmer than the Ustei's.
Rule: a Duke of Boko, a silver-ranker through cores, as is normal for political leaders; noble houses exist.
Adventurers: the Adventure Society has a branch, but Boko "was not a strong adventuring city".
Trouble: a movement against intellectuals among low-rankers began in Boko proper before it spread out; officials suspect more sinister backing and a power base shift to Greenstone and Boko.
It has a mirage chamber that Danielle helped rebuild.
Book 1: the Adventure Society returns the Ustei captives to Boko, where Jason arrives through Hester's portal; he, Gary and Rufus explore it.
Book 12: Li Li Mei lives in Boko and is being hunted.
After the assassination the city is evacuated, the blast containment zone gives out and the city is gone; most of its ninety thousand people are evacuated. They shelter in Jason's astral kingdom.
The crater becomes a harbour, and Jason names the astral city New Water, not Boko.
The Duke of Boko; Li Li Mei.
Theatres, painting, poetry and dance draw visitors; local dress is loose and breathable.

Cartise was a river city and the major hub of trade and travel in its area, destroyed just before the great surge when the Builder cult claimed a nearby astral space and a diamond-rank monster then overwhelmed the city.
Before: "the river city of Cartise", the major hub for trade and travel in the area.
It had many adventurers who now protect the fortress towns.

The fall: the Builder cult claimed a nearby astral space, which separated from the world with widespread destruction; a diamond-rank monster manifested shortly after and overwhelmed the city; most people were evacuated to towns along the river.
After: the ruins look like London after the Blitz, with blocks reduced to fist-sized rubble.
Refugees overpopulate the surrounding towns and the loss strains logistics.
Clearing the ruins: Jason's team sweeps a route guided by an Adventure Society functionary named Vestine, as one of several teams.
It is where Sophie's Book 8 delivery contract leads, and where a gang is hired to ambush her on behalf of Purity loyalists.
Position: the border city of Girlano, which lies inland and south of the Storm Kingdom.
The region is the part of Girlano that comes closest to the coast, near enough that a tall hill gives a view of the Sea of Storms.
Border station: Storm Kingdom border guards run a station at the city gates.
Streets: generously spaced, with rooftops used by Jason and Sophie for a private talk.
Gangs and cartels: the surrounding country is run by cartels producing heavily controlled or banned substances from rare plants and minerals.
The eight men who ambush Sophie are members of a small gang from the nearby city, one of many satellite groups to the local cartel, mostly strongmen who keep low-end officials in line.
Hired muscle: they are silver-rank in their forties, "raw garbage" with no training and reeking of cores, hired by Purity loyalists to bring Sophie in.

Adventure Society presence: the Society ignores borders and keeps monsters out of population centres; its neutrality is why Sophie heads this way, and Liara says "we have a large force in Casallini because it's a border city".
Smuggler's paths: semi-hidden paths through jungle-covered hills avoid border checkpoints, which have no patrols during the surge.
Character: "a lawless town full of crappy guys" in Sophie's words.
Book 8: the gang is hired and the ambush fails.
Jason and Liara judge the tip to be a trap, a "worm on a hook" from the Order of Redeeming Light, and Liara cancels Sophie's contract and sends Storm Kingdom civic forces to sweep the gang up.
Sophie, meanwhile, scouts the city on her own and hands her prisoners to the border guards.
The Dragon Lands are the Pallimustus version of Antarctica: an island continent that is not icy but volcanic, the native land of the draconians.
Setting: an island continent named for its "dragon mouth" flame geysers.
Land: dark stone mountains rise from green lowlands of forest and vast farmland laid out like a map, with a climate Jason compares to Scotland or Ireland.
Geology: subterranean apertures lead to a realm of fire, giving active volcanoes, steaming hot springs and the geysers.
Peoples: draconians; they are called isolationist and are not welcoming to strangers, and trade through proxies outside their lands.
Trade: agricultural products are the second-largest trade through Greenstone's port, after low-rank spirit coins.
Most nations tariff the goods heavily over political issues, which makes them a luxury food.

The magic leaking from the astral spaces has earth affinity as well as fire; it draws ash from the sky into the ground and makes the farmland famously rich, the best place for gold-rank cooking ingredients.
Book 12: the team's sky ship approaches the coast and later leaves the Dragon Lands' airspace quickly after a conversation with Anna Tilden.
Girlano is a landlocked inland nation south of the Storm Kingdom, ostensibly a kingdom but controlled by cartels that produce heavily controlled or banned substances, with a puppet government.
Position: inland, to the south of the Storm Kingdom, whose coast it comes close to; from a tall hill the Sea of Storms can be seen.
Border city: Casallini.
Border country: jungle-covered hills with many semi-hidden smuggling paths between the border and the shore.

Cartels: the illicit leadership keeps its position through under-the-table deals with powerful groups in neighbouring countries, which prop up the puppet government while their own governments pay lip service to suppression.
Trade: the rare plants and minerals of the region are what the cartels exploit, and strong public sanctions and border controls surround the nation.
Adventure Society: it ignores borders and politics and keeps monsters out of population centres, so long as its work is not interfered with.
Reputation: Liara calls it "a stain full of drug dealers and smugglers"; Belinda finds it "famously sketchy" and tempting.
Book 8: Sophie heads toward Girlano and Casallini on a specialised delivery.
Book 9: the team turns east at the coast, not south toward Girlano.
Hornis is a port city on the coast south and around from Greenstone, reached overland through the delta, the veldt and then south.
Location: "a port city, like Greenstone, south and around the coast"; the overland route runs east into the veldt and then south.
Port: smuggled goods can come in "through the port in Hornis or the one here in Greenstone".
Adventure Society: Hornis has a branch that mounts large searches.
Magic Society: Hornis has its own Magic Society people and a mirage chamber that Danielle helped rebuild and maintains.
Underworld: the Big Three's influence is a factor in Greenstone; Sophie plans to buy her way past it in Hornis.
Book 1: Sophie plans to flee through the delta and the veldt to Hornis with the spirit coin vault's money.
Book 2: smuggled materials are traced to shipments into Hornis before being moved to private vessels; Jonah's team is found in Hornis on a boat bound for distant shores.
Book 3: Lucian Lamprey hopes to escape to Hornis through a contact.
Book 9: the team's route home runs south, across the Great Southern Continent, then north to Hornis on the way to Greenstone, Vitesse and Cyrion.
Book 12: a Greenstone resident says Hornis is the furthest south he has been.
Isart is named once: a city on Jason's procession south where Emir asks to meet him to discuss a job and bring the person who made the cloud flasks.

Emir says there is "a city called Isart that you should arrive at on your procession south", will meet Jason there when the detour is done, will arrive in about two weeks and bring the maker of the cloud flasks.
Jayapura is a port on the northern coast of Pranay, the large southern land equivalent to Sri Lanka, and the birthplace of Hester.
Jason's team stays several days after the Reaper trial to awaken abilities, summon familiars and get tattoos.
Setting: one of the important sea-trade ports on Pranay's northern coast, in a world with no Arabian Peninsula.
Arrival: Hester opens a portal into the city; Jason and Sophie, with astral affinities, are unaffected by the transition.
Mirage chamber complex: larger and more sophisticated than the Geller chamber in Greenstone, with concurrent chambers, because the magic is denser.
Mystic Quarter and markets: floating discs for sale in the Mystic Quarter; markets the team visits.
Mirage Chamber Association: owns the complex, has close ties to the Magic Society, Adventure Society and local government and holds significant power.
Entertainment: essence users fight one another or illusions for a paying audience.
Higher than Greenstone; it allows advanced dimensional effects.
Those who can afford them ride platter-sized floating discs; the team finds new customs and food; Jason remembers kulfi-like ice cream there.
A nondescript tattoo parlour run by Tilly is where Jason gets his crest.
Book 3: the team's mirage-arena memories inform their confidence.
Kazlahk is a wealthy coastal city on the eastern border of Estercost, surrounded by desert and used for spirit coin farms, with a famously scalding climate.
Setting: "a city of sandstone, palm trees and money", on Estercost's eastern border, surrounded by desert.
Coast: gorgeous beaches lined with the massive houses of coin barons and major adventuring families; a luxury resort for merchants, adventurers and nobility.
Wealth: its spirit coins and sea trade; as with Greenstone, the empty desert is a premium site for spirit coin farms, but the higher magic makes for more valuable denominations.

Kazlahk University of Medicine: the most notable beach institution; healing studies focus on essence and ritual magic over alchemy because the Magic Society and Adventure Society fund them, with some money from the Healer's church.
Its School of Alchemical Efficiency appears in a disclaimer.
Book 11: the group considers a detour to Kazlahk on the way to Estercost.
Kurdansk is a river city in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil and Sophie Wexler's birthplace.
It has a busy skyport, an entertainment quarter in a former warehouse district, many dark-skinned, silver-haired celestines and prisons that hold criminals for years.
Nation: the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil.
Humphrey remarks that the more a nation calls itself free and righteous, the more tyrannical it is.
Entertainment quarter: a former warehouse district by the Kurdan River docks, now the most viable site for large theatre halls, "a heady mix of pleasure, criminality and money".
Skyport: busy, with towers where airships dock; Emir's cloud ship recovers its full function there.
Houses: narrow row houses wedged together.
Peoples: celestines with dark skin and silver hair are common.
Law: the city locks criminals up for years, and a Book 12 speaker asks about the operating costs of such places.

Book 6: Emir tells Sophie she was born in Kurdansk; the team searches the city, and Marta Fries, a silver-rank celestine and friend of Melody Jain, escapes through a hidden panel Melody once used to fake her death, about two decades earlier.
Book 9: Melody Jain's story begins in Kurdansk about twenty-five years before; she and Sophie's father were both secret members of organisations, the Order of the Reaper among them.
Leust is one of the largest and richest towns in the delta, with paved roads and stone buildings instead of mud brick.
Town: mostly yellow desert stone, with some green stone buildings; the water affinity of green stone keeps interiors cool, and Jason stays at a large green stone inn.

Lumber region: on the south side of the river in the eastern delta, the furthest part from the city; more solid ground than marsh, laid out like a forestry reserve with trees in neat rows, saplings and cleared fields. Wagons carry lumber to Leust.
Industry: lumber; the land rights are heavily regulated, and the lumber region is one of the few places in the delta where lumber-worthy trees grow.
Mill owners: Kyle Lindover, a leonid larger than Gary, owns the Lindover Lumber Mill and shut it after repeated fergax sightings; his family stays with her parents in Greenstone.

Book 1: Jason takes an unusual contract to hunt a fergax that is never found, stays in Leust, finds the Clementson property and the adventurer Dean Tuckell summoning monsters, and learns that Thadwick Mercer set it up.
Mill and house: a still, empty lumber mill, past which Jason finds a "sizeable farmhouse".
The mill is reached through a wooden archway bearing its name on a road through neat rows of trees.
Owner: Kyle Lindover is a leonid larger than Gary, "the most lumberjack-looking man Jason had ever seen".
He shut the mill after repeated fergax sightings so no worker would be hurt; his wife and children are staying with her parents in Greenstone.
Stakes: his reserves are falling short, most workers have taken jobs elsewhere, and he fears a black mark on his record.
Tracks: bear tracks are almost identical to a fergax's, so other adventurers dismissed his reports.
Layout: laid out like the Lindover property but in full operation, with magical saws audible from the mill and a farmhouse "both larger and more ostentatious".
Owner: Eustace Clementson, who sweats and tries to divert Jason, then falls in behind him under his aura.
Guest house: a stone-and-wood building apart from the main residence, where the iron-rank adventurer Dean Tuckell lays low between visits.
Book 1: Jason takes the contract at the Adventure Society, stays at an inn in Leust, and tracks the monster's aura from Lindover's land to Clementson's property.
Dean says Thadwick Mercer set up the "land-grab deal": every couple of weeks Dean spooked Lindover with his summon and then hid in Clementson's guest house.
In the settlement Jason negotiates with Thalia Mercer, the Mercer family compensates Lindover for the months of stalled production and Clementson's takeover preparations are rolled back.
How Clementson was recruited, and what the Mercer family planned to gain from the land beyond "you'd probably end up with the land, anyway".
Oleyu is an unremarkable border city on a river, "pleasant, prosperous, and moderately sized", built on river trade with a mid-range level of magic.
Position: Clive's route follows a river to "the border city of Oleyu", where the Rakesh Magic Society branch's area of influence ends.
Standing: not as big or important as Rakesh or Vitesse, or unusual like Greenstone.
Magic Society building: Clive lodges a protest here over his treatment by the Rakesh branch, without optimism.
Palisaros is a small laid-back town on the island of Arnote in the Storm Kingdom, arranged along a lagoon and the clifftop above it, where Jason settles his cloud house.
Island: Arnote, the quiet residential island of Rimaros's three public islands.
Lagoon and cliff: the town lies along the lagoon shore and the clifftop bordering it, with a waterfall and a river spilling over the cliff.
Houses: colourful, two or three storeys, with open space, covered walkways, balconies and awnings, and hidden magical amenities.
Jason's house: his cloud house stands on a clifftop near the river, with an invisible barrier along the cliff edge.
Residents: mostly normals, irons and bronzes using cores, with a few silver and gold auras, and many caramel-skinned celestines.
Pace: small-town, with none of the residents in a rush, calmer than busy Livaros.
Mayor: Pelli, a member of the royal family but separate from them, living a relatively humble life as a core user.
Guide: Argy shows visitors the saloon, eateries and market.
Book 7: Jason meets Argy and Pelli in the town and settles there; during the surge only Jason and Pelli remain to defend it, and Jason leaves shortly after his team.
Book 8: Vidal rides into the lagoon to find Wexler's team staying in a house by the waterfall.
