Rakesh is a populous, caste-divided city on the north coast of the Africa-like continent, home of the Adventure Society's continental council and of the continent's largest Magic Society and Adventure Society strongholds.
Setting: on the north coast; a desert gulch with a hidden Builder-cult portal lies a few dozen kilometres south.
Buildings: desert stone, plastered and painted in large, coordinated murals, each district's dominant colour grading into the next.
Campus: one sprawling campus joins the largest Magic Society and Adventure Society strongholds on the continent.
Link to Vitesse: Danielle teleports Humphrey and Sophie across the Gramid Passage from Vitesse to Rakesh.
Caste system: society is divided into castes, and the caste system justifies holding someone seen as lowly against their will; it dismisses Belinda as unimportant.
Culture: busy but quiet streets, a local culture that values calm decorum, most people on foot or in animal-drawn carriages.
The Magic Society branch: one of the most powerful on the continent; officials there have power and connections, so consequences come from the Adventure Society, not other branches.
The campus prevents portals outside designated zones.
The Adventure Society: the continental council sits here.

Vitesse is also described as the seat of a continental council; the text reads most simply as one council per continent, with Rakesh serving the Africa-like continent and Vitesse the continent of Estercost, but it never states this.
Enough to support floating platforms, a common sight, unlike low-magic Greenstone.

Book 6: Clive is recruited from Greenstone by Lorelei Grantham, Vice-Dean of the astral magic research department, and finds himself a prisoner of the campus; he and Belinda spend about two months planning an escape through the Builder cult's portal network.
He later lodges a protest in Oleyu about his treatment by the Rakesh branch.
The Rakesh Magic Society wants the cult's astral magic, not the fight against it.
Lorelei Grantham (Vice-Dean), Lady Ajus (an official interested in Clive's research); Carlivexistrix, whom Danielle will not keep waiting.
Floating platforms for essence users, from standing discs to floating palanquins; calm public manners.
Sadi Andali is "a little dirtball country", famously almost lawless, where slave markets sell unusual and restricted goods and the Adventure Society keeps no branch.
A captive guesses "Eastern desert?" and a fellow prisoner answers "Obviously", so the country is in or near an eastern desert. Cells there are mud brick, reinforced.
Law: "famous for being almost lawless"; the Adventure Society has no branch and only sends people in to sweep for illegal research and restricted essences, finding plenty of both.
Slave trade: unusual products move through its slave markets; Ben asks whether destroying the Sadi Andali slave trade is Jason's price.
Reach: events "all across Sadi Andali" are set against the great and noble houses of Cyrion.
Book 12: Garret and Patterson wake in suppression collars in Sadi Andali; Garret's experience there may have knocked some sense into him, according to Percival.
Patterson and Garret; Ben.
Zartos is a subterranean city built around an underground river, largely populated by celestines, and the home of the diamond-rank smith Virid, Gary's mentor.
A city built around an underground river.
Virid keeps a personal smithy in the city, "the best place to forge a great work".
Peoples: "Zartos has a large celestine community"; the city is "largely populated by celestines".
Not stated. A diamond-ranker lives and works there.
Book 1: Gary and Farrah mention Zartos on the road; Rufus has not been there, though his brother recommended it.
Book 7: after Jason's death the team waits in Zartos while Gary and Virid examine and reforge Dread Salvation, a collaboration that Jason's soul-bond guides; the sword returns as Hegemon's Will.
Virid Martine, diamond-rank weaponsmith and Gary's mentor.
Nothing further is established; the team's stay is described only as a reunion while the smiths work.

In the text it is separate from Eurasia (see the World Primer), is far more populous in the north than the south, and has its continental Adventure Society and Magic Society strongholds at Rakesh on the north coast.

sec: 2. The far south: Greenstone and its delta
claim: It was settled from Estercost a few centuries ago.

sec: 2. The far south: Greenstone and its delta
claim: Magic level: Clive rates Greenstone's density at about mid-iron, "which is very low".

sec: 2. The far south: Greenstone and its delta
claim: The cities of the south are low-magic and sparsely populated, while the north is far more populous (in the Greenstone file).

sec: 2. The far south: Greenstone and its delta
claim: The delta and the veldt: the overland route from Greenstone runs through the delta, east into the veldt and then south to Hornis.

sec: 2. The far south: Greenstone and its delta
claim: The lumber region: on the south side of the river in the eastern delta, farthest from the city, is Leust with the Lindover and Clementson lumber properties (see../Minor_Places/Leust.md and../Minor_Places/Lindover_and_Clementson_Properties.md).

sec: 3. Ports and cities of the south and coast
claim: Hornis is a port "south and around the coast" from Greenstone, Greenstone's nearest rival port, used for smuggling and escape routes.

sec: 3. Ports and cities of the south and coast
claim: Boko is an old desert city of academics and artists to the north of Greenstone, about an hour's recovery by portal from it for Hester. It was a coastal city but never a port. It is destroyed in Book 12.

sec: 3. Ports and cities of the south and coast
claim: The Ustei: a desert people whose fashion is less calm than Boko's.

sec: 4. The north: Rakesh and the border country
claim: Rakesh is a populous, caste-divided city on the north coast, with a desert gulch and a hidden Builder-cult portal a few dozen kilometres south.

sec: 4. The north: Rakesh and the border country
claim: The Gramid Passage links it with Vitesse.

sec: 4. The north: Rakesh and the border country
claim: Oleyu is a pleasant, prosperous border city of moderate size on river trade, where the Rakesh Magic Society branch's area of influence ends.

sec: 4. The north: Rakesh and the border country
claim: Zartos is a celestine-populated underground city around an underground river; its continent is not stated.

sec: 4. The north: Rakesh and the border country
claim: Sadi Andali is "a little dirtball country", almost lawless, in or near an eastern desert.

The continental council of the Adventure Society sits at Rakesh, while Cyrion and Vitesse are also described as seats of a council; the text reads most simply as one council per continent (see../Minor_Places/Rakesh.md).

The only mention is the team's route plan in Book 9: move south down the continent, cross to the Great Southern Continent, cross north again to Hornis, then on to Greenstone, Vitesse and Cyrion. Nothing describes it.
Estercost is the kingdom whose capital Cyrion is the largest city in the world and whose Vitesse sits on the equivalent of the French Riviera.
Crown: a queen in Book 12, her name not found.
Capital: Cyrion, ringed by concentric walls and farmland of "some of the most magical and valuable growing land on the planet".
It looks "like Tokyo by way of the Emerald City of Oz" from the air.
Vitesse: the City of Flowers on Estercost's southern coast, famous for garden towers with every third or fourth floor given to gardens.
Remore Academy and the Burning Violet guild house stand opposite each other.
Kazlahk: a wealthy coastal city on Estercost's eastern border, surrounded by desert and spirit coin farms, famous for scalding heat.
Remains of an old war: toppled Builder world-engineer golems lie beyond Cyrion's outer wall from before the messenger invasion.
Greenstone was settled from Estercost (see Africa_like_Continent.md).
Rakesh is reached from Vitesse across the Gramid Passage.
Kurdansk is in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil, Sophie's birthplace; the files do not say it is on this continent.
The books give no numeric density figure for Vitesse, but its monsters run to silver with frequent gold (see../Vitesse.md).
The Storm Kingdom is a nation of islands in the Sea of Storms, the Caribbean analogue, founded by Soramir Rimaros.
Its best-known city, Rimaros, spans three public islands; its largest and most populous city is Jaitari.
The three public islands of Rimaros run east to west: Livaros, Arnote and Provo.
Livaros: "the adventurer island", with the Adventure Society campus, the skyport and most services for essence users.
Arnote: the westernmost island, home to wealthier citizens and a minor branch of the royal family, the least populous and least defended.
Palisaros is a laid-back town on it, where Jason's cloud house stands.
Provo: the easternmost, most populous island, the trade hub with most of the non-magical citizens.

The central landmass: the largest concentration of the kingdom's people lives on a central landmass made up of what would be Cuba, Haiti and the Dominican Republic (see../Rimaros.md); the largest city there is Jaitari.
The coast and Girlano: the Storm Kingdom controls the coast, and inland Girlano lies to its south, close enough that the Sea of Storms is visible from a tall hill. Casallini is Girlano's border city.
Surges and forces: the Storm Kingdom provides border-station guards and civic forces beyond the Adventure Society.
Soramir Rimaros, the founder, is still alive and deferred to even by the king.
Dawn (spoiler level 2): Dawn is the World-Phoenix's First Servant, the head of its cult and its primary vessel (describes the post; the notes identify Dawn...
The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash (spoiler level 0): A familiar is a purely magical creature from the deep astral given a body by a summoning (Clive).
Operations Director of the Network's Lyon branch, working out of the black site; one of the secretive staff who knew of and worked in the dimensional fortress, and has been cultivating loyalists.
He leaves the dimensional space by another aperture just before it is sealed, alone, with no EOA and no prisoner.
In Book 5 he takes the seat of Mr East, speaking of "the previous Mr East" and of vetting his people.
Mr North says his own minions were disappointing before Barbou came along.
Anna says Barbou is not hers to give; Farrah says "Barbou belongs to me".
Gerling hits him and demands help reaching the Saint-Étienne dimensional space.
In the zone he is the only one not attacked by the soul attacks and Jason declines to take him.
In 2038 Farrah recalls him as the man behind her incarceration and tells Anna to retire the "bad apple" excuse.

Jason brought him out of the zone alive; Mr North asked for a quick death and Jason left the decision to Farrah, who describes disposing of bodies without denying what she did, so Anna concludes "Barbou isn't alive". In Book 6 Anna did not know his fate.
Calculating and self-protective; he stays at the edge of a fight and tries to look insignificant.
Farrah never says outright that she killed him; the scene implies it.
An elf with a library full of art, including a large desert painting.
Patient and measured: "Your mistake was your need to feel in control".
Protective father: "A father's wish for his child to go further than he".
Quietly threatening: "Don't forget who my daughter is".
Content with legitimacy: "Once a powerful crime lord, he found that legitimacy sat very well with him".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: His aura senses are less trained than Thalia Mercer's.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He keeps his word, chasing down materials Clive listed.
By Book 6 Humphrey says "Adris Dorgan's goal is legitimacy".
Last of the Big Three crime lords, later mayor of Old City.
Book 1: Jason meets him in his library.
Book 2: his daughter can now take tea in his courtyards openly; he warns "Don't forget who my daughter is" in a private conversation; he is chasing down the shipments on Clive's lists.
Book 12: Jason promises "Nothing will happen to your daughter from my people".
Elspeth Arella: daughter.
Jason: Jason tells him "Nothing will happen to your daughter from my people".
His daughter's parentage was kept secret for years.
Not described in detail in the lines read; she crouches on rooftops and wears a sword at her left hip.
Reserved and formal: after joining the Network team, "her reserve that Jason had cracked open went back in place".
Ritualist: she meditates on a mat with a stitched ritual circle, a monster core in her hands.
Horror at Jason's methods: she watches leeches drain a monster and melt into blood in Jason's hand.
Duty-minded: she tells her escort to inform her father of a change in plan.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Essences sword, adept and magic, a master confluence; she carries a genuine chokuto and has a blinking teleport that leaves exploding after-images.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver-rank speed and strength outstrip Dawn's, but Dawn's perfect positioning turns her hits into near misses.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She and Jason started sparring evenly matched; she was a specialised swordswoman caught up in human fighting styles.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: By Book 13 she wears a rare gold-rank sword Valdis forged using other-world techniques.
Her father is the silver-rank patriarch of the Asano clan, named Shiro like Ken and Hiro's older brother.
Her grandmother claims her for a hug and wonders what Jason wants from them.
Book 5: she watches Jason pass on a rooftop; Jason says her clan should have sent her home; spars with him; chases him across the slum rooftops; the Tiwari trip.
Book 13: wears the sword Valdis gave her; her husband Itsuki leaves her three weeks before she notices.
Jason: sparring partner and relative.
Dawn: spars with her.
Itsuki Tiwari: her husband, who tells her "your life doesn't have room for me anymore" and moves out to join the vampire war.
Valdis Volaire: sword training partner for the past decade.
Her father and grandmother: the clan's patriarch, and her grandmother.
Her years of sword training, after having her monster core residue removed, cost her marriage: "You love the sword".
Diamond-rank beauty that she turns aside with her aura; soft green eyes, light-brown skin "of a fawn's fur" and wavy wood-brown hair, "like a dryad of myth".
Playful but exact: she tries to put Jason at ease "with some playful teasing".
Learns to read power: she realises that pushing Jason as hard as Charist advocated "could have greater repercussions".
Unrepentant: she turns on the dead envoys without guilt.
Understanding of burden: she nods at Jason's account of power and responsibility.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Diamond rank, the most powerful at the meeting, in the front row.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She moves in a blur to stand before Jason.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She works with a silver priestess when they find an incongruity in the ruins.
Resident of Yaresh; "the more reclusive Lady Allayeth".
She raised Team Moon's Edge, the all-female team led by Miriam Vance.
Book 9: finds Schaat's corpse with Charist and sees a star phoenix.
Book 10: Allayeth and Charist discuss his approach inside a privacy screen; she explains Gormanston Bynes to Jason; in the siege she leads Moon's Edge among the gold-rankers.
Book 12: at a VIP gathering.
Charist: fellow diamond and rival; he looks like a child caught doing something stupid when they talk.
Jason: she learns to respect his concessions.
Team Moon's Edge: trained by her.
Trenchant asks whether anyone has worked with Amos Pensinata.
Dawn names him as a gold-ranker whose experiences with soul trauma left him with a more capable aura than most; she has convinced him to travel with Jason to teach soul manipulation.
Jason knows him by reputation as the man who defeated the same forces that had forced Jason to flee the underwater complex.
Jason later learns from him how to combine auras into a single force and about controlling aspects of the soul in isolation, which helped him expand perception without a beacon-like aura.
Clive turns on him at the Yaresh camp: "You were brought on to help Jason, not make things worse. But your baggage...".
He debriefs a Rimaros team in Cardinas and is among the few able to resist the zone's corruption.
In Book 11 he grows troubled, does not flee with the other gold-rankers but goes into the water orb, and Jason promises to try to get him back.
His nephew is Orin Pensinata (see Orin_Pensinata.md); he joins Jason's journey partly because Orin insisted on coming.
Jason extracts him from his attempted "suicide-by-messenger" and the gold-rankers escape into Jason's soul realm.
After the zone he takes Orin and the scout Rosa back to Rimaros.
What he tells Jason in the dinghy is not summarised here.
Wavy brown hair and fair skin, "pretty, but only by Earth standards" compared with the other world's beauties.
Steady and perceptive: her face is stricken as she catalogues the changes from the boy she remembered.
Protective: she stands ahead of her daughters at the Book 13 meeting.
Wary of Jason emotionally, not physically: she knows he is an emotional threat to her children.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Amy has seen essences before; Book 4 marks her first time holding one.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She is the village's "de facto mayor" and acts as mayor in the Book 5 evacuation.
The girl next door and Jason's best friend; she had a crush on Kaito from early on.
Her parents retired to Tasmania and sold her the house next door.
The notes add that she is mayor of the Casselton Regional Council.
Book 4: the family party; reunion; marina arrival; essence holding.
Book 5: village leader.
Book 13: floats up with Emi and her daughters.
Kaito: husband; widowed in Book 5.
Hana and Jace: daughters.
Jason: history "like London fog".
Her daughters grow up with "a dead father" and a mysterious absent uncle.
An elf, platinum-haired and fair-skinned, in fitted white adventuring gear.
Zealous: Rufus calls her "Zealous girl. Dangerously committed".
Ruthless: Farrah says "Anisa killed him before he could get a word out".
Defiant of correction: Gary tells her "You don't get a say in what we do anymore, Anisa... You're out".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: In the Book 3 fight she is "a near-perfect counter to Jason", protecting herself and cleansing afflictions.
A temporary addition to Rufus's party at the start of the books.
After Purity is implicated in the cult she vanishes with the archbishop and much of the Lasalle family.
Book 2: runs the temple's response to a star seed incident ("We are evacuating no one"); leads church militants to claim an abandoned site.
Book 3: meets the cult's Timos at the Vane estate; stands near Archbishop Hendren; dies in the battle (Book 3, Ch58-60 L5).
Rufus and Farrah: former party leaders.
Nicolas Hendren: her archbishop.
Jason notes most of the people he first met in this world are dead.

Roles: Director of the Network's Sydney operation, a government-faceless "suit" who hunts magic events from a helicopter, addressed as "Director" by Ketevan Arziani; on the Steering Committee of old family Network members in Book 5; UN Liaison to the Asano clan in Book 6; Under-Secretary-General of the Office of Supernatural Affairs by Book 11, an ex-Network official who knew Jason with "trust and scared".
Family: wife Susan; brother Terrance, the Network's media director.
Habits: Nigel Thornton's team is most often contracted by her, and Nigel says he came to Rexion on her job ("Anna Tilden. You know her, right?").
In Book 13 she sets up a meeting in Canberra for ambassadors and officials of the nations whose people were displaced; that she works with Boris Ket Lundi is from notes, Book 13.
Book 4: meets Jason and negotiates with him; her group's agreement template for his family is "the template we intend to use for your entire family".

Book 6: Anna is asked to be go-between for a meeting of Network, EOA and Cabal members held in Jason's spirit domain, and arrives with Craig Vermillion and Taika Williams; the meeting takes place outside the city of Nitra, where a magical dome has appeared, and the GDN is the Network's name after going public; Anna is asked to be go-between for a meeting arranged by the GDN, and arrives at the GDN camp in a party of eight that includes former EOA members who joined the GDN (to L8); that she belongs to the GDN delegation is not stated.

Book 12: she is a UN official in New York with an off-the-books observation team in Europe and sends contractors to the Asano clan; Asano's wish to recruit her is open knowledge among the delegation, and she is invited to Europe to talk to Jason; she suspects the System could be some cosmic force rather than Jason, and Jason answers with a System Administrator window, "I'm being as open as I can, Anna" (to L101); she then provisionally accepts his offer (to L106).
The fact that his interface was made available to everyone is stated to Jason in.
Book 13: arranges diplomacy; her UN successor is Holly Macrossan.
Dark-skinned, "even darker skin than her husband", with long hair dyed rainbow colours "in the Vitesse style".
Wry and perceptive: she tells a bureaucrat she can only assume he is eager to step through a portal, in a pointed tone that Allayeth enjoys.
Firm: "The amusement passed from Arabelle's face and the flint in the tone of her next words arrested his attention".
Cares for her patients: she helps Jason explore traumatic memories and teaches him how to recover.
Family-minded: "I think it's time for another child, husband. A daughter, this time".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Healer and therapist: a member of the Church of the Healer specialising in mental health and trauma recovery.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Life drain: she moves "through like a breeze, the enemies she touched with her hand collapsing to withered husks", each death leaving an urn of life force to fuel her other powers.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: In Book 10 she drains the magic from the undead, leaving them inert.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Medical advice: she and Carlos conclude Jason should use his mana as much as he can tolerate.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Administration: she organises procurement lists in the cloud palace's offices.
Old team: she, her husband Gabriel, Callum Morse and Emir were a team.
Never sent deep: as a valuable healer she was never sent deeper into the city than the surface during the Book 7 crisis.
Family: Roland Remore is her father-in-law.
Book 2-3: the strike on the cult island; therapy with Jason on the houseboat (Book 3, Ch24).
Book 8-9: Jason's recovery; she meets Jason's group in Rimaros and talks with him over tea.
Book 10: she stands up for Jason in the Yaresh meeting and fights in Cardinas.
Book 11-12: she advises Jason about giving Rufus space and travels in Onslow's shell.
Gabriel: her husband, an instructor of adventurers; see Gabriel_Remore.md.
Rufus: her son; she shares his concerns with Jason.
Sophie: she sits with Sophie and Melody.
Carlos: her working partner.
Emir and Callum: old teammates.
Laconic: Jason "happily fell into Argy's laconic pace".
Hospitable: he greets everyone he passes in the sealed streets.
Friendly nickname: "Emmett Dillivan, but folks just call me Argy".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Not an essence user in the lines read; his family has grown the fruit "longer than most can remember".
Named for the fruit he is eating, which looks like a large tangerine.
Book 7: leads Jason to town; walks them to the cliffs and waterfall cave.
Pelli: local mayor; he says "You'll want to talk to Pelli".
Jason: calls Palisaros "a genuine paradise".
Dry about herself: "I was always fancy".
Modest about her job: "I'm just an administrator there... My job is to keep the people doing the actual work happy and funded".
Deliberate in contact: she asked for the Sydney slot because she went to school with Jason.
Shaken by the gap between boy and man: the recording of Jason's power unnerved her, set against "the boy she had known" with his "sexy, impish grin".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: An executive-level Network administrator given an essence to reach category one, without monster cores.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She operates the helicopter's weapons when a winged lizard enters her sights.
Went to school with Jason and Greg.
Her mother Rabia sits on the Asano Village committee for the non-Asano families and helps introduce the village to magic.
Her cousin is Lina Karadeniz, who is also Emi's friend.
Book 4: she arrives with Anna and speaks with Jason's circle; follows Hector at the cloud lodge; visits the Network's local headquarters with Jason, Farrah and Jason's sister.
Book 5: on the plane and in the helicopter crew with Greg; sits beside Jason on the motorboat; the core of the new combat team with Greg and Kaito; dies in Berlin.
After: her family confronts Jason and her mother slaps him; the Karadeniz and Greg's families are brought into the Asano clan.
Jason: old school friend; she enters his spirit vault "as her relationship with Jason deepened".
Greg and Kaito: teammates.
Anna: "The bastards killed Asya".
Rabia and the Karadeniz family: mother and relatives.
Her death in Berlin is a loss the Karadeniz family blames on Jason and is later part of the clan tension around Emi and Lina.
Not described in the lines read; her body is a clone grown from her DNA with Cabal biological material.
Pressed by colleagues: Mr North and Mrs West press her to go along with them.
Composed about her condition: Jason says she has learned to manage the state left by her old programme.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She is the clan's energy-vampire research director.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She woke in a body that had been in stasis for more than a dozen years, the last remnant of a secret programme whose progenitors she had killed.
She ran a sketchy joint programme between the magical factions decades ago and has lived in a magic city for a decade among vampires.
Book 5: Mrs South among the Network committee; wakes in a new body.
Book 13: introduced to Team Biscuit; the Asano clan snatched her from the Network as a coup; research director.
Mr North: former committee colleague.
Jason: now her employer.
Her new body was cloned from her own DNA with Cabal biological material.
Baseph is Liara's husband, silver rank, met leaving her townhouse.
In Book 8 he hammers a pipe to draw raiders, fears what lies below because it is people who died because of what he did and is saved by Jason. He holds Liara's hand under the table.
Dara is the eldest, a one-star adventurer happy to hunt monsters, with Liara's height and Baseph's dark copper hair and eyes, a muscular frontline combatant.
Zareen is the middle child, physically smaller, with the royal family's sapphire hair and eyes, a politics enthusiast close to Vesper and a three-star adventurer.
Joseph is the youngest and only son, an administrative official with the Amouz family business interests like his father; he wants to meet the man who saved his father.
Dara's later remark about "the one from up north" with the elf twins refers to Rick.
He shares his name with Thadwick Mercer's father (Beaufort Mercer) but is not him.
Who he is: "the head of the Cult of the Builder's forces and their uneasy ally"; the gold-ranker "had given up his essence powers and was some manner of semi-artificial" being.
He would stay in his fifteen-foot metal skeleton war form if diplomacy allowed.
He has two extra arms, longer than his legs, wielding magically enhanced weapons swapped through his internal portal.
His view of himself: his true form is "so much more perfect than his old elf body, which now served as little more than a disguise".
Alliance: "Come now, Lorenn. The choice may be hard, but the calculation is easy"; he urges the brighthearts to abandon the cult's uneasy alliance if they must. They keep it.
Jason: he calls Jason "the Defier", "perhaps, the greatest enemy of my Lord Builder on this planet".

The cult's story: it invaded Cardinas with no interest in the natural array, fought its way into the local astral space and tried to sever it from the universe for the Builder; the astral space was too unique and they were trapped underground.
In battle: a trident shot from his arm, trailing a chain, injects a messenger with volatile liquid metal.
He and the cult's gold-rankers burrow into the enemy while silvers are spent where replaceable.

Meeting Jason: Jason says "I'm going to sneak through the enemy, talk with this Beaufort bloke"; Beaufort answers "If even our Lord finds dealing with him an issue, what chance does some god playing pretend have?".
Control of the cultists: Jason judges that "this Beaufort character seems to have them on a tight leash".
In the brightheart realm he leads the expedition through the empty heart of the chamber.
Allied council: the cult's leader in the alliance, who insists a decision should be "a group decision and not one for you alone".

Fighting on: he and Boris are the non-adventurer gold-rankers trapped with the adventurers; "The head Builder cultist was the one that dug their way out", his body "a massive frame of narrow metal and sharp blades, like a man made of scaffolding".

After the extraction: when Jason removes the star seeds, Beaufort loses his composure ("You did this to us, Asano") while Jason says "I still did this for you", and Jason presses him about what the cultists want now.
Playful and delighted by her own power: when she settles on the Charlatan confluence she says, with glee, "I was looking through the abilities it's known to give and they sound fantastic".
She teases Jason about Sophie (: "Has Sophie seen this whole half-naked, dirty workman thing you've got going on?").

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Essences: Magic, Trap and Adept, which she traded for in Book 2, producing the Charlatan confluence.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Abilities: Echo Spirit is her first charlatan ability; Bait and Switch, Rune Trap, Force Tether, Lightning Tether and Pit of the Reaper; shapeshifting.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Disguises: she infiltrates the Order of Redeeming Light as "Keth Gino" and, in the jungle territory of the transformation zone, passes as the silver messenger "Relia Vin Vala".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Aura disguise: her power gives her an edge in learning aura disguises, which she teaches Jason.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Storage: a personal storage space that even the Magic Society cannot peek into "without killing her first".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Familiars: Shimmer, a summoned astral lantern (; see Familiars/Shimmer.md), and an echo spirit that looks like a blurry version of her.

Grew up in the Old City with Sophie; began working with Clive at the Magic Society after she was caught; the notes add that in Rakesh she works as the off-campus errand-runner while the caste system dismisses her as unimportant; she tracks a signal in the desert south of Rakesh.
Book 12: teaches at Remore Academy, with Estella (earlier notes); her ex Jory Tillman is awkward around her.
Book 13: married to Estella Warnock; the wiki records them as dating in Book 12.
Cues: "Charlatan," she says with glee; she urges Jason to find an excuse to head up on deck where Sophie can see him.
Not described in the lines read; she carries a duffel of fight outfits.
Neutral by necessity: she is relieved but not fool enough to thank the messenger, as showing that his consideration mattered would get her punished.
Self-possessed: "Benella," she corrected with an annoyed shake of her head.
Uncertain under scrutiny: she is unsure why Kaal is interested in her thought process.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Not an essence user in the lines read; she is Zolit's aide, silent until the priest leaves.
Her master is Fal Vin Garath; he scolds her and demands she explain the servant races' different way.

Book 9: offers Jason fight outfits; Zolit's quiet aide at the fights; has "one chance to prove herself still valuable" by presenting Jason as a threat; presents to Voice Kaal; Kaal probes her emotions and deduces more.
Fal Vin Garath: her abusive master.
Jes Fin Kaal: the Voice she presents to.
Zolit: the fighter she aids.
Brisk: "We're going to move on the sand barge".
Encouraging: "Welcome to the path to bronze rank".
Compared with Cassandra's brother: Cassandra says the way Jason describes his brother reminds her of Beth.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Water healer; Jason envies her affliction-blanketing powers.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Struck down by the thorn fountain's retributive damage in the Fallen Echoes fight.
Introduces herself to Jason at the Adventure Society as Beth Cavendish, meeting her cousin Mose.
The Cavendish family names a Greenstone district.
Book 1: leads Hudson Kettering, Niko, Emily and Mose against the Ustei sand barge; Jason joins as a roaming scout.
Book 2: in the front cluster of the Fallen Echoes trial; her team fights Rick's team (Book 2, Ch29-30).
Book 3: trains against Jason's team in the mirage chamber.
Hudson, Niko, Emily, Mose: team members.
Jason: junior ally.
A messenger with no indoctrination, from Earth, who says "I'm from Earth, Asano" and that he has been on Earth "for a lot longer than you"; the television detail is from notes, Book 10.
Unorthodoxy messengers hid on Earth since before hominids; Earth was chosen because of the Builder sanction scandal; the Council of Kings avoids it.
He is Unorthodoxy secretly, serving under Vesta Carmis Zell, who hired him for his elemental powers; what she knows of astral kings outside the Council is from notes, Book 11.
The Cabal's "angelic founders" were messengers, and a database lists Boris Ketland as a Cabal executive; that he is a founder is from notes, Book 10.
In Book 13 he contemplates events from the Cabal's main headquarters in what was the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
He worked with the founder's familiar to betray the Network's founder to the early societies.
Messengers can hide their wings and shrink their size; Boris has long been comfortable with human proportions and once spent several millennia as a celestine research assistant.
Elemental powers; he can take two people with him when he returns to Earth; he draws ritual diagrams with Clive and Belinda to carry Rufus and Taika by egg-shaped conjured vessels.
Book 10: Gabriel and Arabelle Remore meet him at the death-chamber gate in Cardinas, where he gives his real name as Boris Ket Lundi.
Cue: "I am unfortunately inclined to agree," he tells Taika, and says he will attempt to simplify their situation.
Introduced by Emir as a gold-ranker who, if he does not want to be seen, cannot be seen by anyone short of diamond rank.
Described as "the gold-ranked assassination specialist" and the group's best scout; his attacks on a gold-rank priest land strongly but do not kill at once.
He, Gabriel and Arabelle Remore have been companions for decades.
Emir, Arabelle, Gabriel and Callum were an old team.
An avid monster-hunter, he is one of the few gold-rankers who obsessively raise their strength.

He stops Sophie and Humphrey from running off after the Order of the Reaper: "I'm stopping you until you are ready. Hate me if you like", and explains the order split from the cult and became self-serving assassins.
His fixation on Melody Jain, Sophie's mother, is because he is connected to her: she kept him as her only real connection to the order; he lost track of her and has searched ever since.
Jason avoids his petitions to see Melody, and finds his aura dangerously unstable even after things are in the open.
In Book 13 he conjures rats to track a creature through a pipe.
Book 2: scouts for the strike on the Builder cult's island.
Book 3: reports on the cultists' escape and the Purity evidence.
Book 6: stops Sophie and Humphrey in Kurdansk.
Books 8-10: petitions Jason to see Melody.
Book 13: part of the expedition, tracking a creature in a pipe with conjured rats.
Quiet, patient and unfazed; he lets a hard decision stand and speaks plainly. "Sensible," Callum agrees.
A broad-shouldered, swarthy man with the polished perfection of gold rank, who wears casual clothes rather than Healer robes.
"A humble man in simple clothes, though the world will not let a gold-ranker be too humble".
Priest first: "First and foremost, though I am a priest of the Healer. Before anything else, I'm here to help you, not for you to help me".
Uneasy at society events: Arabelle plays guide to "Carlos, a priest of the Healer who was not comfortable at fancy social events".

Dogged: he once harangued Jason to be an experimental subject when Jason had barely woken from a coma, and Jason threw him across the room with his aura; Carlos backing down since is called "considerable progress".
Protective of patients: in a lab coat and a glare he looks "like a doctor shooing people away from his harried patient".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Specialty: "Finding and dealing with soul influences is his specialty; he's at the top of his field. From star seeds to vampirism to plain soul trauma, he's the best there is".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Star seeds: the Healer's church took over extracting star seeds from Purity: "we, the church of the Healer, have taken over that task"; he warns that extraction can be lethal without continuous healing.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rituals: gold-rank soul-projection ritual lamps and circles.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Soul realm research: he conducts his research inside Jason's soul realm because there "pain, damage, even death itself could be suspended"; they work seven hours of ritual magic and pseudo-surgery.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: The Quilido Procedure: a slow process that removes the taint of monster cores from an essence user (see EDJI_and_Post_Reveal_Institutions.md).
He once met Amos Pensinata "in a lunatic's dungeon" and has worked with Arabelle many times.
The leader and healer of Team Work Saw.
Book 3: arrives in Greenstone portalled and examines Jason; helps with soul projection and the adventurer group therapy (Ch23).
Book 8-9: leads his team; he helps Jason after the coma; goes with Arabelle on the long journey.
Book 10: develops the calming technique for Melody with Jason and Amos, explains how the Flames differ from lesser vampirism, and is one of the gold-rank participants in Cardinas.
Book 12-13: soul-realm research (Book 12, Ch9) and the Earth healing work with Neil and Ian.
Arabelle: long-time colleague and the other half of the therapy partnership.
Jason: patient, research subject and eventually collaborator; he can still be thrown across the room.
Melody Jain: his long-term case.
His work on the Flames of Redemption leads to the Book 10 conclusion that they are an extreme modification of lesser vampirism.
Smart, capable and "gorgeous", the object of many Mercer-orbit boys' crushes.
Her mother looks "more like her daughter's sister" thanks to silver-rank essences.
Sweet and sharp: she investigates Jason's background and kisses him back forcefully.
Drawn to rescue: she thinks of a hot shower after bog monsters.
Bound by family: Neil explains that she dumped Jason "not because she wanted to, but because her family decided he wasn't going to amount to anything".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Bronze rank with a hidden aura in Book 1; by Book 12 her team fights silver-rank bog monsters.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Thalia oversaw her training personally.
Four years older than Neil, who had a crush on her.
Her brother tried to kill Jason.
Book 1: awakens to breakfast being laid; Jason and Cassandra's first kiss.
Book 2: on the family boat with Jason.
Book 12: leaves the jobs hall with Jiralla and Henrietta Geller; meets the changed Jason.
Book 13: Thalia watches her from afar.
Jason: first romance, ended by her family.
Neil: admirer from youth.
Thalia and Thadwick: mother and brother.
Not described in the lines read; he flies "superhero-style" while Allayeth sits on a throne of glittering lights.
Sociable: "Lord Charist was the more social of the two".
Courtly: "Your father is known to me. Convey my regards".
Reluctant: he "dislikes many of the responsibilities that come with his level of power".
Sheepish: he looks like a child caught doing something stupid when Allayeth calls out his approach.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Diamond-rank; no silver-ranker can open a portal that diamond-rankers can use.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He eavesdrops on Jason and Allayeth's talks.
Resident of Yaresh; he and Allayeth stay in the city because its people love Hana Shavar.
Book 9: finds Schaat's corpse with Allayeth and demands to know "what's going on here".
Book 10: arrives with Allayeth; his approach discussed behind a privacy screen.
Book 12: at the reunion VIP gathering.
Allayeth: fellow diamond.
Jason: opposed then wary; Jason tells Allayeth "you know your friend Charist is listening".
Strong-willed: she flashes "a well-recognised look of dissatisfaction" at Jason's poke but calms herself.
Stern: Jason jokes "Mum is quite stern".
Grieving: she looks at Jason "like she'd seen a ghost" and hugs him tightly once she steels her nerve.
Overworked: she hasn't been into the office in two days, unlike her.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She is "the pre-eminent upscale realtor in the Greater Casselton area".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She is non-essence in the lines read; portal travel sickens her.
Her family are "miners and farmers, tracing their bloodline back through bushrangers, convicts, and indigenous Australians"; she was the one fascinated with Japan.
Her brother is Robert; her mother makes a miraculous recovery.
Jason is told his parents divorced a year ago and that his mother moved to Castle Reach.
Book 1-2: Jason describes his mother's side as rural.
Book 4: the hospital waiting room; the hug; the houseboat portal; the family meeting.
Jason: son.
Erika and Kaito: other children.
Amy: puts a restraining hand on Cheryl's arm.
Not described beyond her hazmat suit in the quarantine tent.
Wry: "My biggest enemy beat me out for the good parking space at the hospital where I used to work".
Awed but steady: she watches Jason calm the ward "in disbelief".
Friendly: Jason calls her "a good egg".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A medical scientist, not an essence user in the lines read; by Book 13 she works with healers on magical healing.
French; a Doctors Without Borders epidemiologist.
In Book 11 she and her family are displaced by the vampire occupation and taken in by the clan.
Book 5: the quarantine tent and Jason's family meeting.
Book 11: sheltered with the clan.
Book 13: healing discussion; Taika jokes with her over Kenny Loggins.
Jason: friend.
Ian: works with him on healing.
Vincent Baudrillard: same family.
Dark cascading hair and a walk "so sultry she was almost swerving"; she looks only a few years older than the two women with her.
Calculating: "The key to controlling a person was finding what they wanted".
Amused: she is "happily imagining the look on Silva's face" as she watches Sophie's match.
Irritated by independence: she is less happy with Sophie's friend Belinda.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rank is not stated in the lines read; she travels with a huge leonid bodyguard.
Lives in a sprawling manor in Old City's canal district, which has its own internal city wall.
Her arrangement with Sophie: Sophie would help her provoke Silva into the kind of rash action his father would have prevented.
Book 1: enters the chamber with Sophie and Belinda; watches Sophie's match; learns Lucian's wants; summons Sophie and Belinda to her manor.
Sophie: indentured servant.
Cole Silva: rival, newest of the Big Three.
Lucian Lamprey: someone she plans to control.
"Rather tall, but his narrow frame and hunched posture made him seem lanky and awkward", wearing voluminous scholarly robes that "dangled off him like they'd been hung out to dry".
A lecturer who loses the thread and apologises ("Sorry. Where were we?"); he wants dumpling soup in the middle of his own lecture on the cosmos.
He says he venerates, not worships, the Celestial Book: "There's a difference"; an archbishop asks "You admit to being a heretic?" and Clive answers that he "could be considered a heretic".
He jokes about his background: "I'm the son of eel farmers".
A stranger accuses him of sleeping with a wife he says he does not have, which becomes a running gag.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Essences: Magic, Rune, Balance and the Karmic confluence (: "Clive has the magic, rune, balance and karmic essences").

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A rune essence came to him as "an epic four-star essence".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Abilities: Wrath of the Magister, a rune circle that triggers effects when attacked, the damage-reflecting buff Mantle of Retribution and the zone ability Eye of Karma; Mana Equilibrium.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Racial gift: a blessing from the Celestial Book changed his human Special Attack Affinity into a spell affinity.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Familiar: Onslow (see Familiars/Onslow.md), a rune tortoise who sits at the prow of the airboat, carries Clive, and becomes a runic tattoo on his torso when called back.
Grew up on an eel farm in the delta near Greenstone; recruited to the Magic Society by the Greenstone branch's then-director.
His family sheltered in the Geller estate during the surge before last.
Book 3: identifies the vessel nature of the Reaper-trial astral space and plans the inversion.
Books 11-12: Archchancellor of the Magical Research Association, a rival to the Magic Society.
Book 13: by 2038 he and Lorelei Grantham are in a relationship that gives his Balance essence the equilibrium it needed.
Cues: "Sorry. Where were we? Right, formation interactivity"; "Having a conversation with you is like wrestling an eel".
Rash: Clarissa plans to provoke him "into the kind of rash action that his father always kept him from making".
Predatory: his father's protection of Sophie is gone and he watches her match from a viewing box.
His father had a small operation catering to nobles with low tastes, with the money and connections to arrange expensive cleansings.
The father died in his sleep "a couple of months ago"; the son stepped up.
Cole's father killed a man who tried to rob him.
Book 1: watches Sophie's match.
Book 2: Jason is told he put himself "in the path of Cole Silva and Lucian Lamprey".
Book 3: the elf Palpatine-to-Vader joke; held in the prison tower with Lamprey; his organisation fights over succession after his arrest.
Book 9: Jason's kidnapping and star seed implantation are traced to him and Lamprey.
Clarissa Ventress: rival crime lord.
Lucian Lamprey: partner in the kidnapping.
Normally shoulder-length brown hair, which she cropped short before reaching gold; pale skin and light green and brown armour.
Steadying: she subtly indicates which guests will not respond well to Jason's social graces.
Detail-oriented: "the detail-oriented half of the pairing, which sometimes made her closer to a babysitter than she would admit to liking".
Dry and firm with Emir: she gives her husband "a stern look"; Jason checks with her rather than him.
Pragmatic: "What we missed doesn't matter. What we do now does".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver rank in Book 2; she holds off three enemies in the island battle, one the construct that killed Farrah.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Gold rank by Book 9, only for a couple of years when Jason hides his aura from her.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She is part of the reformed gold-rank team for the Cardinas mission.
Emir's chief of staff, "the object of his affections"; she took leave and went with Callum Morse, intending not to return until she reached gold rank.
Emir and Constance had moved around each other for years with a power imbalance between employer and employee, gold and silver.
Book 1-2: waits at the palace exit with Emir and Jason; among the strike force; watches Sophie.
Book 6: returns at gold rank.
Book 9: trained with Callum; the office meeting with Jason.
Book 10: replaces Callum on the mission; the sphere.
Emir: employer, then husband; "Emir's wife" and chief of staff.
Callum: her trainer, who puts a calming hand on her arm.
Sophie and Humphrey: she warns Humphrey she will tell his mother.
A vampire who drives a 1967 Maserati Ghibli.
Casual behind the mystique: "Craig is fine when I'm not on the job. I have to play it sinister and mysterious around the normals".
Helpful: Jason thanks him for the information.
Wry: "I say roll with it... You built this place for melodrama, right?".
Troubled: he worries about the sane vampires' future.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Vampire for seventy years; every aura in the room trembles at the name Vermillion.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: By Book 12 he has accelerated to gold rank by feeding on several risen vampire lords, though he lacked the power to defeat a lord himself.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Jason developed his blend-into-crowds technique by studying Craig's aura.
The Cabal's Sydney front man.
Explains the magical world's three dominant forces and that a new magic appeared five centuries ago.
Book 4: briefs Jason (Book 4, Ch9-11); Jason telepathically tells him how to bring Hiro; with Greg and Asya.
Book 5-6: the townhouse once Hiro's; crystal bottle on the boat with the winch; Erika calls him a longtime student of magical politics.
Book 12-13: stands beside Jason on the roof; the park bench; walks into the room.
Jason: friend.
Hiro: Jason asks him to fetch Hiro.
Susan: "Craig Vermillion was always so nice".
A young-looking woman in her early thirties with olive skin and dark hair, "no older than her son Landemere".
Standing next to the ordinary-looking high priest Darryl, she is "the beautiful Cressida Vane".
Haughty: "I am Lady Cressida Vane"; Jason mocks her high-priestess name.
Traditional: "This is my manor, my family, and we do things the traditional way".
Dismissive of her husband: "I don't care what my stupid husband thinks; he married into the family".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Leader of the blood cult family's rituals.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Complained that astral beings were "the death" of her son.
Mother of Landemere Vane; she asks what Landemere was trying to summon.
Book 1: the basement scene; her body lands on the chamber floor, not the pool; Jason reflects on her.
Book 2: Jason asks Clive what she said about her son.
Landemere: son.
Darryl: the high priest beside her.
Her body ends up on the stone floor at the edge of the chamber rather than in the pool; Jason later alludes to her head being "smashed open".
Silver-rank and ageless-looking: she seems about thirty and is fifty in fact; Jason sees the same agelessness in Emir and Thalia Mercer.
In Book 1 she "may have looked too young to be Humphrey's mother".
In Book 7 she is gold-rank with dark olive skin and black hair.

She defends the family's methods (the Geller estate trains the whole family in low-magic Greenstone, notes, Book 1), gives blunt strategic advice ("Nothing speaks louder than power", notes, Book 3; "do the opposite of every instinct", notes, Book 12), and teases her son at once when she hears a name: "Gabrielle?", in a tone of having latched on to a weakness.
She is shown as a diplomacy teacher: "diplomacy is war".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Time: a time confluence, with only forward time travel possible; in Book 3 she outpaces Lucian Lamprey in a fight, teleporting behind him and cutting his neck. She is called "Time Witch of Vitesse".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Dimension: a dimension essence, as Emir says, with gold rank from the notes; she teleports behind Lamprey in a fight.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Estate and training: the Geller estate's mirage chamber can run at bronze rank only "for limited periods" because Greenstone's magic is low, and at iron rank Danielle offers it to Rufus; a family member from the generation that first settled the region may still be alive.
Mother of Humphrey and wife of Keith Geller.
The Geller family's wall is older than the Old City.
Book 1: Gabriel Remore asks about "this outworlder of yours" in a call; Danielle leads the search pattern on the Greenstone expedition into the desert astral space, where Henry Geller dies.
Book 7: takes the 119 outworlders to the Geller estate in Cyrion.
Book 11: sits with Gwydion Remore, a priest of Hero, at her table and later helps Lorenn with diplomacy.
Book 12: Jason asks her to be his political adviser on Earth.
Cues: "Gabrielle?", asked as if she has latched on to a weakness; "I said that diplomacy is war, Jason, and wars have objectives".
Dawn is the World-Phoenix's First Servant, the head of its cult and its primary vessel (describes the post; the notes identify Dawn as holder of it, notes, Book 4).
Her true body is a celestine with ruby eyes and hair.
She appears in many avatars; Jason kills and loots one (: "I killed and looted Dawn"; the replacement avatar is described in).
In Book 7 her vessel is a cottage inside a floating bubble that carries her; in Book 9 a recording crystal projects her face over a projector.

When Jason has just punched her avatar she says "You realise that you could have asked that instead of punching my nose through my brain" and teases that she is "a little more mature than someone who just turned twenty-six".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Role: First Servant of the World-Phoenix, head of its cult and the primary vessel of the great astral being.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Diamond-rank vessels of great astral beings can withstand the strain and keep their selves, and former vessels end up as peak existences.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: One intervention: the Hierophant is allowed to intervene in Pallimustus a single time (Soramir to Jason); in Book 7 she says she will use one full-power intervention, and she destroys a Builder rolling city with a phoenix.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Art: the paintings by "Dawn" that Jason buys show two planets with four pillars and "The Invasion of Pallimustus".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Home: Interstice, the city-universe at the cosmos's centre.
Book 5: arrives at Asano Village in a new avatar; explains the danger of transformation zones as dimensional ulceration; tells him the Reaper "was the one who offered" Farrah's return.
Book 6: arrives in her true body to negotiate with the Builder after Shako kills Jason.
Book 13: Boris says "Dawn exceeded mandate".
Jason, the World-Phoenix (Helsveth is the current prime vessel), Shako ("I cared about you very deeply, once", notes, Book 6), Soramir Rimaros.
Cue: "You realise that you could have asked that instead of punching my nose through my brain".
Leader from the front: his messengers "had inherited the toughness of the massive brightheart Durrum, who led them from the front"; Lorus pushes aggressively while Durrum is "more conservative".
Origins of his territory: he and Lorus arrived after claiming other territories and looking to expand; their standoff lasted so long that the Undeath priests and the Builder cult forced the issue.
Anti-cult but practical: he "hated the Builder cult as much as every other brightheart, yet had been willing to abide by their alliance" and tries to reconcile the cult and the brighthearts.
In battle: his earth powers leave him unobstructed by mud, strong enough to hurl enemy messengers and undead aside as he fights his way to Lorus.
Confronting Lorus: "LORUS! Are you betraying us?" and "Every second we spend arguing or fighting the cultists takes us closer to defeat. You're killing us".
He warns Lorus not to give a lightning-wielding Neil a reason to make him the demonstration.
Wall and talks: his protective wall, with Dustin's, keeps the cultists from attacking the brighthearts on sight so that all sides agree to talk.
Calling out Lorus: "Because you hid yours behind mine and let them do the dying"; he tells Lorus to let "the aboveworlder finish".
Terms: if Neil can bring lightning control into each new territory he will agree to Neil's leadership, and he asks him to share how the lightning is controlled.
Trust: "I am willing to trust in our people. In the strength we have, not that of the monsters we've shackled"; he accepts Lorus's territory. The cult says it will follow Durrum.
Relief: after he claims the territory he first feels power, then relief when it is gone.
The rabbit: he looms over Nik and challenges his claim to know how things are done where he comes from.
He says "Asano took what was left of my people and gave them a haven... I would never do anything to offend him".
Ambush: he and another earth brightheart, Kurik, hide Neil, Dustin and elite brighthearts underground to spring a trap on the priests.
His rumbling voice, "a sound like gravel being crushed", is the signature.
One of Thadwick Mercer's two offsiders with Neil: he protects the group with his powers while Neil heals them.
The Davone and Kettering families have close ties to the Mercers, which is how the boys came to Thadwick's side.
He and Neil are relieved to be free, having been known as Thadwick's flunkeys.
A local who fills Jonah Geller's defender role on Rick's team: "a classic defender, not very mobile but very hard to go around or through", clad in armour forged entirely of ice.
His cousin Hudson Kettering is his counterpart on Beth Cavendish's team.
In Book 7 he is a friend of Neil's from their time on Thadwick's team; by Book 9 he is the only non-local on Rick's team, picked up after Jonah's death.
In Book 11 he is dropped into the same territory as Neil, gives the party a frontline and healer pairing and helps hold a protective wall between brighthearts and Builder cultists.
Book 1-2: Thadwick's team, then Rick's.
Book 7: arrives with Rick's group in Rimaros.
Book 10-11: fights messengers on Rick's team, where Stash smashes him and Rick together; in Book 11 he and Neil claim a territory as a defender-healer pair.
Dry and steady, a shield for others; he points out hard truths about the weight of numbers.
Pale skin, red lips, delicate features and midnight hair; her face lacks an essence user's polish, but her slight smile and smouldering eyes hold "the seductive promise of sultry intelligence".
She moves in a ball gown "like she was floating".
Dangerous when asked her name: those around her stopped asking if she was Báthory once she started "immediately eating anyone who did".
Pragmatic: her edicts about treating humans better were not compassion; they bought sustainability.
Primus inter pares: Jason says "You clearly have primacy amongst them" about the other vampires.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A gold-ranker and "a master of luring groups into traps set out using blood rituals".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She and Mr North pair their ritual magics for defence; her five ritual circles send out red tentacles that extend and snake round corners to squeeze the vorger.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Humanity tried to kill her with a nuclear device flooding Rome with magical sunlight, modified from a design Travis made for Jason.
Under her, the vampires establish a détente: every major city still hides vampires, and bombings in Europe are answered by assassinations in Beijing, Washington, Moscow and London.
She rests in a vault in Venice that was once a bank.
Book 6: led out to Jason by Shade and settled with the coalition; fights the vorger.
Book 11: leader of the European vampires and target of the sunlight device.
Book 13: with Gerling and her blood orb trailing "like pets", steps through a portal, followed by Remy; at a meeting table opposite Neil, Carlos and Ian.
Gerling: her blood slave.
Mr North: ally in ritual defence.
Jason: he asks her to settle the other vampires, acknowledging her primacy.
Her treatment of humans is strategic rather than compassionate.
An elf; Jason had spoken with her only once before the inquiry.
Controlling: Dorgan tells her "Your mistake was your need to feel in control".
Wary of Jason: she asks "What is it you want in return for silence?".
Resentful: "she felt trapped" while her father felt elevated.
Unwilling to forget: she recalls lifting "some jumped up iron-ranker by the throat" on the spot where he returns.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She can lift a person by the throat with her powers.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She is flanked by her deputy, Genevieve.
Director of the Greenstone branch.
Raised in secret by her mother, with clandestine visits to her father Dorgan.
Her backroom dealings and her status as "daughter of an Old City crime lord" were dragged into the light after the disastrous expedition.
Her father rose from last of the Big Three crime lords to legitimate mayor of Old City.
Book 1: pointed out to Jason at a social outing; sits at the inquiry bench; greets the party at the platform; confronts Jason in her office.
Book 2: tea with her father; attends the party.
Book 9: among adventurers uneasy at a strange cloak monster.
Book 12: waits in her office and is first in the meet-and-greet line.
Dorgan: father.
Jason: antagonist turned polite acquaintance.
Lucian Lamprey: the power she bargained with.
Her parentage was once secret.
She is twelve when he comes home in Book 4 and learns the truth about magic from him.
She trains in ritual magic under Farrah, decides at thirteen that she does not want to fight as he does, and takes her essences at about sixteen under Rufus.
By Book 13 she is an upper-silver ritualist and researcher, and Vincent Baudrillard's partner.
The System names her as the contact "Emi Evans-Asano" when Jason returns, and he senses her aura with Erika's and Ian's.
Jason calls her "Moppet".
Her father says she has always been hard to parent: "You thought you were smarter than me by age seven, and by age nine, you were right.".
Jason's remark on her at twelve is "twelve going on forty".
Erika says Emi took his death hard and that Erika's own conspiracy-theory phase did not help.
Her cousins are Hana and Jace, Kaito and Amy's daughters; her great-grandmother Yumi is "Nana Yumi" to her.
By Book 11 she is described as "the princess of the Asano clan".
At twelve she stands up to a group of boys picking on another student at Jason's old school, which Jason watches through Shade.
Jason promises Erika he will tell her everything.
Emi guesses something is wrong from how her parents are acting, throws herself into his arms when he appears, and her parents nod their agreement to let her go with him.
He takes her for a drive, and she asks whether he is "the Starlight Angel".
At a coastal lookout he asks "Do you believe in magic, Emi?", the car dissolves into his shadow, and she says "You're him".
He takes her through a portal arch, her first dimensional translocation, and she endures it better than expected.
She asks Jason to help Nanna, who has Alzheimer's, and he says it looks like it worked.
She enjoys "having this big secret", is introduced to Shade as "Miss Emi", and has seen Jason's recordings.
She vanishes her scooter into Shade's storage in front of two police officers, and leads Farrah by the hand into the bar lounge when Farrah first arrives.
She asks to be Jason's assistant "when I get magic powers".
Jason plans to take her out of school for intensive training.
At his farewell barbecue she is angry that he is leaving again, then runs back through the portal to hug him.
She sends recordings to and from Jason through Shade and is "especially excited" about her ritual magic lessons with Farrah, which take the sting out of not being old enough for essences.
She shows Jason round the new family compound, pointing out the training facilities and the Network office.
She tells reporter Dennier his story was "an exercise in buffoonery".
Erika sends her to Coffs Harbour to make sure no monster waves arrive, and Jason jokes about her "dimensional membrane protrusion-precursor analysis".
Erika is unwilling to put her thirteen-year-old daughter near that.
She flies with the family to Japan and goes down the sea-cave shaft with Jason.
The essences Jason picked for her were chosen to keep her safe, and she would not be ready for essences for about a year.
After the death of her uncle Kaito ("Uncle Kai"), she tells Jason she does not want to kill things or be an adventurer, and he says he is not disappointed.
She adds that he took her out of school for training.
She chooses a specialty, formation interactivity (the interference between nearby magical formations), though Farrah advises her to see the breadth of options first.
In Book 6 she tells Dawn that almost everyone at the cloud palace is an Asano and Dawn should call him Jason.
Jason works at being "the cool uncle", which has not restored their old closeness, but she is less ill at ease.
Ritual magic: before she had essences she had "greater command of ritual magic than most people on Earth".
Travis names her and Hiro as the clan's people with strong magical-theory knowledge, taught by Farrah.
Essences: she picks Vast, Myriad and Harmonic, two legendaries and an epic, which she expects to produce the Unity confluence.
Rufus conducts the absorption rite, and her confluence is Resonant.
Combat rituals: she is "the one person on Earth able to use them", with stacked ritual-circle shields whose synergy magnifies each shield.
She uses Consolidate Mana to turn broken rituals into power for her next spell.
Cube devices: nine cubes of shimmering dark metal from the outermost reaches of the astral space orbit her, each face divided into nine rune sections.
They keep her and others aloft, and she builds cube constructs with Clive and Gary.

Rank: she is bronze when she faces a silver-rank manticore with her team, silver by the time of the rooftop scene and still in the upper reaches of silver in Book 13, because she favours magic research over combat.
Once Jason and Farrah leave Earth, the family grows "strangely protective" and she goes from wizard back to teenager.
Only she receives one-on-one training from Rufus and Taika.
She moves to Saint-Étienne, where she befriends Lina Karadeniz, cousin of Asya, though the Karadeniz family blame Jason for Asya's death and politics strain the friendship.
Erika wants her to use monster cores like her parents, and Ian suggests forty-eight as the age; Emi says she will not use cores.
Rufus tells her parents "Emi isn't an adventurer" and that she is too focused on fighting monsters at the cost of her studies, partly because she is running from her mother.
Her relationship with Erika is soured by her refusal to use cores.
After her team's manticore fight, Rufus talks to her as a commanding officer would.
Travis recalls that after Jason left, things were tense between Erika and Emi for a long time, and she blamed her mother and herself.
In the last scene of Book 12 she walks out of a bakery to find a portal arch, rams into Jason and he says "Hey, Moppet".
She meets Zara and tells her about the recordings of Jason's first visit.
She stands with Jason on a platform in a tree mansion in Arbour.
Vincent Baudrillard is her lover and Jason notes that she is a grown woman who does not need his protection.
Shade has looked after her since she was young.
She and Vincent have an apartment, and she explores the tower in Saint-Étienne with him.
She works the bar with Jason at a pop-up stand, and she studies a completed ritual circle with Clive.
She waits beside Bussinger, floating just above the floor, as Bussinger wakes from the ritual.
When Nik reaches gold, she tells Jason on a rooftop that she is sorry she is not there yet.
She floats in meditation with Jason and Nik over the River Furan.
Voice (condensed): sharp, literary and political at thirteen; she can flip from a death glare to wide-eyed innocence; she teases her uncle.
Not a fighter by temperament: she told Jason she did not want to kill things, then ran toward monsters in Book 11 against her mother's wishes. Keep both pulls in the scene.
Her pressure points: her mother's protectiveness, being treated as the clan's princess, and Jason's long absences.
Dark-skinned, with dark curly hair tied back behind his head, "midnight skin" and sleek clothes.
He wears his hair in colourful beads, close to the head.
He "looked no more than thirty but ageless" and dresses well, largely thanks to Constance.
He carries a staff he can extend and shrink.
Likes grand entrances: "I'm hosting a grand event. It requires grandeur".
He announces a competition and a grand-prize cloud palace in a speech that throws the crowd into turmoil.
Warm and wry: he tells Rufus "Comrades behind her, enemies in front of her and friends beside her" of Farrah's apparent death and sighs "world-weary" when Jason storms off.
Cautious in accusation: "Making that kind of accusation against a church is no small matter and even I'm not completely convinced yet".
Not used to being the responsible one: that is Constance's job, but he is the older and higher-ranked man.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Essences: he has "staff, might, magic and mystic".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Cloud ship and palace: a cloud ship the size of an ocean liner that morphs into a palace (; see Cloud_Constructs_and_Palaces.md).

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: His preferred design is a five-towered castle.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Staff and speed: he conjures copies of his staff under every construct, smashing the iron and bronze ones and tossing the silvers and catches Danielle before she can lunge.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Aura mastery: he can block the senses of others, normally taught only to gold-rankers.
The Reaper search: he has "studied the style more than most outsiders to the Order of the Reaper" and hypothesised that it was meant to be learned through skill books.
His patron's search for Order remnants is why Emir has hunted them for years.
Old team: he, Arabelle, Gabriel and Callum Morse were a team.
Family: a son who died, whose wife died with him, leaving his granddaughter Ketis, raised by her grandmother.
Books 1-3: the team moves into his cloud palace, and his chief of staff Constance is among the silver-rankers of the strike force on the Builder cult island.
Books 6-9: he waits for Constance to reach gold and marries her; Jason calls on him as an old ally and tells him of his changes (Book 9, Ch49-51).
Books 10-12: his palace hosts the large meetings; in Cardinas he deflects debris from the collapsing wall; in Book 12 he and his wife rise to greet newcomers.
Constance: his chief of staff and "the object of his affections"; she returns at gold rank and they marry.
Jason: he gives him a thick notebook of cloud flask knowledge and is startled by the change in him in Book 9.
Callum Morse: old teammate.
Sophie: she and Emir used Sophie as bait for the order, which Callum resented.
He knew of the Order of the Reaper's return long before the team.
Silver metal wings, alabaster skin, amber glass eyes and no hair, in a toga of interlaced metal.
Insistent on names: "His name is the Builder... He is not one of our kind anymore".
Corrects titles: he corrects Jamis's usage of the Builder's name.
Supervisory: he warns that the planet goes nowhere unless civility is kept.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Prime vessel of the Builder; the avatars gather around him on the dimensional ship.
Originally a messenger of the Unorthodoxy, he says he has moved on from it.
Became prime vessel after the Sundered Throne took Shako.
Book 10: the observation-room scene with the astral king avatars.
Jamis Fran Muskar: an astral king whose avatar he corrects.
The Builder: the god he serves.
Not described in the lines read, apart from clothes: she and Ian wear old faded ultra-casual clothes "like it was laundry day" when Jason warns they will not want to wear them again.
Strict-rules household: she and Jason "had grown up with their mother's strict rules about not bringing conflict to the dinner table".
Protective and blunt: she storms into her daughter's bedroom when Jason, Emi and Taika are playing a rhythm game.
A professional: "being the experienced media personality, she had attached herself to the tour" of the hospital, wanting to "reel in her brother's impulsive nature".
Frank about fear: "I'm her mother and I don't like her going out and risking her life. Is that so hard to understand?".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: By Book 11 she is the food logistics director for the whole clan.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She wants Emi to use monster cores like her parents, and Emi's refusal sours their relationship.
She lives in Melbourne with Ian and Emi; her series films in Melbourne and she misses "her big parties in Melbourne" after moving north.
She is Jason's elder sister, with Kaito among her brothers.
Book 4: Jason finds her family's names on his contact list, reunites with them, and she throws a birthday party.
Book 5: she acts as media guide at the medical centre and, with Emi, acts as Jason's ambassador to the family while he is away.
Book 11: she meets Rufus ("I recognise you from my brother's recordings"), walks with him and Ian to the administration centre arguing over Emi's training.
Book 13: she nods Jason out onto the deck for a private talk, and she and Ian tease about marriage.
Ian Evans: her husband, a doctor.
Emi: her daughter, whom she tries to keep from combat.
Jason: "Erika clinging to him like she was afraid he'd disappear again"; she shares his look when he wants a topic changed.
Kaito: she mourns him with Emi.
Hard to surprise, prefers anonymity: she tells a contact she would rather keep her identity from someone who "doesn't know who I am".
Nervous in waiting: she fails to concentrate on a book on a rooftop while a monster manifestation is expected.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Fourfold senses: Jason says they make her "even better than I am" at spotting messenger agents; she maps messenger agents in the city.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She "made a career out of being a spy and urban scout in Livaros" and knows the island's streets, alleys and rooftops.
A Livaros spy and scout.
Book 7: tells a contact she would rather keep her identity hidden; later waits on a rooftop.
Book 9: beside Jason at the gate of Yaresh.
Book 10: maps messenger agents.
Book 13: Belinda's wife.
Belinda: wife.
Jason: employer.
Fair skin and golden hair, a physical counterpart to the other silver messenger.
Imperious: he scowls at Benella and demands answers in a voice "like a command from the heavens".
Resentful of command: he "detested being forced to act at the behest of the Voice of the Will" and sneers at his commander, astral king's Voice and Asano.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver rank; he launches a soul attack on Jason through his connection to Shade and is surprised when Jason fends it off and retaliates.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He seizes Shade and squeezes while Shade drains his mana, until Shade's body is destroyed.
Benella's master, "abusive but not outside the bounds of acceptability to his fellow messengers", free to treat the servant races as he pleased so long as it did not impinge on other messengers.
Book 9: scolds Benella; soul attack and Shade fight; sent on a mission by Kaal.
Benella: his servant.
Jes Fin Kaal: his commander.
Hess Jor Nasala: sits with him at Kaal's meeting.
A familiar is a purely magical creature from the deep astral given a body by a summoning (Clive).
Who: a shadowy figure who appears in Book 2 as the entity that governs the trials of the City of Fallen Echoes.
He was the summoned familiar of the Order of the Reaper's last grandmaster, an outworlder with the dark essence, before he became Jason's.
Book 11 identifies him as one of the Reaper's shadows; the wiki calls him the Reaper's shadow.

Powers: Jason's gold-rank sheet lists Shadow of the Hegemon as three bodies at iron, seven at bronze (with minor physical force and dimensional storage), thirty-one at silver and two hundred and eleven at gold; the notes' detail of incorporeal bodies hiding in other people's shadows and draining mana by touch is from notes, Book 2.
On reaching silver any shadow body can teleport to any other, and the bodies can form vehicles.
Incantation: Jason's summoning chant begins "I call to the realm beyond cold and darkness, where death has no meaning, for life has no place. Let mine be the dark beyond darkness...".
Evolution (Level 3): "Shadow of the Reaper [Shade] has sanctioned himself" and becomes a Shadow of the Hegemon.
His brother Umber is the enemy who plants a ritual to trap Jason's consciousness.
Jason names him in Book 1: "I've decided to call him Colin. And his friends. Team Colin.".

He is summoned using an awakening stone looted from a sanguine horror (on the Flesh Pit in his soul realm: "I looted the awakening stone that let me summon Colin") and lives in Jason's blood: Jason pricks his finger and lets him "melt back into his bloodstream".

Evolutions: a blood clone, four red-eyed copies of Jason, by Book 13 (the Book 5 date is from notes); in Book 9 Colin can awaken as a Voice of the Will after extended hibernation in the astral kingdom.
Origin: Colin comes from the border region between the realms of the All-Devouring Eye and Legion, Legion being the great astral being who administers the cosmic rules of life.
Manner: eager to eat: "I'm definitely not going to eat that. Next time, you should fight the god of blood or flesh. I'll tuck right in there".
Who: Jason's third familiar, named by him in Book 2.
A disembodied dark cloak with a nebula in the shape of an eye in the chest, with blue and orange orbs "drifting around".

Powers: two floating orbs fire sustained beams: an orange beam of resonating-force damage that penetrates armour and a blue beam of disruptive-force damage that works against magical protection and incorporeal enemies.
His orbs also deliver the Harbinger of Doom affliction and create shield orbs.
In Book 9 he draws a massive magical orrery.
Origin: Gordon comes from the realm of the All-Devouring Eye, as the messenger Carmen says in Book 8.
Who: Humphrey Geller's familiar, whose full name is Velitraxistaasch; "He likes 'Stash,' though".
