A mirage dragon who takes small forms: a mouse in Humphrey's pocket, a bird on Jason's shoulder and a puppy.
"Actually, yes, they did"; the wiki says Stash submitted it to the Adventure Society while the team discussed alternatives.
Special attack: Humphrey's racial ability evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon.
Voice (condensed): Shade is butler-formal; Stash barks like a dog while a lizard.
Pretty, with strawberry-blonde hair, a button nose and light skin, "startlingly cute" and clearly unhappy when freed from her cage.
Physically small but "prodigiously strong": she hauls the standing stones into place in Book 7.
A lecturer by habit: whenever she is not pointing out something specific, she is explaining.
She keeps her friends close: in Book 5, away from Gary, she says "I miss Gary".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Essences: Earth, Fire and Potent, which form the Volcano confluence; she explains this herself in Book 1.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Abilities: lava cannon (the Book 1 chapter title is "I Want a Lava Cannon"), a magma golem, lava streams and fire orbs, obsidian domes, shards and columns, and obsidian armour.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Ritual magic: she adjusts circles for ambient magic and builds the infrastructure of Asano Village and the Grid repairs.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Aura teaching: perception and memory games, meditation and aura control.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rank: silver in Book 4 or 5; in Book 12 she is offered the choice of becoming a Voice of the Will or a Defier of the Will; she accepts and becomes the Defier, immortal and "still a step or two from gold".
Daughter of Amelia and William Hurin of Vitesse; a member of the Burning Violet guild.
Book 1: rescued with Rufus and Gary from the cult; dies covering civilians in the desert astral-space ambush ("Farrah died covering those people").

Book 4: Jason finds that she is alive in his world, held captive by the Network's Lyon branch; the Reaper let her go in a negotiation with the World-Phoenix, which was worried that Jason would let Earth die (captive of Barbou and the EOA; the Reaper's negotiation is from the notes, Book 10). Jason rescues her.
Books 5-6: builds the family compound's infrastructure and the Grid repairs, helps destroy a vampire hub, leaves Earth with Jason; of her captor Adrien Barbou she says "Barbou belongs to me".
Books 7-9: settles in Rimaros; co-builds the Sky Link Network with Travis Noble (: "the years we worked together, building the Sky Link Network").
Voice (condensed): A lecturer who turns blunt when angry. Cues: "Barbou belongs to me".
Looks a lot like Rufus: tall, dark and muscular, but with hair worn in colourful beads that trail down to his shoulders in chains.
First seen as a lifelike water-link image.
and "Is it just me, or is this messenger a little bit odd?".
Practical about interrogation: "it's not easy to get a gold-ranker to talk. We can all hold up to a lot of pain".
Deflates when his son is surly: "That's fine!... Understood, son".
Wary of suspicious allies: "If the messengers have people that can go down there... what do they need us for?".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Gold rank with fire powers; his ash cloud carries him and Arabelle and his sword glows yellow-white like molten steel.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He flies a flame-trailing airship down from the sky.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Aura control is among the best Jason had sensed at gold rank.
Old team: Emir, Gabriel, Arabelle and Callum; they stopped adventuring while raising their son, and Gabriel started teaching at the academy.
Danielle Geller investigates Jason at his request.
Book 1-2: image on the water link; at Farrah's wake; jokes about Emir's palace; the strike force.
Book 10: arrives and reunites with Rufus and Arabelle; the old team reforms minus Callum; the Cardinas expedition; defends the wall as the god's power pushes.
Arabelle: wife, field partner.
Rufus: son.
Emir, Callum: old teammates; Callum was swapped out.
By seventeen she was "astoundingly beautiful"; later "basically Helen of Troy".
Olive skin, chocolate hair and graceful poise, "dangerous beauty".
Knowledge priests wear robes "not unlike the ones Jason preferred" in lighter colours.
Stern and accusing: "Where did you learn to use your aura like a messenger?"; "You move like a messenger".
Does not rise to bait: she glowers but doesn't answer teasing.
Hostile to Jason: their dislike was a factor in ending her relationship with Humphrey.
Quiet when separated from her goddess: she is still getting used to the absence of Knowledge.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A silver-rank priestess of the Church of Knowledge.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Jason's spirit domain cuts her off from her goddess, which makes her look like she bit a lemon.
Introduces herself as "just an acolyte, not a full priestess".
Humphrey's girlfriend, until he breaks up with her in Book 2.
Knowledge assigns her to shadow Travis and later attach her to his and Farrah's project.
Book 1-2: clipboards and a crystal ball with Russell at the temple; Jason introduces her to Emir; Humphrey's break-up.
Book 7-9: the grown priestess; picked up with Arabelle and Carlos.
Book 10: the Knowledge party at the Emir meeting; Travis glances at her.
Book 12-13: Travis's wife; the kitchen scene; a cube leaves her chest into Knowledge's hand and she seizes.
Travis Noble: nervous around her at first; later her husband.
Humphrey: ex-boyfriend.
Jason: mutual friction; Jason enjoys baiting her.
Knowledge: her goddess.
Book 13 describes a cube leaving her chest into Knowledge's hand.
Some nine feet tall, a skeleton wrapped in a dark green cloak with glowing red eyes, built from the skeletons of a dozen monsters.
The robe's drape hides what form the body takes.
Cold and strategic: he leaves the mindless hordes clawing at the wall until defences break.
Resentful of Death's interference: Death drives back the territory Undeath claimed.
Cautious in command: he directs his undead "with care and subtlety" so failed commands hide his purpose.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Higher-order undead leader; priests of Undeath range from ordinary essence users to undead mockeries, including vampires commanding ghoul armies and liches.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He designates a priest to control the avatar while he handles Asano.
Leader of the priests of Undeath; most who knew his nature are already slain and turned into his puppets or parts of his body.
Book 10: Death intervenes against his territory; introduces himself as "Garth Larosse, High Priest of Undeath".
Book 11: finds the avatar and regains the power to raise revenants; tries to swarm Asano with undead; tells a subordinate priestess he made "new allies".
Death: his god's nemesis.
Jason: his opponent, who answers him flippantly.
A huge "lion man" whose voice is growly by default; so large "he made bodybuilders look small".
The notes call him a leonid with a lion head.
As a demigod he is a vision of physical might, wreathed in divine power; almost a year later he is a haggard, skeletal figure who hobbles or is carried in a floating chair.
His characteristic line when facing death: "I don't want to be a ghost, rattling around in a hole".
Farrah describes him as "as much a craftsman as an adventurer" and "around the bottom of guild level".
Dominion tells him "That is where monarchs come from... I'll be keeping an eye on you, Gareth Xandier".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Summon: a foundry golem, a roughly three-metre black-iron figure with a molten mouth that drips molten metal.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Equipment: conjured full-body dark-steel plate armour; the notes add a hammer and shield and the runes.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Smithing: he forges Dread Salvation; he reforges it with his mentor Virid Martine as Hegemon's Will.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rank: bronze at the start; "almost silver" by Book 3; silver after using a core.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Demigod: Hero's power gives him divine strength; he says "I'm only a demigod".
A friend of Rufus and Farrah, and a Vitesse adventurer.
In Book 6 he meets the gold-rank smith Virid Martine, who becomes his master.
Book 11: refuses Jason's offer to bind his power to the natural array; dies; Hero decides to sanction himself (Gwydion tells Gary).
Book 12: Gary Sharpton appears: a young leonid who tinkers with a rune puzzle cube and travels aboard a saucer craft with Anna and Rufus.
Book 13: Jason tells the new Gary, "The gift was from my friend Gary. And the gift he gave us was you... He isn't you. And you aren't him." The Reaper "just passed it on".
Voice (condensed): Deep, growling and plain-spoken. Cues: "rattling around in a hole".
A bushy-bearded man rubbing his beard unhappily after a shower in a Network facility.
As Elizabeth's blood slave he looks "much as he had in life, but with blood-red sclera and swarthier skin".
Gruff, bellowing and friendly to those who are kind to him: "You're alright, Cleary... My last handler would have thrown me the chicken like I was a monster in a pit. Most people are scared of me".
Pugnacious: "I don't mind kicking their asses back and forth a little"; he is annoyed by being managed and "not entirely at peace" with joining Jason's push.
Cynical about his handlers: category fours "were beholden to whoever could provide the coins to keep them alive", and a handler is easier to replace.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Essences: might, potent and vast, producing the onslaught confluence; the potent essence is rare, the vast essence "so unheard of" the Network checked records hundreds of years old.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts

Dissatisfied: she looks Jason up and down before going back downstairs.

The agreement with the World-Phoenix ends when the bridge is complete.

Dustin sits beside him with their teams around them.

Powers: his body takes on the colour of the desert stone, flesh transmuting into living rock, and he conjures a huge stone shield at the front of a stone-raft run.
Two wall abilities spend him: "That's both my wall abilities. I won't have them again for a while".
Elemental pair: he shields his team with earth powers while Dustin is clad in ice armour; Humphrey notes that Rick's team has Kettering where "we have Hudson".
Down: Humphrey smashes him after a switch-teleport with Beth leaves him prone, and Hudson is soon "scrambling on the ground and conjuring shield after shield for Humphrey to smash through".
Reaper trial: in the astral city he stays quiet while Beth plans; his earth powers are the team's most prominent.
He receives a vine-looped wrist band that adds effects to his earth conjuration. He appears in the party contact list.
Tall, broad-shouldered and handsome; sixteen or seventeen in Book 1.
Rick Geller, a family member, shares his tall, broad-shouldered build.

Formal in a crisis: in Book 3, facing the Builder's forces, he announces "My name is Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller. My family have been adventurers for sixteen generations. We aren't alchemists or weaponsmiths on the side... For hundreds of years we have done one thing, and one thing only: protect our world from people like you".
Shy in personal matters: when Jason asks in front of his mother whether he has spoken to Gabrielle, he turns white and shakes his head.
Moral voice: in Book 1 he confronts Jason about the cruelty of the mirage-arena ambush.
He later advises against elaborate plans: "We tried that fifteen years ago and we only got from Rimaros to Yaresh".

Easy-going at home: dressed like it was laundry day with Hiro and Erika at the family mansion.

Trusts Jason: "I've known Jason since he was twelve years old".

Moved out of the family house after their daughter did.

Emi: daughter.

Rufus: walks with him over Emi's training.

Admiring: "my essences are dark, blood and omen, with a doom confluence" because he followed Jason's exploits.
Honest in pain: he says his wife's life "doesn't have room for me anymore".
Regretful: he turned to monster cores out of fear and trauma, then came to regret it.

claim: Essences dark, blood and omen forming a doom confluence.

claim: Stealthy scout in Book 5, a poor fit for the combat team.

Akari: his wife.
Koya and the Tiwari elders: his father and uncles.

His Book 13 marriage breakdown is his own choice, framed as a gift to Akari's sword path.

First impression: a "tall, beautiful woman" with long legs, whose addition to Garth's group left him "almost sad to have given up his flesh"; "capable and intelligent, eager and quick to learn", the opposite of another priest he was forced to bring.
Dress: an elegant combat robe and heavy boots.
Garth's feelings: Garth feels a longing for her despite his unliving body but never acts on it, "not allowing himself such a lack of discipline".
Knowledge of Hero: she says she has "never seen anyone who has drunk from the Cup of Heroes" and reads it as Hero's miracle at the brink of defeat.
Before the god: she and Garth drop to their knees when Undeath appears as a living man in black robes with empty sockets and a crimson spark, and she bows to Undeath and then Garth.
In battle: she silences a skeleton's communication magic, watches the divine giants clash and points out that crushing the undead at the wall will cost time to replenish.
Perception: she warns "He's not bluffing, High Priest... The world feels wrong, somehow. Like standing on a frozen lake as the ice starts to crack".
Intelligence work: she extracts what she can about Asano from prisoners, who say his aura is like a gold-ranker's in strength and coverage.
Negotiation with Boris: in the desert she tells Boris "You are not in a position to negotiate" and "You're bluffing... You want Asano dead and he knows it".
Spotting the enemy: she is the first to point out two strange floating vehicles speeding across the desert.

Death: "One of the final priests to die was Jameela, Garth's most trusted subordinate. She refused to go down easy... her beauty destroyed by Taika's fists and her unwillingness to accept that her cause was lost".
Seven feet tall, "diminutive for his kind", with wings; his clothes are not the loose toga style of messengers.
His avatar's wings are completely absorbed into his body.
Vain and sharp when crossed: he snarls at defiant messengers that they directly defied the Council of Kings.
Dismissive of lesser threats: Farrah says "Muskar might not think McKean is dangerous".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rules a sleek dimension ship that looks out of place on Pallimustus.

claim: Says when the task is complete "the price is paid. Zithis Carrow Vayel will have fulfilled his debt to us".
One of the Council of Kings.
Book 10: observes Erigo's clothing.
Book 12: berates messengers; his ship arrives.
Book 13: meets Jason.
Zithis Carrow Vayel: a debtor to the kings.
Jason: Jason says Muskar sees danger only for those he cares about, namely Jason himself.
On arrival: he wakes bald and naked in a hedge maze.

Seeing himself later, he notes his Japanese facial features, inherited from his father, look even sharper than usual, his face is gaunt, and his bald head and absent eyebrows make him look "manic and unhinged". His skin is pale and taut.
Why: his body ceased to exist in the deep astral; his soul, being magical, was given a new body in the way a summoned familiar is (Clive).
At gold his "strange, nebulous eyes" draw attention, though they return to the dark eyes he had at iron when he meets Zara.
Clothing: from Book 3 he buys a Vitesse-style wardrobe from the tailor Gilbert Bertinelli.
He tells the Builder it and Knowledge "should get together and play Mario Kart"; he compares a projected face to Emperor Palpatine. He says "G'day" and "mate".
Self-deprecation: "I'm only twenty-three but I've been pretty efficient about squandering my opportunities".
He does not celebrate his birthday, which falls on 1 April: "It's not a celebratory time. I never liked my birthday anyway".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: His attributes are bound as Power (Blood), Speed (Dark), Spirit (Doom) and Recovery (the fourth essence).

Way of the Reaper martial arts.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Titles: Godless Prophet, Spirit Warrior, Indomitable, Giant Slayer, Reality Hegemon, Keeper of the Cycle.
Home: Casselton Beach on the Mid North Coast of New South Wales.

His father Ken is a landscape architect; his mother Cheryl comes from a large family of mostly rural people; his older sister Erika and her husband Ian live nearby with their daughter Emi; his brother Kaito and Kaito's wife Amy live next door to his parents' house.
His uncles are Hiro, the black sheep with minor involvement in organised crime, and Shiro, the favourite.

Before Pallimustus: "a brief stint at university" studying political science, then Melbourne "the last couple of years", seeing little of his family apart from his sister's household (Book 1, Ch52 says only that he had little contact with his family after they fell out), where he is "the cheapest childcare in town".
He worked as an assistant manager at a retail bulk office supplier.
Birthday: 1 April.
Arrival: pulled from his bed in late November by Landemere Vane's failed summoning.
Books 7-9 (level 2): returns to Pallimustus as the great surge begins; the One Day War; becomes an astral king; the Battle of Yaresh; takes in messengers.
Books 12-13 (level 3): a gold-rank "prime avatar of an astral nexus" who returns to Earth in 2038.

Mentors and early friends: Rufus, Gary and Farrah; Rufus runs his field assessment and guides his first meditation; Farrah trains his perception and aura projection with memory games and other exercises.
Level 2: he has died four times by Book 6 (the Church of Death's certificate; the card in); he is an astral king.
Level 3: his transformation into a prime avatar of an astral nexus.
Knowledge has been using him as a key part of her plan to invade Earth for half a millennium (the plan's origin).

At the end of Book 13 Umber's ritual is designed to bind his consciousness into the prime avatar, and Jason walks to the standing stones knowingly, promising Knowledge "the next time we meet, Goddess, will be the day you die".
Cue: "Do I have to pay a wizard to identify items?".
Not described in the lines read; she checks a pocket watch.

Suspicious of politics: the roster is like "a mad alchemist throwing volatile ingredients in a pot".
Practical: she plans for the worst and does not slow when she senses the clearing's oddity.

Not described in detail in the lines read; on a mission he puts away his coat and pulls out another one "covered in pockets".
Idealist: "If I can make alchemical products affordable to everyone, not only can it help a huge number of people, but it will open up huge new markets".
Honest about himself: technically an adventurer, he is "the first to admit he rarely went on adventures"; his "true calling was alchemy".
Gentle: he tells Jason "You have a good day" to a guard and nurses patients with Healer priests.
Passionate teacher: "He lit up when talking about his alchemy, and his passion for helping people was wildly appealing".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Alchemy: he brews potions and elixirs from materials he gathers in towns and villages and runs an alchemy lab and medical clinic, the Broad Street Clinic.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Miracle potion: his facility produces the first batch of lesser miracle potions, a thank-you to Jason who funded it.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: In a fight: floating clear orbs and materials from his pockets and belts in the Reaper trials and quick to throw enemies overboard on a skyship.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Teaching: in Book 11 he lectures a group of students on a stage in a hazy hall.
Member of the Adventure Society and the Alchemist Association.
The Healer makes his clinic a sanctuary and the church backs him; "The Church of the Healer gave him a mandate and funding to spread his methods around the world".
Book 1-3: he finds Jason, patches him up and offers a clinic (Book 1, Ch35); treats Sophie; the Healer visit (Book 1, Ch95).
Book 5-6: the Healer's mandate; Belinda contacts him through a water link.
Book 7: he is on the skyship to Vitesse with Gary and the team and is summoned away by the Church of the Healer.
Book 11-13: he teaches and joins the healers' discussions on Earth.
Belinda: her boyfriend, and the one who sees her cry in the classroom.
Jason: first friend; "Jory is such a good friend to you".
Neil and the Healer's people: they work together at the clinic.
The Healer's direct support is one reason the clinic is protected.
Weary and proud: he reflects that the universe-city of Interstice is "for most practical purposes, the centre of the cosmos".
Self-aware: arrogance cost him opportunities.
Cautious: he watches Jason float towards him, noting the impenetrable aura and the scars probably not affectations.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Gold rank; his vessel is a rarity, only gold rank, which suits certain jobs.
Born in a feeder realm, he fell short of Interstice at gold rank and ended up serving "a self-styled cosmic admiral" who was a pirate lord.
Book 12: sits on his bridge; hosted on Earth by Noriko, who visits daily; meets Jason.
Noriko Asano: his host on Earth.
Jason: wary of his power.
Jason's face is more angular than his brother's; Kaito has a "signature easy-going smile" that Jason spent years learning to copy.
At a party he wears a pale suit and pastel shirt.
Jason's resemblance to him grows with each rank, until Jason stops begrudging it after Kaito's death.
Socially adroit: Jason says he never had "Kaito's skill for getting along".
The favourite: their parents "got Kaito, so they were willing to put up with me".
Casual: he greets the family meeting with "G'day... We're arrived for the mysterious family meeting".
Dry on pop culture: his knowledge of classic pop culture "appeared to begin and end with Miami Vice".
Warm with his children: he leads Hana by the hand and carries Jace.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: After Jason's return he joins the Network-defector combat team with Asya and Greg.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He flies drones to sweep the ruins of a town and owns the helicopter Jason and Akari ride in.
A year older than Jason; the "well-received original" at school, so Jason felt like "a disappointing rehash".
He and Amy bought her parents' house next door to Jason's family.
He and Amy's relationship caused the fallout that left Jason dropping out of university; Jason did not want details.
Book 4: Jason sees his contact appear on the interface and sees the home he shares with Amy; Erika and Kaito discuss Amy and Jason; the family reunion; the helicopter check with Erika.
Book 5: the strike team and helicopter crew; dies in Berlin with Asya and Greg; Jason at the funeral: "died for something that truly matters. To give his children a future".
Later: Amy and the girls are Book 13 family; his death is the grief behind Emi's uncle.
Jason: brother; Jason says Kaito made his own choice to stand up for his world and that Amy knows it.
Amy: wife, with daughters Hana and Jace.
Erika: sister who keeps the family together.
Hiro: his uncle, who spoke Japanese with his mother behind their father's back.
His death is why Amy's children grow up without a father "because he followed me".
Hot-headed: Korinne tells her "still-angry team member" to let go of a quarrel, "You don't want to make an enemy of the next Amos Pensinata".
History with Jason: he first met Jason "at a bad time", at the height of Jason's volatility.
They worked together on the underwater rescue under Korinne, after which Kalif "wanted nothing more to do with Asano" and was relieved he would leave Rimaros.
Agreeing to go: "Of course we go. That doesn't mean we go blindly, and you know that Asano and I have bad blood". He eventually shakes Jason's hand.
Team Storm Shredder: he names the team to Jason and thinks being watched by Jason's guard dog is "unsettling. Makes it hard to relax".
Driving: left behind to drive the team's new vehicle, he is "starting to get a handle on it" and has hit few other craft.
Vitesse approach: he sums up Humphrey's idea as "the Vitesse approach, but scaled up".
Complaints: he grumbles that his team will work for two weeks while Jason is "knocking boots with the cute pink-haired woman".
Opinions on afflictions: he says of area specialists, "No iron-rank monster is tough enough to make afflictions worthwhile".
Cardinas: in the siege of Cardinas he asks "There's ten of us. How many undead are out there?" and "Shouldn't we have brought more people?".
In Book 11 he commands silver-rankers with the cult and brighthearts.
Wanting to rest: after the surge he and others argue they should "loosen up and enjoy what we've earned".
Not described beyond a House Irios crest on his arm.
Shaken: his movements are "oddly stumbling" and he freezes when he sees Jason.
Eager to please: shocked when Jason names himself the dead man.
Nervous: his friends pick up on his nervousness.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A peak-level bronze-ranker, close to silver like his three young friends.
Zara's intended match was "a member of the Irios family".
Vesper engineered Jason's meeting with him for political reasons, and Jason's overture to the family was not taken up.
Book 7: meets Jason at the tailor shop and walks the street with him.
Book 12: an adventurer now; Orin is the only one on his team to hit gold so far.
Jason: unwilling companion.
Orin Pensinata: teammate.
Solid and reliable: "Compared to Danielle, her husband, Keith, was more akin to their son: a solid and reliable counterpoint to her domineering charms".
Father of Henrietta, who takes her role as Humphrey's older sister seriously.
Book 2: with the Geller family at the gathering.
Book 12: arrives at Jason's reunion with Danielle.
Danielle Geller: wife.
Humphrey and Henrietta: son and daughter.
Not described in detail in the lines read; he brushes his fingers over his son's scars.
Convert's zeal: "Proving there is no zealot like a convert, Ken was all about the Australian lifestyle, from pub rock to footy matches and weekend barbecues".
Warm and undemanding: Jason finds "his father's warm and undemanding support was a balm".
Emotional: he goes still, then "exploded forward" to hug Jason.
Straightforward: he asks whether Jason has gone "a little far" with his domain.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Has the skirmish confluence, which suits running battles; many powers trip up the enemy.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A landscape architect.
Born in Japan, raised in Australia from a very young age.
The middle brother: Shiro was the favourite, Hiro the disappointment, "your father laid low in the middle".
Book 4: the reunion; plays with his granddaughters on the cloud house; marches into the portal.
Book 5: guides Jason through the compound with Hiro and Emi.
Book 7: sits in the front row with the team and Gary; his skirmish confluence helps hold off constructs round the skimmer.
Book 13: walks with Jason through a garden park.
Jason: son.
Hiro and Shiro: brothers.
Kaito: his other son.
Jason guesses she is about thirty, athletic, with short brown hair.
Analytical: Anna places a lot of trust in her analytical abilities.
Sceptical: in Book 11 she doubts Jason's plans while Yumi has faith.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Formal title: Assistant to the Director of Operations, Sydney branch.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Investigates a hospital event up the coast.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Jason saves her life with one of Shade's bodies forming a parachute.
She leads the Network defectors' intake and sits on calls with the Sydney branch.
After the Network's Australian branch breaks up, Yumi hires her for her administrative skill.
Book 4: Anna's assistant; parachute rescue.
Book 5: tells Jason's side "We've got a bunch of people coming in from the EOA looking to defect".
Book 11: Yumi's hire.
Book 12: chief of staff to the clan matriarch; drives Anna through Saint-Étienne.
Anna Tilden: her director.
Yumi Asano: her new principal.
Unctuous and without limits: he ushers in guests.
Merciless: he argues that a man who can defy the star seed's power cannot be left alive.
Exploitative: in Book 8 he is described as dangerous for how he wormed into corners, exploiting and betraying those he works with.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Not given a rank in the lines read; Laront says his real name isn't Laurent, he "chose that to annoy me".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He uses a star seed for the cult.
"Of the bronze rankers under Silva, Killian was the unquestionable leader" and he runs the secret site.
He had worked behind the scenes to plunder the Silva family while Jason distracted Silva.
Book 2: Silva calls for him.
Book 3: waits in Silva's lounge; Jason's team hunts him for days; he leaves the city on a ship loaded with Silva's holdings.
Book 9: Havi plans to deliver him but he captures Havi first; Jason's team takes and chains him in a ritual array.
Book 10: Jason can only guess at his fate.
Cole Silva: employer he betrays.
Jason: enemy.
Open question: where he is held after Book 9 and whether he escapes; Jason only guesses he is "in a Magic Society basement somewhere".
In Book 1 a statue is replaced by a woman with colourful clothes and Mediterranean features, beautiful yet "detached and untouchable", not holding the statue's book.
She knows everything anyone in her world knows, including Jason, so she knows Mario Kart shortcuts.
A melodious voice behind Jason says "Such a shame. I was hoping to be your first".

The Book 13 briefing says she has been preparing to invade Earth for half a millennium and used Jason; that she promised the messengers' leader a chance to invade Pallimustus and claim Purity's relic; and that around a third of the priests and priestesses of Knowledge are her spies.
She removes the divine essence of Gabrielle Pellin, a cube leaving Gabrielle's chest into her hand.
Jason's last word to her: "The next time we meet, Goddess, will be the day you die".
Jason; Gabrielle Pellin; Purity and Disguise; the Church of Knowledge (one of the churches that contribute funding to the MRA).
Voice (condensed): Detached and untouchable in manner. Cue:.
Not described in detail in the lines read; in Book 11 she has "dead eyes" until she finds Rosa.
Efficient: she relays orders swiftly, her efficiency "only enhanced by Jason's communication power".
Loyal: "he's our asshole, and we don't turn on our own assholes".
Peacemaker: "Let it go, Kalif... You don't want to make an enemy of the next Amos Pensinata".
Guarded then curious: she visits Jason's cabin guarded about his methods and takes a slice of baked goods thoughtfully.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Leader of a silver-rank guild team of six; they were star performers, clearing enemies faster than the other teams, with two high-damage members and the rest built around them.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Her team "operated alone through most of the surge".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She feels Jason's aura as "the cold anger of an icy hell".
Leader of Orin and Kalif's team, who coordinated the underwater complex rescue.
Her team eschewed the yacht for their own vehicle during travel.
Book 7: the mixed-force expedition.
Book 8: one of Shade's four intact bodies stays with her at the mining facility.
Book 9: asks Jason to train the team (Book 9, Ch25); travels in convoy; Zara joins the team vehicle.
Book 10: "Storm Shredder's leader" at the breach; in Jason's group meeting.
Book 11: stalked by a priest, finds Jetta dead and meets Rosa.
Rosa, Orin, Kalif, Zara: team members.
Jetta: a friend, dead as a puppet.
Jason: she guesses he will lecture on Rimaros-style versus Vitesse-style adventuring.
Book 11 shows her stalked and traumatised during the Undeath siege.
His mother looks to be in her early thirties "no older than her son Landemere"; no other description appears in the lines read.
Ambitious and out of his depth: Dougall says Landemere summoned "one of them entities from beyond the void".
Traditional family: his mother says "this is my manor, my family, and we do things the traditional way".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Clive explains that Landemere's summoning went wrong, possibly because he reached beyond his ability or a dimensional event interfered.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He was holding more than a thousand coins when killed.
His mother, who looks no older than her son, is among the cultists who greet Jason.
The Vane family treats the summoning as a family matter: "This is my manor, my family".
Familiar: Jason's first encounter with a native creature was Vane's familiar, which tried to avenge him and fell victim to aging masonry.
Book 1: the summoning in the Vane basement; Jason reflects on the "very first person Jason met" and first killed.
Book 2: Clive regrets losing his notes.
Book 4-7: the first kill shakes Jason; Clive's later explanation.
Cressida Vane: his mother, who calls him "poor Landemere".
Jason: accidental killer.
Clive says random dimensional events connecting worlds are rare but more frequent because of the link between the worlds.
Not described in the lines read; sweat drips off her in the monitoring room in the middle of the night.
Disillusioned: "her excitement had been well and truly killed off".
Composed: she pinches the bridge of her nose, breathes out and schools her expression.
Dry: Anna says she will "play this objectively".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A core user and not a fighter.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She directs operations from the command-and-control room, the bunker's most restricted zone.
Excited to join the program out of university, then a year in the monitoring room drained that.
Worked there for "almost her entire adult life".
Her deputy Barry is mayor of the artefact city.
Book 11: monitoring room.
Book 12: Jason's arrival and the pirate battle.
Book 13: occupies the former mayoral residence.
Barry: her deputy.
Anna: counterpart.
Diplomatic: she hopes for a "more modest collaboration in the future".
Adaptive: one of the few with political experience in both worlds.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver rank in Books 4-6; Jason uses her as a test subject for refining his control of the System.
Daughter of Li Ning; her gold-rank uncle is Li Chen.
Has lived in Boko for years.
Book 4: meets Jason in a business resort lobby.
Book 6: appears beside the dome and portal with two Chinese gold-rankers.
Book 12: Jason finds her in Boko more than fifteen years after they last met; she stays near him during Boko's destruction.
Book 13: meets the international committee or the Chinese delegation with Li Chen.
Li Ning and Li Chen: father and uncle.
Jason: acquaintance and test subject.
Tall (her eldest daughter has "Liara's height") and gold-rank fast, flitting through streets unnoticed.
Brisk and official: she is working without rest as the city fills with adventurers to be filtered for cultists.
Wary of politics: she "disdained" the politics she "could never seem to escape".
Self-critical but resolute: after Gibson Amouz's capture she "allowed shame to flash over her expression before schooling it"; she stands up to his father, "Get out of my office, Lord Amouz".
Protective: "Don't even think about it", she tells Zareen of Jason.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rank: a gold-ranker, leader of the Book 8 expedition with her former teammate Jana Costi as second.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Investigator: her search for the cult's portal users is a process of elimination through portal schedules, market tracking and field reports.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Not for rescues: she understands why she was told not to take part personally in the mining-complex rescue: "Her abilities were ill-suited to the task and her emotional investment would not be an asset".

Royal branch: "from one of the more remote branches of the royal family", not close enough to be called a princess, but entitled to a home on the royal sky island and to take part in the contests for the throne in her youth.
Career: "a long and prestigious career in Adventure Society special operations".
Marriage: in her youth she married a local lordling, Baseph, "to secure royal influence"; they live largely separate lives but remain friends. Baseph is born into House Amouz.
Book 7: she has been "working without rest" as adventurers are filtered for potential cultists; Jason is told "Pelli and Liara Rimaros will be your contact points".
She and Keel watch Jason and Farrah through a seeing stone, and takes Jason to a private meeting room in the administration building.
Book 8: she leads the expedition on the Builder complex, faces Lord Amouz, re-collates her files and, assigned to handle Jason for the royal family, meets him with an agenda rather than gratitude.
Book 9: she tells Jason's group not to roam like a pack, sits with him at the confrontation and goes to the cloud house.
Book 12-13: she visits Jason's island for a barbecue with her husband and family; her daughter Zareen serves in the delegation to Earth.
Baseph and the children: Baseph, Dara, Zareen and Joseph; see Baseph_and_the_Rimaros_Children.md and Zareen_Rimaros.md.
Amouz family: Cassin Amouz is her husband's family; she calls him "Uncle Cassin" when angry.
Trenchant Moore: stands beside her in the royal guard crisis.
Jason: she keeps him on a short leash for the crown but with warmth.
A fair-skinned blonde woman, bronze rank in Book 3.
Protective: she shields Clive from Lady Ajus and stalls Lady Ajus without asking what he was doing.
Deferential to research: she later studies the notes he left.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Vice-Dean of the astral magic research department in Rakesh; Vice Chancellor of the Magic Research Association by Book 12.
She introduces herself as a researcher assigned to the Adventure Society's Continental Council when recruiting Jason's team's help against the Builder cult.
She recruited Clive out of Greenstone; Clive thinks she was misled too.
Book 3: "My name is Lorelei Grantham and I'm a researcher assigned to work with the Adventure Society's Continental Council".
Book 6: Rakesh, Clive's recruitment and escape.
Book 12-13: brings researchers to Earth with the expedition; works with Clive on the vampire laboratory; leads Clive out of a lab by the arm; full-time staff at Jason's school.
Clive: partner.

Last of the council: the brighthearts had a ruling council of nine, "three elected from the gold-rankers, three from the normal-rankers and three from the guilds"; only Lorenn remains, the others "having sacrificed everything to keep the rest of us alive". She is addressed as Councilwoman.
Appearance: an ash aspect, with "smoky greys" that she thinks far less appealing than the forge-glow of her fire-aspect friend Marla.

War room: she stands alone in the old council chamber, now a war room, before a live model of the city drawn from the natural array and mostly covered in the sickly green of the elemental messengers' tree.
Marla: Marla urges evacuating a number of people they can feed; Lorenn breaks down, then accepts the comfort.
Beaufort: she keeps the alliance with the Builder cult's commander despite loathing the cultists, "Our alliance stands".
Later she tells the adventurers that accepting them "was not an easy choice" because "we are not warriors".
Suspicion of the surface: she cannot bring herself to be happy at the prospect of more surface invaders.
Meeting the adventurers: she says "I am Lorenn... You, as I understand it, are Beaufort's enemies" and "So long as you can do something about the elemental messengers, I don't care what you are".
Her people's story: almost all the brighthearts died in three cycles of the messenger war, and the bodies rose; she says "We, so far as I know, are all the brighthearts that exist".
Accepting the loss of home: "Losing the array is a blow our people may not recover from... if we are going to last as a people, we need to leave our home behind".
Jason's offer: she doubts "a silver-ranker saving us all", and decides that "if we're choosing between no chance of survival and betting everything on a stranger, that's not a choice at all".
She asks what happens to the people in his soul realm if he dies.
Crossing over: she has never used a portal; she walks through with Jason as the soul realm forms chambers for her people, and fresh food appears.
The new realm: after her trip into it she tells Jason it is closer to the old array without its instability.

Book 11: she hands her territories to Jason, whose brand replaces hers; she objects to putting aside a weapon without discussion, joins the alliance council and urges striking once the enemy messengers are destroyed.
She objects to a statue of the tree that "will loom over us, every day".
She finds the new subterranean city "not the home she'd lost" but hopes it becomes home.
Fire aspect: "Lorus, a fire-aspect brightheart whose messengers were likewise possessed of flame powers", each shrouded in steam as they evaporated the rain.
Aggressive: he pushes aggressively "in spite of casualties" while Durrum is more conservative, and he has no intention of stopping his offensive against the cult.
Betrayal charge: Durrum shouts "Are you betraying us?" and "You're killing us".
Defiance of Neil: the brighthearts around him yell that they would never let the undead go, and Lorus grandstands once Neil has left the cage.
His case: "I will not hand over my power on their say-so. Those cultist abominations invaded our city. They were the beginning of the end for our entire people!".
Power grab: "Then give the territories to me. Once everyone actually obeys, I will make us stronger as we go... Our messengers are stronger than theirs".

Neil's read: Neil gambles that Lorus is "a volatile mix of ambition, impatience and pride, with an unearned sense of entitlement", and says his actions show he likes "having command of all these messengers".
Losing support: Lorus looks around and finds even his followers will not meet his eyes, "their faces showing disgust, disdain or disappointment".
Last appeal: "Durrum. Don't let this outsider lead you to disaster. Without enough messengers...".
Durrum answers that he has never been content with what he has.
Outcome: Durrum accepts Lorus's territory.
An uncommonly muscular elf who "would not look out of place in the fighting pits himself", in expensive clothes.
Smug and indulgent: he arrives at his viewing room "with a contented sigh".
Handsy: he strokes his fingers over a face in the viewing window.
Quick to blame: his fury threatens to erupt when pressed.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Danielle outpaces him in a duel and cuts him.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: His handling of a star seed for the Church of Purity comes under scrutiny.
"Banished to Greenstone for previous improprieties"; he is not a member of the local elf community.
His deputy Pochard maintains the city campus so he can use the Fortress as his office.
Book 1: the fighting pits viewing rooms (Book 1, Ch42-43).
Book 2: Clive's racks discussion.
Book 3: held in the prison tower.
Book 9: the kidnapping traced to him and Cole Silva.
Pochard Finn: deputy and friend.
Cole Silva: co-conspirator.
Danielle Geller: opponent.
A massive leonid carrying a huge axe.
Cheerful and blunt: "an adventurer and the man the Adventure Society saw fit to deploy to your city".
Wry: he wonders if a familiar picked Team Biscuit's name.
Confrontational: "I was warned that you might give me trouble" to Gormanston Bynes.
Accommodating to Jason: which unsettles Jason's allies.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: "A high-level agent of the Adventure Society's continental council, Marcus was a troubleshooter and enforcer".
His arrival and the support he wins from figures such as Gormanston leave the aristocrats scattered.
Book 10: Yaresh arrival; Bynes; aristocrats scattered; Cardinas planning.
Book 12: dispatched to Yaresh again on hearing of Jason's return.
Gormanston Bynes: opponent turned supporter.
Jason: ally.
Nine-foot messenger with wings; he and Tera wear synthetic leather armour rather than the diaphanous clothes messengers favour.
Arrogant, then honest: confident in his superiority over "servant races", but he learns that "when pushed, even the least of sapient species would push back".
Respects craft: he appreciates "a power used well over one that was mindlessly strong" and wants to face Humphrey in battle.
Disaffected from the Voice: he hates Jes Fin Kaal and avoids politics.
Quietly longing for freedom: freedom from astral kings "was what he had always hoped for and never believed possible".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Gold-rank commander; he blocks a projectile with his wing without effort.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He spent far longer than Tera's lifetime working free of the conditioning every messenger goes through.
Messengers' soul spaces are blank concrete utilitarian landscapes; Marek compares them with Jali's vibrant realm.

Book 9: leads the breach force; worries as Humphrey plunges into the monster torrent; Schaat sees him as a potential rival; recognises Jason as Asano; sits with Payan Nior Roel and pauses at Tera's fate.
Book 10: waits in Jason's kingdom near the cocoon dome; fears the leonid prisoner; Jason says "Your kind are easy to hate"; leads the messenger prisoners.
Tera Jun Casta: young messenger whose identity rests on the indoctrination; Marek sits beside her with concern.
Jason: his captor; Marek senses Jason looks "for reasons not to kill them".
Jes Fin Kaal: he hates the Voice.
Humphrey: a respected enemy.
He notes that knowing messengers can survive without an astral king will be a revelation.
Not described in the lines read; she sips hot chocolate in a glass-walled chalet.
Controlling and secretive: she thinks she is running a tight operation.
Professional: she answers a call as "Finnegan".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She uses earth-shaping powers to create a basin at a rocky shore.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She runs video conferencing with feeds from Pakistan and a grid system.
The recently expelled director of the Zurich Network branch, fleeing with Elizabeth.
The leadership council kept the vampire programme contained at her insistence; her contacts with Elizabeth and McKean were critical.
Her backers called using Elizabeth the smart choice.
She worked directly with Elizabeth, "intimately" according to Remy.
Book 13: chalet introduction; flees with Elizabeth; council backing; Remy's account; storm shore; Jason talks to her and says he will hand her to the Network.
Elizabeth: her vampire partner.
Simon McKean: contact.
Jason: her captor.
Her programme with Elizabeth and McKean was kept contained at her insistence.
A fire aspect, dark-skinned, with skin markings, eyes and hair the yellow-orange of steel in a forge.
In Book 12 her hair and eyes glow like molten steel and she has a warrior's physique.
Comforting: she comforts Lorenn, the city's leader, when she breaks down.
Practical: she briefs Jason on the citadel's defences, the children in the growth chambers and the messengers' failed attempts to cross the death chamber.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Commander of the brightheart military; she commands the citadel's response when Gary drinks from the Cup of Heroes and coordinates reinforcements.
Leader of the brightheart military in Cardinas.
Book 10: Cardinas defence (Book 10, Ch72-73; Book 10, Ch88-89).
Book 11: the brightheart commander beside Beaufort of the Builder cult.
Book 12: leader of the brightheart military.
Lorenn: the city's leader whom she comforts.
Jason and Gary: allies in the defence.
White hair and dark skin; she wears white leather armour stained and torn from shielding the fort.
Fanatical and sharp: "sharp, fanatical and brainwashed" when Jason met her.
Clean habits: she likes showers and is "ever at the ready" in her marred armour.
Commanding: she silences her second with a gesture.
Softening later: after therapy with her daughter she is "less hostile and manipulative".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: An essence user responsible for a fort holding out without supplies.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A sword fighter fast enough to dance with Jason's blade.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Shackled, she still runs and hides through a cloud-stuff palace.
Faked her death twenty years before Book 6, using a wall panel in Marta Fries's house in Kurdansk.
Arabelle dates the story to "around a quarter of a century ago".
The Order of Redeeming Light is a creation of the god Disguise masquerading as Purity; its Flames of Redemption are a modification of lesser vampirism.
Book 7: she leads the enclave, wanting a captive to lure her daughter to Rimaros.
Book 8: leads the local forces; fights Jason; escapes briefly and is recaptured.
Book 9-10: locked in the cloud palace while they seek a cure; the mind-war of her fractured brainwashing; Jason pins her with his aura.
Book 13: she gives Jason a motherly smile.
Sophie: her daughter.
Arabelle: helps look after her.
Sendira: her second.
Jason: his team holds her captive; by Book 13 she gives him a motherly smile.
The more she fights the brainwashing, the more the taint fights back.
Past posting: he was stationed at Saint-Étienne "two decades and several ranks ago", before the Asano Clan took over.
Seen the horrors: he has seen "with his own eyes the power of the vampire lords and the land of horrors they had made" and believes the stories of Asano reclaiming his territory.
The EDJI: he had never thought it would happen and was there for the negotiations when China and Russia demanded more influence; the US almost derailed it over the spelling of "defense".
He does not approve of the troops calling it "edgy".
Doctrine: he commanded the Infantry Reimplementation Program, redefining infantry doctrine as augmented soldiers with magitech weapons returned infantry to the forefront.
Command: with his doctrine knowledge and experience fighting vampires, he is placed "in operational command of the EDJI's largest military action to date".

Observations of the base: he is met by a saluting EDJI lieutenant in a US Army-marked uniform; the tarmac holds augmented infantry and Cabal contingents, and he finds a "wild amount of diversity" in Asano Clan territory.
Hopes and fears: he hopes the unity will outlast the common enemy, and worries what awaits when the threat is dealt with.
Politics: he has no Network origins and has navigated Network and anti-Network factions his whole career.
Meeting Jason: he has met Jason several times, mostly in passing at political events.
In a meeting with Yumi he says "It was always my intention to pit you against McKean".
Candour: "Mr Asano, it's been many years since you first came back to Earth. Yes, a lot of people made less than ideal choices in those days".
He asks why Jason has spent a decade forging humanity's military into a single sword rather than going home, and why he has not told anyone about the specific threat.

Spokesperson: he is chosen as the spokesperson for the EDJI member states, "known as someone who could handle Jason without triggering some meeting-ending debacle", and enters in an informal EDJI service dress uniform with a briefcase.
Not described in the lines read; he looks "ready to snap if he got bad news".
Harried: he stumbles out of his chair and hurries around the table when Clive arrives.
Frank about orders: "This contract didn't come down through normal channels. It came down from on high".
Reputation-minded: "Reputation is everything in this town".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver rank "entirely from cores", with paper, knowledge, rune and scribe essences.
Senior administrator at the Vitesse Adventure Society.
Book 6: Clive's team visits his office.
Book 7: briefs Humphrey's team; prepares the Purity-stronghold strike force; supervises a mission with the temporary leader Kenneth; meets Jason's team at the outworlder arrival.
Book 12: hurries across the Vitesse campus after Jason's return and shares tea with Clive's assistant.
Humphrey and Clive: officials he briefs and warns.
Introduced as "the leader of Team Moon's Edge, Miriam Vance".
Moon's Edge is a team of six women, all gold rank, raised and supervised by Allayeth from early in their careers.
She is the expedition's Tactical Commander and tells Jason no when he wants to add his butterflies to a messy flying battle.
Her gold-rank senses read Jason's emotions through his aura.
She notices how Allayeth acts around Jason, questions him about astral kings and the goddess, and argues with him over command. Death addresses her by name.
She runs the withdrawal through the citadel tunnels as overall commander and sets the defensive perimeter.

In Book 11 she is the zone's co-commander with Jason, directs Moon's Edge to destroy the tree crystals and protects the non-combatants in Ramona's invisibility sphere when Amos Pensinata goes into the orb.
Her team "was the most powerful force on the battlefield other than the cloud buildings and the two divine entities".
Jason introduces her to Gordon, his avatar of doom.
A different Miriam, Miriam Coyle, heads a magitech weapons institute in Book 13.
A grinning man who meets Jason "grinning like a snake who found a nest full of baby mice".
When he drops the act he is stern, adjusting his tie and cuffs, "the grinning, languid man Jason had met was nowhere to be seen".
He is a gold-ranker, not an essence user, and "a bonded familiar, but your bond has been severed".
Jason tells Anna that "He was a magic spider. A familiar of the man you know as the network founder".
Amused and mocking: "You're a smart man, Mr Asano. More or less"; he calls Jason "a parade of delights".
Controlled: "He had long ago schooled himself out of dangerous curiosity and exploitable impatience".
Ruthless about outcomes: with the Grid down for months he says "A wide-scale collapse of civic and social infrastructure does not obviate our objectives" and "So long as we rule".
A manipulator of principles: "Be wary of your principles, Mr Asano. I might use them to be assured that you enter that astral space".
Paranoid and lonely: Barbou thinks he is "older and more powerful than anyone realises", not human, and "lonely".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Webs: he draws ritual circles in webbing that contain auras, sound, scent and magic.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He buries himself in a cocoon before the nuclear solar rockets, and digs out afterwards.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Magitech without theory: he developed magitech "with almost no knowledge of magical theory, drastically low ambient magic, and essentially zero technology", and was too paranoid to trust capable scientists; Audrey Blaine "was a buffer between North's ambitions and his paranoia".
A rune spider: "I was a rune spider, originally".
The Network founder was his essence user; "My essence user was blinded by faith... giving up power and prestige to lift up a bunch of savages", and the bond broke before the founder died.
Betrayal: Noreth sold out the founder to the early magic societies.
Centuries on Earth: Boris supplied him with spirit coins to survive as a gold-ranker but North never trusted him; had he trusted him, "North's core research might not have been such a mess".
The EOA: his organisation is named for his project of engineering people without essences; its leader "secretly being some kind of spider".
Book 5: the Cardinal's meetings and the shutdown plan. He takes Barbou from Mrs West's circle.
He meets Jason in the Builder's door space, tells him to absorb the door and says "It's about time you showed up".
Book 6: he stays near Jason through the transformation zone work.
He insists Jason will go into the astral space "whether I give you Barbou or not" and later dies killing Gerling.
Later books: his vault of EOA secrets goes to Jason and the clan uses his research.
Jason: sometimes ally, sometimes enemy; Jason "never trusted" him but believed his intentions were good.
Barbou: he calls him a quality subordinate and takes him after the Lyon plans fail.
Audrey Blaine: his own cardinal Mrs South, whom the cardinals murder for refusing the plan.
Gerling: "You took my friend", he says, and kills him at the cost of his own life.
Boris: they knew each other, but "North's paranoia prevented them from working together".
His identity as the Network founder's familiar is revealed to Jason in Book 5 and to everyone else in Book 13.
Noreth's failure was not seeing that Asano was an ally.
Calm: he announces a potential alliance with the messenger leader while auras erupt in consternation.
Careful: he talks behind a privacy screen with Jillet, watched by the whole room.
Distrustful: he presents the messenger-delivered device with distrust.
An elf, as are most Yaresh locals.
He is "director of the Adventure Society's Yaresh branch".
Book 10: the meeting at Emir's palace; the privacy-screen talk; stares down Vidal Ladiv in his office.
Jillet: an official he consults.
Distracted by proximity: she pays half attention at the symposium after realising who is sitting next to her.
Startled easily: Jason rises from her shadow.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver-ranker trained on Farrah's and Rufus's methods.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Manages the video feeds in the briefing room.
A young girl at Jason's last visit.
She states it has been more than four years since a confirmed trace of McKean.
Book 13: assigned as liaison; in the Asano Village briefing room; startled by Jason; the symposium; McKean update.
Jason: her assigned principal.
Muscular (Sophie and Belinda comment on his "muscular body"), though the notes describe him as "chubby for an elf".

He grew up in the Mercer family's orbit: he started spending time at the Mercer compound as a boy because Thadwick needed friends his own age and the Davone and Kettering families had close ties to the Mercers.
At thirteen he had a crush on Cassandra Mercer, four years older.
He makes a stand in the Temple of the Healer, and after being rejected by the Mercers' circle the guards treat him as "just another iron-ranker".
He is uncertain about joining Jason's team and shows a nervous expression when pressed.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Essences: Shield, Growth and Renewal, producing the Prosperity confluence (Jason's notebook): short-lived shields that intercept attacks, healing and cleansing.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Abilities: size-growth power and Armour of Renewal, which reduces damage taken and gives healing over time; the Reaper's Redoubt.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Summon: a chrysalis golem "like an ogre carved out of diamond" with runes appearing on its facets as it is hit.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Late: his Growth, Renewal and Prosperity essences find fertile ground in desert reclamation in Australia and North Africa.
An elf of the Davone family, whose household is on the Island and holds tea lands in the Mistrun valley (where a maid serves the family's blend).

He was initially Thadwick Mercer's lackey and team mate; after the disastrous expedition Thadwick disbanded the team without notice and the two were glad to be free of being known as Thadwick's flunkeys, and Neil then joined Jason's team.
Cassandra Mercer is not his ex: as a youth he admired Thadwick's older sister, and he was angry that she chose Jason.
She was Jason's girlfriend and ended it.
Book 11: a defender-healer in the transformation zone with Dustin Kettering.
Book 12: in the Mirror Kingdom with Nik, portalled in with Team Shining Scabbard led by Sigrid Freyn, with whom Neil had been training.
Cue: Asano's visit left Neil uncertain, since the only real attraction to joining the team was Humphrey Geller.
Disgruntled and proud: he is summoned to the cult camp and refuses to taint the church for "short-term power".
Moral authority absent god: his god's voice is silent, making him the highest moral authority in the realm he stands in.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver-rank barrier and force specialist: his barrier shields his group from a falling building; a force wave power; "always the true danger".
Archbishop of the Church of Purity, introduced at a Greenstone meeting. One Book 3 line spells the name Hedron.
Book 2: enters the ritual room with Danielle Geller, Thalia Mercer, Elspeth Arella and Emir Bahadir.

Book 3: vanishes on a "previously scheduled sabbatical"; joins the camp (Book 3, Ch54-56); the battle (Book 3, Ch58-59); killed, with a large part of Purity's funds in his storage; the Builder says losing Hendren's power is a blow though he was a reluctant ally.
The Builder cult: reluctant ally.
He took a large part of Purity's funds with him.
In the camp he wears black fatigues under magical tactical armour, carrying no firearms, only a thigh-mounted magic knife.
By Book 12 he holds a gold-rank pistol with a magical silencer, a gift from a grateful client.
Disciplined: "We can't match up to your gear... But we have training and discipline".
Direct and proud of results: "We've taken out four category threes just today".
Bitter at the blood farms: "How many farms were left running while the Asanos were hiding in their magic hole?".
Careful: he spends more time hiding than moving in the city and freezes when a vampire sniffs the cellar.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: First gold-ranker outside the US without cores; "the US had non-core training programs long before Farrah Hurin arrived".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: The rest of his team are silver-rank core users.
His team is the same nine-person unit it was almost two decades earlier, when it belonged to the Network's secret paramilitary wing.
When the Network schismed, they left, sickened by infighting and the Australian government, and became mercenaries.
Book 4: Keith brings Nigel to the grandmother's visit; his team sweeps a camp perimeter; Jason shows him his party voice chat and tells him the Network's methods are reaching their limits.
Book 5: he is Gladys's bodyguard when Jason's rage flares.
Book 12: hides in a vampire city; moves blood farm victims with the clan.
Book 13: infiltrates Multan, Pakistan; his teams bring vampires back when clearing farms.
Jason: Jason's tutor on how teams will fail against stronger monsters.
Rufus: rides back with him from the blood farms.
Gladys: he is her bodyguard.
Nik is a four-foot humanoid rabbit in a top hat and tuxedo whom Jason brought into being, unplanned, when his soul realm became a transformation zone.
He curses constantly, is bleeped on the page, and calls Jason "Dad".
He is the control key to the zone's network, trains at the Geller estate, reaches gold rank and acts as a team's coordinator and overwatch through drones and mapping powers.
Nik first appears to Neil and Dustin in the soul realm as a "four-foot humanoid rabbit in a top hat and tuxedo", with swearing bleeped and a "bleeper" he does not recall being installed.

Jason names him in a forest: "Nik. NIK, no C", from "Lehenik", a word from the language of Jason's birth world meaning "first" or "firstly", and the name Jason would give a people of which Nik is the first instance.
Jason declines to name him after Kai and offers him the Asano surname if he wants it.
The transformation zone created him, with the Healer's gift erasing any flaws; Jason "unconsciously brought" him into being.
He says he is "six months old" and that most of what he knows is "random nonsense put in my head".
He is "the key" to the network of control nodes Jason made while changing the zone, and the node's lock is broken.
He and one of Shade's bodies bring Jason's friends into the soul realm as "plan B" and lead them to the objective. He calls Boris "Two-Piece Feed".
He attacks by making wind sounds with his mouth, and a small cloud appears.
He he runs the weather machine across the unified territory from a platform of control panels.
His head can pass through a portal while his body stays hundreds of kilometres away.
He learns a board game from Neil and suggests planting the tree in Jason's soul realm.
He is part of Jason's "core group of friends" in the tree city.
After the zone, being normal rank among gods left him feeling "vulnerable and weak", and he trains at the Geller estate in Greenstone.
His combination is from Earth: the technology essence Jason brought, with Myriad and Vast, producing the Network confluence.
Danielle Geller's introduction gets him into the family's most elite training programme, building a support set as the "central hub of a team". He is bronze when he leaves Greenstone.
He calls Neil "Uncle Neil".
Neil and Nik are portalled in from the Mirror Kingdom with Team Shining Scabbard, led by Sigrid Freyn.
Jason estimates that Nik was "five, maybe" when he left.
Nik tells Jason: "Dad, you created me out of thin air like you were starting your own bible, sent me to violence boarding school and then vanished for a decade and a half".
Jason promises to do better, warns him that Emi will hug him all week, and Nik asks him for a hug.
He travels on Jason's cloud ship and in Vitesse, where he points out the flowering towers.
At the sky port battle he offers to get the arriving groups "in line", saying he is used to jumping in with groups that do not know him.
His System ability: a raid group invitation notes that "the powers of [Nik Asano] interface with you".
He is nervous about meeting the Asano family, wishes Jason had come back, and wants to find a team on Earth.
His mapping powers are more precise than Jason's tactical map, and he can relay powers and devices remotely.
He acts as overwatch through an earpiece and through a drone over briefings and the field.
He tells Michael that Jason "created me" and complains he has not been given a girlfriend, saying he might be the last of his kind.
He reaches gold rank, with a celebration party.
Sophie will teach him, Jason and Emi to use wingsuits.
After Jason destroys McKean's astral space, Nik takes over McKean's broadcast and keeps it going.
Voice (condensed): blunt and profane, with bleeped swearing and a love of pop-culture references such as Superman and Lois Lane; fond of "Dad" and wary about being treated as a toy.
What drives him: wanting power that is his own rather than borrowed, and wanting Jason to stay.
How he works in a group: a support set built around being the hub of a team, with mapping and relays.
The books leave the Lehenik as an intention, not a people.
Not described in the lines read; she presides with eight elders at a low table.
Contemptuous of honour: "You sound like your new white friend, Asano".
Strength-first: she argues there is only shame in weakness and "only the strongest shall rise".
Calculating: she tells the others not to inform Mei and Akari, so they act as a mask for the clan's own plans.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: The strongest member of the old Asano clan.
She wrests control of the clan from her son, the former head Shiro, whose closest family settle in Asano Village.
She explains the government seized land from the "upstart clan" and gave it to the "true Asano clan".
Book 5: seizes the clan and confronts Jason; Jason says "My Asano family and your Asano clan henceforth have no connections, Noriko" (Book 5, Ch36-37, Ch52).
Book 12: hosts the pirate admiral Jota Withers with daily visits and servants.
Shiro: son she displaces.
Jason: opponent.
Jota Withers: guest.
Book 12 calls her matriarch of the Asano clan while Yumi is also called matriarch; the two descriptions are not reconciled (open question).
Impassive: he stands apart while guilders tease the independents.
Restraining: "Complications. Best left alone".
Steadfast: the steady one, fresh from a rank-up.
Intractable about coming along: Jason had been reluctant to accept his team, but Orin had proven intractable.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver-ranker most notable for his famous uncle; gold by Book 12.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Storm Shredder is built around buffed high-damage ranged specialists.
He goes on Jason's journey because his uncle insisted.
First met Jason through Vesper's arranged meeting with Kasper Irios.
Book 9: Storm Shredder with Korinne.
Book 11: Storm Shredder loses two members; Orin is the only one strong enough to force Zara back; Amos takes Orin and Rosa back to Rimaros.
Book 12: reached gold on a team with Kasper Irios and friends; a friend of Hils Jaramaris who went on to travel with Asano is presumably him.
Amos: uncle.
Korinne: team leader.
Zara: teammate.
Onyx skin and fiery eyes typical of her people; unaffected by heat.
Keen and grieving: Farrah was her idol and mentor; she lets Jason vent her frustration.
Obedient to instructors: Instructor Gabriel's voice triggers conditioned obedience.
Ignores interruptions: when Lance calls out under his breath, she ignores him.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Leader of a Vitesse team of Rufus's juniors.
Trained at Remore Academy a few years behind Rufus.
She had waited for Farrah's return to Vitesse and, when Farrah died, joined Emir's call for adventurers.
Book 2: cadet Padma Parsell; Farrah's parents seek her out; her team joins the trial late.
Book 3: wants to test itself against Jason's team; standoffish at first, warming up; her team leader builds a rivalry with Valdis.
Farrah: mentor.
Jason: friend and rival.
Valdis: sword rival.
Walks up the path from town with two celestines with emerald hair and eyes.
Blunt: "The name's Pelli and I'll thank you to use it".
Teasing and self-deprecating: "I'm just an old core user"; she shakes her head at "an abundance of experience, dear gods".
Protective: she fights outside the town to spare Kasilaro's residents.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A gold-ranker and core user; she fights a pirate captain outside a town.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She had a magic barrier put on a cave behind the waterfall.
"Aunt Pelli" to Vesper from when she was a girl.
Mayor-level authority in Palisaros: Argy tells Jason "You'll want to talk to Pelli".
Book 7: meets Jason and Rufus; greets Vesper; tells Zara where Jason is; the pirate fight.
Book 8: organises civilians and mining facility evacuees.
Argy: local friend.
Vesper: calls her "Aunt Pelli".
Rufus: she asks about his father and the sword.
Darker skin and much lighter hair than Humphrey, from a distant branch family; light-brown pixie-cut hair.
Dry: "I suspect your mother's hand will be firmly pressed down on the scale".
Relaxed: she settles happily in a chair sipping her second glass while watching Sophie.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A pugilist, "a more damage-oriented version of Sophie"; she launches off Stash's palm to strike multiple enemies.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Iron rank in Book 1 and with the Adventure Society for over half a year.
Distant cousin of Humphrey; the two share a last name but barely any ethnicity.
Rick's sister, on his team but absent for family issues at one point.
Book 1: meets Humphrey on his return from a contract; present when Rick and Humphrey arrive.
Book 2: watches Sophie's practice.
Book 9: back on Rick's team.
Book 10: fights beside Dustin with Stash's help.
Rick: brother.
Humphrey: cousin.
An elf and a local.
Discreet: "a man who understood the value of discretion".
Protective of his boss: he steps up when fury crosses Lamprey's face.
Judges Humphrey fairly: he remembers the Geller son as "polite, forthright and a little lacking in confidence".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He keeps the city campus running while frequently travelling to the Fortress.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He arranges the lifelike water-link to Gabriel Remore.
Long-time deputy who did the real work during Lamprey's famously corrupt tenure.
His son Cassowary is Lamprey's dogsbody and go-between.
Book 1: explains the Fortress office arrangement; watches Clive.
Book 2: Emir and Finn contain Lamprey's outburst.
Book 11: at his desk when Humphrey arrives.
Lucian Lamprey: friend and employer.
Cassowary Finn: son.
An elf with dark brown skin and light brown hair flecked with green.
Direct: "I am Raythe, and I have told you as much of my intentions as you need to know. Leave or die".
Calm and amused: "You shall see me again when it is done. Not too soon, as you have earned your rest".
Reluctant when needed: she tells Jason with a straight face that the World-Phoenix will crawl into his soul, with reluctance in her expression.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Prime vessel of the Keeper of Moments; with Velius she leads the descent of peak diamond-rankers into the shaft.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Boris says the Keeper of Moments polices time manipulation harshly.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She tells Jason only the nameless will stand with the World-Phoenix against him.
After the great beings leave, she alone remains; time there is synchronised with Jason's universe.
Book 9: in Yaresh she tells a challenger to "Leave or die".
Book 11: asks if the Reaper did not tell Velius why they came; the descent; revealed as the Keeper's vessel.
Book 12: remains with Jason.
Book 13: walks beside Jason through the empty tree city of Arbour.
Velius: fellow peak diamond-ranker.
Jason: ally and counsel.

Kakadu: he and Sebastian have taken Miranda (Ellis) out of Australia; her complaint that "Twelve hundred kilometres is the best you can do? And you have to wait an hour between portals?" draws "Let's see your portal power".
They are in Kakadu National Park, which Remy is scornful of her not recognising.
Range: he says no essence user can portal sixteen thousand kilometres, and that the Chinese reportedly have someone near category four who can do a few thousand at a time.
He notes the rule that "You cannot portal where you have never been".
Barbou's men: Miranda calls Remy a failure of "the great portal master Barbou promised".
After a glance, Sebastian kills her with metal hummingbirds and a kick; Remy says "A personality like that is practically a suicide note". He reports to Adrien by phone.
Book 5: "Hi, I'm Remy. You two came in pretty hot", and he takes Jason and a companion through a portal to a command post near Paotere Harbour.

Book 13: Finnegan's portal man: he opens a portal "About time... If any gold-rankers turned up, I was just going to bail", is careful around "that guy", and follows Marie, Gerling and the blood orb through it.
Hurt by Jason's field: a teleport attempt leaves him "doubled over in pain" in Book 13, after which the portal flickers like an old TV. He recovers on a bus roof.

Old job: he did a job for the Lyon branch "back when Asano had just returned to Earth the first time" and explains how a silver-rank was sent to kidnap Jason; Sebastian kicked her off a rock in Kakadu.
Interrogated: Jason reads a spike of panic in his aura when asked who he is protecting and tells him "Give me a name, Remy".
Finnegan and Elizabeth: Jason learns from Remy that Marie has been working "intimately" with Elizabeth, the vampire queen increasingly on the outs with her subjects.
Last scenes: Remy scrambles through a portal with Elizabeth and Marie and wonders "What is this place?" at Elizabeth's refuge.
Elizabeth apologises for jabbing at his weakness.
"Like his sister, his skin was dark brown, his hair light brown. His build was more like Humphrey, tall and broad-shouldered".
Earnest and wide-eyed: the 'standard Rick' expression is wide-eyed, as Jason thinks of it.
Respectful of rank: he realises he is speaking to a gold-rank princess and his head dips as if yanked by a string.
Loyal to his team: he does not like having his team split, and watches over his cousin in the rescue.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A huge sword wielded "like a baton", with an essence ability that "temporarily ramped up his speed and power".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rank: iron-rank in Book 1, a spear-wielder by Book 10 whose team smashes messengers with Stash's help.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Hunt style: put an enemy in front of him and nothing at iron rank survives.
Brother of Phoebe Geller; his team includes Jonah, Henry, the Adeah twins and later Dustin Kettering.
His girlfriend is Hannah Adeah, who slaps the back of his head in Book 10.
Book 1-3: the mirage-arena match with Jason (Book 1, Ch66-67), the survivors of the expedition, Jonah's death, the team contest.
Book 7: he and his team arrive in Rimaros, taken to the throne room by Vesper and present a recording.
Book 9-11: he meets Jason in Rimaros, flies over Yaresh after the battle, fights in Cardinas and brings groups to Jason's territory with Sophie.
Dustin: Rick's team replaced Jonah's role with Dustin, who "was a friend of Neil's".
Humphrey: a close match in style.
Jonah: the cousin he fails to save.
Phoebe: his sister, on his team.
"A well-preserved forty, a tenth of the reality": tall, strong and handsome, with a round bush of dark curly hair.
Weighty and remote: his presence on the Academy campus is always felt and draws all eyes.
Proud of the guild: Gabriel says "He's always treated the guild like it's his own little fiefdom".
Famous: Rufus often repeats his advice.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Diamond-rank sword master; his aura surges out in Book 13.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He personally brought a boy from the countryside to the academy, rumoured.
Archchancellor of Remore Academy; the guild Burning Violet became more associated with the Academy after he became guild leader.
Rufus's grandfather; Gabriel's father.
Book 3: introduced via Rufus's advice and the Academy.
Book 7: Farrah has met him.
Book 9: Jason asks about him.
Book 12: Humphrey says Roland was looking forward to meeting Jason.
Book 13: emerges from the dimensional vessel and meets Jason's aura.
Rufus: grandson, who repeats his advice.
Gabriel: his son.
Humphrey: friend of Rufus who knows his reputation.
Introduced as a rival: a Rimaros adventurer addresses her as "Rosa Liselos, isn't it? What do you say, Liselos? Can you do better than Asano's shadows?".
Role: "Rosa Liselos, the scout from Korinne's team"; "the team scout, she had the best perception amongst them".
