Comfort: she says she "can definitely live with it" if working for Jason means cloud beds and giant dinner spreads, and joins Kalif in telling Korinne the monster surge is over: "This is a can for storing food, not adventurers".
Insight: she names the difference "between adventuring approaches in Rimaros and Vitesse".
Gossip: she bets Jason "doesn't go for those stuffy society dances".
Candour about Zara: she tells a princess to get over a man who is not keen on her and senses him "skulking around".
Surprise: she asks "How did you get so close? You didn't use to be this good" of someone who has improved.
Book 11: the team scout guides the wounded team back to friendly lines "through the enemy throng" to the healers.
Book 12: "Rosa retired. She works for the Adventure Society now".
Dark skin, a bald head and "stupidly handsome"; when Jason first sees him, grimy from his ordeal, he looks like an action hero heading into act three. His voice is "like dark chocolate".
He is "tall and lean" and a "tall, leanly muscular adventurer"; no height in numbers is given.
He is calm under pressure: when Anisa demands that Jason be burned as tainted, he answers "I did [know]" and refuses her any say.
He feels responsible as the leader of his group: Farrah tells Jason "Rufus is in charge, so he blames himself" for their capture, and says the pressure on him from his family is enormous.
After Farrah's death he is driven by obsession, which strains his relationships.
The family joke, repeated by Arabelle and Rufus in Book 10, is "my family runs a school".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Swordsmanship: an elegant scimitar of golden light with red-gold inscriptions that he conjures in his hand; silver and golden swords.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Other powers: boots that let him walk on water and a "speed of light" power that makes the world "seem to freeze in time" for "two seconds of accelerated time".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Kingdom of Eclipse: a sun-and-moon power invoked by incantation ("Darkness and light, sun and moon; be mine to awaken and move at my command...").

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rank: bronze at the start of the series (: "We're bronze-rank adventurers"), and in Book 11 he is the most powerful combatant on Earth below gold rank; the chapters read do not state that he reaches gold.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Teaching: he teaches Jason footwork, balance and combat and later teaches the Asano clan.

Son of Gabriel and Arabelle Remore; grandson of Roland Remore (Humphrey calls Roland "the grandfather who means so much to his friend"); his older brother Gwydion is a priest of Hero; Rufus's uncle is clergy of Hero.
Rufus was "really late fighting his first monster" but did it "by nineteen".
Books 2-3: uses his Kingdom of Eclipse power in the strike on the Builder cult camp.
Book 11: travels to Earth with Taika and Boris, arriving at the standing stones and meeting Yumi Asano (Yumi is from the notes).
Book 13: by 2038 he teaches the Asano clan; he introduces Hassan Dukhtar, whom he is dating.
Voice (condensed): Courteous and formal, quick to apologise for discourtesy. Cue: his apology to Priestess Pellin.
Rank in the order: Melody leads the enclave and Sendira, her second, reports on what the scouts have found.
The overall leadership is the same silver rank as the individual cell leaders, so there is "a constant tension".
Reliability: she is "ever-reliable"; like another cell leader, Kelleigh, she is not ambitious, which places her as Melody's second.

Doctrine: she tells the converted, "Only Purity is worthy of our devotion, not his servants... We are all unworthy, seeking to cleanse the taint that lingers within us", and "Distraction and frivolity taint pure dedication of purpose".
Command on the island: she is "the commander of the Purity forces on the island", separating from most of her group to take a smaller team underground.
Control of subordinates: she wants Fila and Ramona "under her thumb instead of causing trouble for Melody's plans".
She snaps at Ramona that "What Melody wants with the target is no concern of yours. Your place is to obey, not criticise in ignorance".
The beacon: when the grab team seizes Melody's daughter, "Sendira couldn't activate the beacon fast enough".
She launches a flare that scatters motes of light, and the beacon's pervasive aura drenches the island until it is cut off, at which she shows "an expression of uncertainty".
Clockwork kings: when the Builder cult delivered the first clockwork king, it came with a control device; she explains that the order purified both.
She orders the kings through a portal after taking out a silver pyramid.
Doubt among her people: Jaime says "Sendira is using us as decoys".
Assessment: "The likelihood of their having realised our objective is high".
At the leaders' meeting: she stands next to Melody as hostile cell leaders glare; angry at a remark, she is silenced by Melody's gesture.
Melody asks whether she has been telling people they were going after Melody's daughter.
Search: she crouches with the others to feel faint vibrations through the floor.
Pale, freckled skin, wild red hair and eyes so green they almost glow.
Impatient and proud: he sighs at his petitioners despite not needing breath for centuries.
Contemptuous: he sneers when Jason tries to push back.
Struck still when overridden: when the Builder speaks through him he goes stiff.
Told he has no authority of his own: "You don't have any authority, do you, Shako?".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Diamond-rank: his aura crushes Jason's aura and lifts him into his grip.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Can enter through a window opened by the transformation event as long as he leaves before it closes.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Moves faster than Jason can think; a tablet throws him back with a sonic boom.
A servant of the Builder; in Book 3 he is seen in an imperial throne room with an empress.
Dawn warns that killing Jason violated the compact between the Builder, the Reaper and the World-Phoenix.
Book 3: the imperial palace scene and the Reaper's district.
Book 6: introduces himself and kills Jason; Dawn confronts him; Jason wonders whether he was sent to "lose control".
Book 8: tablet incident and Dawn-Builder switch; catatonic afterwards.
Book 10-11: Erigo replaces him; Jason mentions him.
Dawn: confronts him.
Jason: killer and later subject of questions.
The Builder: his master.
The Church of Death's certification counts Jason's deaths; Shako's killing is the fourth.
A celestine woman.
Apologetic for Valdis: she quietly apologises for him.
Dry and practical: she tells Valdis to be more respectful of his father and king.
Networking: she steers him toward making connections.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Healer and team leader; "the most impactful person on the field" in the mock battle; named by the system when Jason's team defeats her.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She keeps a dimensional space with cushions.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Leads Team Shining Scabbard, a famously capable leader and healer whom Neil has been training with; faces Neil in a healer match.
She greets Hastor, the Mirror King's portal specialist, as "Father"; the king is her father-in-law.
Open question: whether Hastor is still the king's portal specialist in Book 12; the text calls the specialist only "the Mirror King's own portal specialist".
Book 12: the reunion and healer match.
Book 13: credited as Sigrid Volaire, Prince Valdis's team healer and wife, on the expedition.
Valdis: husband.
Neil: sparring partner.
Hastor: father.
Obsessed with the fight: Boris warns Jason that McKean "has spent the last decade preparing for this fight. To him, battling you is not a means but an end in itself".
Cunning: he baited the coalition into the fight, and no one knows why.
Controlled: he watches Jason and two familiars move through his tunnels from a monitoring room.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Expert in the grid: "about as expert in it as anyone but you" and understands it better than anyone other than Farrah.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Created vampire-magitech abominations by mixing modern magitech with blood magic.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Modified a vine to revive the undead and bound souls of vampires and minions to it.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He took Gerling from the vampire queen and used him as an agent.
Head of the Earth researchers, ranked only behind Farrah in the workgroup.
He and Farrah repaired the grid together after the Engineers of Ascension sabotaged it.

Book 13: Farrah describes him; Boris's warning; Michael and Jason plan the strike; Jason will "confront McKean tomorrow"; the castle was a Network operations centre; the vine; his broadcast breaks up at the collapse.
Farrah: the only one in Jason's circle who knows him personally.
The vampires: he is already working with them.
Gerling: his agent.
Jason says McKean is "just a warm-up compared to what comes next".

Chocolate skin, shining silver hair and sharp eyes that exactly match the hair, "the matching metallics a giveaway trait of the celestine race"; normally shoulder length, tied back in a simple, practical ponytail.
Suspicious of kindness at first: "Are you trying to tell me that Jory is such a good friend to you that you'd go this far over some girl he likes?".
She fights through pain without complaint; in Book 2, one-armed and struggling to her knees, she waves off the lesser miracle potion Jason offers. Her laugh is "free".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Essences: Swift, Balance and Wind, producing the Mystic confluence: Clive answers "Mystic" when Rufus asks what that combination produces.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Before Jason's help she had only the Swift essence and its single ability for more than half a dozen years.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Abilities: Eternal Moment, a massive acceleration power in which "time seemed to freeze" as she produced wind blades; Between the Raindrops (from the Awakening Stone of the Rain; notes, Book 2); Mirage Step and Wind Blade; unarmed Way of the Reaper strikes.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Racial gifts (celestine): Mana Integrity evolves into Mana Wellspring, Astral Affinity into Boundary Breaker, which removes the damage reduction from rank disparity, and Celestial Swiftness into Princess of the Firmament.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Late: in Book 13 she has spent several years purging whole cities of disease with her wind and aura.
Born in Kurdansk, in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil (Emir).
Her father's failed expedition left her with a huge debt at sixteen or seventeen, and she worked as a pit fighter; Cole Silva, whose father her father had worked for, wanted her.
Her mother is Melody Jain, who faked her death some twenty years earlier.
Book 7: Jason learns that her mother leads the Order of Redeeming Light in Rimaros.
Book 11: Humphrey calls her his fiancée.
Cues: she asks why Jason would do so much for them; she grimaces silently through the pain of a broken arm.
Emerald hair and eyes at a party, then natural royal blue.
Calming and formal: his aura spreads calm that oppresses the agitated Farrah and Liara.
Plain-spoken about debts: "It is undeniable that we have dragged Jason Asano into events he never asked for".
Deference from others: even the Storm King defers to the founder in the private lounge.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Diamond-rank ruler.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He tells Jason that the Hierophant may intervene in the world a single time.
Palindromic first and last names "were assigned in adulthood rather than at birth and denoted important members of a given family".
Sits with the Storm King and core royal family members in an elevated lounge.
Book 7: meets Jason; the balcony meeting with Liara and Trenchant; leads Dawn away; the Builder's fortress emerges.
Book 9: with the royal family at the confrontation; he steps in when Jason soul-attacks a man in front of the king.
Book 10: his connection to Jason keeps the Adventure Society from accusing him.
Book 13: not among the diamond-rankers who emerge from the dimensional vessel.
Liara: royal officer and relative.
Jason: protector and uneasy debtor.
Dawn: he leads her away from the crowd.
His connection to a diamond-ranker Jason knows deferentially is not explained in the lines read.
"The mountainous Māori", comparable in size to a leonid or a draconian, with tattoos that stand out against his skin when it turns emerald to resist damage.
A "massive frame" that does not buckle a reinforced chair when he drops into it.
In bird form he is a giant golden bird.
Easy and cheerful: "Taika, by the way. Like the director, but I don't make films"; "the numbers for letters thing is a bit naff, though, right? It's not 2004".
Companionable: he sits behind a plastic drum kit while Jason and Emi play a rhythm game.
He tells Jason "I don't normally like watching people's holiday videos, but they were pretty sweet".
Sharp-eyed: his "narrowed eyes lingered on Boris" before he got to work.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rank: he races up through the proto-spaces and monster waves, "especially with being human as an accelerating factor".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He is "on the very cusp of silver" at the end of the surge (per the Power Sets file).

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A mobility brawler: Farrah teaches him to fight "like Taika", adapting to his new abilities, and his performance helps convince the Network to grant him a place.
He is "Taika Williams", employed by Hiro in Sydney and knows the ropes of the Asano family business.
When offered the renewal essence and immortal confluence Jason picked out, he chose a different combination after discussion.
Book 4: he phones to say a man claiming to be Hiro's nephew is looking for him and drives Jason to a code-locked building, telling him the code so he can come and go.
Book 7: he and Travis stay with the Gellers in dormitories for young trainees, preferential treatment for being Jason's friends.
Book 9: his rank-up, his fight with the messenger Fal (Book 9, Ch93) and his meeting with Haliastur.
Book 10-11: he flies after Jason and Farrah as a golden bird, meditates atop Onslow's shell and goes to Earth with Rufus and Boris.
Book 12: he and Boris's group go to meet Shiro and the bodyguards, and his bird form carries a saucer.
Hiro Asano: his boss, who rides in silence with him in Book 4.
Rufus: both could benefit from each other's knowledge; they travel together.
Jason: "boss".
Emi: sits behind a drum kit as she and Jason play a rhythm game.
Voice (condensed): Large, good-humoured and loyal; a complaint about his mother's opinions on French food is his signature.
She and Marek wear simple leather armour of magical synthetic instead of the diaphanous clothing messengers favour.
Zealous: "I am Tera Jun Casta... I will be the one to kill you".
Rigid and devout: a "zealous follower of the messenger orthodoxy before her forced liberation".
Duellist by temperament: she chooses weapons that instil the most fear.
Guarded: she listens to Jason's story "without comment or expression, but her aura was a calamity of emotions".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She fights comfortably with her abilities suppressed, in an orthodox style.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Her seal keeps her at silver rank; Jason removes it by working inside her soul.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: A messenger unable to advance beyond silver is a loose addition to the raid forces.
Her soul is branded and she was raised on lies and exploited her entire life.
Her old friend from "their days of enslavement" is Jali Corrik Fen.
Book 9: duel with Jason in a ruined tavern and dormitory; stripped of her seal.
Book 10: Marek sits with her; the astral king punishes the emotions she held back.
Book 11-13: Jali's only friend; at the kitchen table with Jason, Boris and Jali.
Jali Corrik Fen: old friend.
Marek Nior Vargas: her commander.
Jason: freed her against her will.
Inflicting soul torture on her was the only way Jason could win the death match she forced on him.
Not described in detail in the lines read; his gear includes a blade with a ruby and onyx hilt and a spiked grip in Book 13.
Arrogant and cruel: "a fool whose arrogance and incompetence only escalated over time" and "the worst".
Fixated on Jason: "Thadwick was always fixated on me. I think he might have had a sister complex", after Jason dated his sister Cassandra.
Leashed: a rival greets him, "I see your mother let you out, so long as you wore your leash".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Lightning, wind, potent and storm essences (see Essence_Catalogue.md).

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He fights from behind his protectors: Dustin used his powers to protect while Neil healed him, and Thadwick "had been blasting powers".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: After the star seed he becomes a vessel for the Builder and later "some weird vampire".
Family: his father Beaufort Mercer is the Duke of Greenstone's brother; his mother Thalia is an adventurer.
Companions by obligation: "Neil and Dustin were forced to train and work with Thadwick through the obligation of their families".
Sister: Cassandra Mercer is four years older than Neil and the object of his youthful affection.
Book 1: his entourage at the Mercer gatherings; the expedition.
Book 2: he faces Timos and wipes the sneer off his face; he is missing and hunted.
Book 3: he enters a hole to receive power and is in the cult's care when Jason appears as a shadow.
Book 9: an energy vampire who took the sword; in Book 10 "the vampire once known as Thadwick" speaks.
Book 13: he carries the relic blade and meets Thalia in a warehouse.
Neil and Dustin: his offsiders, "both stuck under Thadwick due to their families".
Thalia and Beaufort: parents, one adamant about training, the other guilty.
Cassandra: his sister, who dated Jason.
He was possessed by the Builder at one point, and is the subject of Umber's later plans.
Welcoming with an edge: "You must be the young man people are getting so curious about".
Wry and diplomatic: "I daresay you're right. So, you're willing to leave Thadwick to my family?".
Unhappy about her husband's decision: she tried to convince him Thadwick needed more training.
Motherly under pressure: she fusses over Thadwick as he is carried through a portal.
Sentimental about her daughter: she hasn't seen Cassandra "in years" and watches her from behind a tree.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver rank with might, potent, swift and onslaught essences: "in terms of pure explosive power she was a match for any adventurer alive".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She blasted Thadwick's door "to splinters with a special attack".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Her Onslaught essence informs her inclinations as well as her power set.
Friend and teammate of Danielle Geller.
Present at the estate when Danielle witnesses Jonah Geller's gruesome end.
Book 1: introduced by Danielle; boards the Geller carriage; settles Thadwick's future.
Book 2: with Danielle, Emir, Arella and the archbishop; the black parlour and the corpse puppets.
Book 13: watches Cassandra; Thadwick leaves the bunker without a word of goodbye.
Thadwick: son.
Cassandra: daughter she hasn't seen in years.
Danielle Geller: friend and teammate.
Her Book 13 watching of Cassandra from a tree implies the estrangement.
Not described in the lines read; he wears dismissive sneers until Thadwick wipes one off.
Regretful: he "quickly came to regret" Thadwick's aggressive self-recruitment.
Cautious: every mistake "threatened to snowball into disaster".
Compartmentalising: he facilitated the cult's insertions and ran operatives in compartmentalised groups.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He kills Frank with a conjured spear.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He takes part in a ritual with Zato and Dougall.
"Timos had been operating in Greenstone for years".
Book 2: Thadwick presses him about flashes of memory; the Frank murder.
Book 3: led with Thadwick across the Vane estate by Zato; the ritual; Zato notes the marks on his neck.
Zato: his leader.
Thadwick: an inconvenient recruit.
Not described in detail in the lines read; "goofy grin" when he watches his wife eat.
Overworked and decent: "Travis Noble was twenty-one years old and a category two magitech weapons engineer from California. He was also having a very bad month".
Clear-sighted on Network faults: "The Network has kidnapped Mr Asano twice, along with killing his friend, his girlfriend and his brother".
A researcher by temperament: "an enthusiastic researcher whose expertise bled into" other fields.
Devoted husband: he is happy and worried watching his wife eat.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Magitech weapons engineer: a specialist in large-scale weaponry.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: His dimensional space is a holographic cabinet with a sliding door, from which he pulls an oversized high-tech revolver.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Cross-world builder: he works with Clive, Gary and Gabrielle on the tools and artifice side of magitech.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Constructs: he waves a rod and a mannequin-like construct walks out.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Sky link: his sky link service carries calls by Book 12.
Category-two Network engineer who becomes head of the Special Munition Stockpile Division when his supervisor goes AWOL, with a team of people who all hate him.
An outworlder from Earth to Pallimustus.
Book 6: Germany, Network base (Book 6, Ch28-29); he stays in France when Jason leaves.
Book 7: Greenstone and Rimaros; Jason takes him to the Church of Knowledge; the battle seen from the cloud house.
Book 9-10: he joins Jason's circle and works on weapons for the siege (Book 10, Ch30).
Book 12-13: he and Farrah own the island; by Book 13 he is the lead researcher for the Joint Magitech Weapons Research Institute.
Gabrielle Pellin: his wife, a priestess of Knowledge.
Taika: close friend.
Clive and Gary: collaborators.
His negotiations with the Church of Knowledge over what Earth magitech he may bring to Pallimustus are part of Knowledge's plan.
A human in a guild of mostly celestines: pale-skinned and dark-haired, lean and angular with icy blue eyes.
Reserved: he drops to one knee before the royals.
Cautious about politics: he warns that Vesper's world is political.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Gold rank sword specialist who has served as a guard on and off for decades.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He boards ships checking society contracts.
The royal family does not shield the Sapphire Crown from surge quotas.

Book 7: summoned to a low-key palace meeting where Vesper Rimaros lets him keep his sword; escorts Jason's group to the cloud house; Jason tells him to hear his debrief; stands with Liara when Zara confronts them.
Liara: stands beside her.
Vesper Rimaros: the royal who gives him leave to keep his sword.
Appears as a mass of shadow with smoky orange eyes.
Resentful of change: fixated on the idea that changing from the original state means falling from grace; he hates Shade for embracing it.
Opportunistic and bitter: he plays games when Shade's power is limited by a vessel.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He built the bridge anchor ritual to bind Jason's consciousness into the prime avatar; a word from Jason makes him reel.
Shade says Umber told him he had Shade trapped in an astral space for centuries "to teach you a lesson about duty".
Umber persuaded Shade's summoner to trap him.
Astral beings are things of spirit with defined natures: Colin an avatar of hunger, Gordon a herald of annihilation, Shade "a shepherd of death".
Book 8: Shade recounts his imprisonment.
Book 13: Shade explains the siblings; marshalling yard.
Shade: brother and enemy.
He serves Knowledge's plan against Jason.
Introduces himself as "Valdis" and praises Clive's reputation; the system names him Valdis Volaire.

A prince of the small but influential Kingdom of Mirrors, whose borders have not changed in eight centuries; his father, the Mirror King, is eight hundred years old and the kingdom is "thick with princes and princesses".
A reckless enthusiast who leads his three teammates up a tower in search of treasure; he has a light-step power, a slow-fall power and a wall run.
He chooses the path of courage in the trial and is the first to step forward.
A sword master, mobile striker and the stronger team's leader; his team is a highly efficient cohort trained since before they had essences.
His father collects him from Jason's ship, to Valdis's embarrassment; he portals in for Jason's memorial.
By Book 12 he is Sigrid's husband, assembles an arena event in under two days, and fights Jason in a mirage chamber using Mind's Eye to sense the space around him.
Book 3: friendly rival team; mock battles (Book 3, Ch4).
Boisterous, flirtatious and fond of a good story ("the virile verve of ten men"); he loves duelling famous warriors for the push, not the win.
"A tall celestine, with dark skin and a bushy mound of curly, silver hair that matched his eyes".
When the Reaper speaks, his eyes become black orbs and his voice turns cold and bleak.
Warm: Shako greets him warmly in the dome chamber and he waves Shako into a lounge chair.
Rueful about descendants: he says he made the mistake of getting his descendants out of trouble again and again until he washed his hands of them.
Earnest in work: Rufus finds him "earnest and diligent" in a role normally handled by the church of Fertility.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Prime vessel of the Reaper.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: With Raythe he leads the descent of peak diamond-rankers into the shaft.
Someone who has known Velius a very long time calls him "an old friend".
Book 3: the dome chamber.
Book 11: says the Builder is done with Pallimustus; the descent; the Reaper speaks through him; asks for a meeting in the clan maternity ward.
Shako: friendly rival.
Raythe: fellow peak diamond-ranker.
When he and Shako change, the Reaper speaks through Velius and the voice becomes cold.
Cold and curious: she watches servant race armies battle to the death, resurrecting them and bestowing abilities "to keep things interesting".
Soul engineer: known for her fascination with soul engineering.
Separate goals: she chose a separate goal from the rest of the group and is young.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: She feels one of her seals vanish when Jason removes it from Tera.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Jason says Vesta used Tera, keeping her at silver rank.
"The astral king who rules the local messenger forces" and a known practitioner of soul engineering.
Marek served her until recently.
Book 9: introduced; the seal incident.
Book 10: Jason removes her brand from Tera; at the Council of Kings her prime avatar scolds Jamis.
Book 11: Boris says she hired messengers with elemental powers and would never accept a member of the Unorthodoxy, and has no idea he is one.
Marek, Tera: servants.
Jamis Fran Muskar: fellow king.
Boris is of the Unorthodoxy and she does not know it.
Increasingly dishevelled hair that "only further set off his rakish good looks".
Anxious: pacing around a rooftop garden while Emi eats a sandwich and teases him.
Driven: his drive is more valuable than his talent; the Remore teaching method gives the most time to those with motivation.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Swordsman, close to gold: his aura is in the upper reaches of silver.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rufus picked him out early for his swordsmanship and self-motivation.
Member of the Baudrillard family; Chloe Baudrillard, an epidemiologist Jason befriended, is of the same family.
Jason has watched him grow from a boy to a man through the domain.
Book 13: the Saint-Étienne rooftop scene.
Emi: love interest; Jason's interest is as a match for her, and rank matters for the ageing question.
Rufus: his mentor.
A moustache that "extended past either side of his head"; in Book 12 "everything about Vincent Trenslow was drooping except for his immaculate moustache".
Professional: Rufus notes his manner "had been nothing but professional".
Barking: "Mercer, if I see you try to use an ability on a fellow candidate again, you will fail on the spot".
Disdainful of favouritism: he shows "a hint of disdain around the eyes" at Guy's division of the group.
Unhappy official: he explains an administrative error "unhappily".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He uses a silver-grey recording crystal during assessments.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: He identifies thirteen ratlings that would run to their burrows.
Rufus worked closely with him during the last field assessment and called him "exactly what I expect from a Society official".
He extends the director's apologies and says she is "new to the role".
Book 1: explains the assessment procedure; hands Jason his badge and explains stars.
Book 2-3: drinks with Rufus on the houseboat; at the marina group; on the terrace with Rufus.
Book 12: managing requests from nobility before the gold-rankers arrive.
Rufus: worked together on the assessment.
Elspeth Arella: his director.
Her flesh-warping powers restored her youth, giving her a mid-twenties appearance; in Book 13 she looks to be in her early thirties.
Stern: Jason greets her "G'day, Nanna... Sorry, Grandmother" and earns a glare.
Deliberate: she quietly takes in Jason's explanation, sipping tea, before responding.
Scolding: she scolds Jason "in a very matronly tone".
Wary: she wonders whether any of the boy she knew is still inside Jason.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Flesh-shaping powers.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Forbids members going far outside the domain.
Jason's paternal grandmother.
Book 12 also calls a woman named Noriko "matriarch of the Asano clan"; the two descriptions are not reconciled (open question).
Book 4: raises her eyebrows at Jason.
Book 5: hears Jason's warning; chats with Dawn.
Book 6: pushes Jason to formalise the clan; raps Jason on the arm.
Book 11-13: zeppelin over Nitra; contribution points; Jason confides his fear of a god; sits as matriarch beside General Mills.
Jason: grandson.
Erika: shares contribution-point plans.
Jason says "That's a god, Grandmother" about what awaits him.
Celestine with caramel skin, sapphire eyes and waterfall-blue hair.
After her adoption into her mother's House Nareen she has milky teal hair and eyes; by Book 12 she is still "turning your hair and eyes copper".
At first she is regal ("royal highness") and wary: in Book 2 Jason teleports into her tent and offers gem-berry and milk-nut squares.
She invents a fiancé and seeks "a place to belong".
In Book 13 she advises Jason to keep a consistent persona: "a good lord, not a good leader".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Powers: wind and water, big storms (says she has "been blowing things up with big storms"); recovery, speed, astral and holy affinity.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Rank: gold by Book 12: she stays in a suite fit for gold-rank adventurers and calls up a storm of gold-rank force; her rank when she first meets Jason is not stated in the chapters read.

Firstborn daughter of the Storm King, called the Hurricane Princess; her brother Emiliano becomes Storm King, and the notes for Book 13 call him her "adopted cousin-brother", an adopted baby shielded from the parents' treason; Zara herself is adopted into her mother's House Nareen.

Vesper Rimaros is Zara's aunt; Vesper says she is sixty-seven and calls Pelli "Aunt Pelli", who remembers her as a wilful girl on the island, so the notes' "descendant of Pelli" is corrected to niece (or at least a younger relative); she hopes to reach gold during the surge, which places her below gold, and she is silver rank ("Vesper's silver-rank vision"; "Vesper was only silver rank to Liara's gold"); Liara Rimaros is a gold-ranker of the royal house, and Zareen Rimaros, Zara's lady in waiting and cousin, is Liara's daughter.
Book 7: Zara had been matched with a member of House Irios, a political marriage the royals wanted for stability before the surge.

Book 9: she is a former princess of the Storm Kingdom by Book 9; she says "I'm Zara Nareen now" and that she adopted into her mother's house, whose colouration she wears, to signal her withdrawal from the contest for the crown.
Book 12: meets Jason again after fifteen years; has joined Team Biscuit.

Book 13: she is left with Emi and Erika for an hour, and Jason's father and brother-in-law join them; Jason tells Ken how they met twenty years ago; she walks the promenade deck hand in hand with Jason and kisses him later in a scene about Allayeth and Rufus.
Voice (condensed): Courtly, with a threat in the smile. Cue:.
Family: "Dara was the eldest and, like the middle child, Zareen, had followed their mother into adventuring"; the youngest, Joseph, is an administrator.
Appearance: "physically smaller" than her sister, not inheriting her mother's height, but with "the iconic sapphire hair and eyes of the royal family".

Politics, not combat: she is "much more interested in politics than her mother", and was close to Vesper, "picking up her relative's taste for the politics that Liara disdained but could never seem to escape".
Interest in Jason: "I'm more interested in the man himself... Is it true that his aura is as strong as a gold-ranker's?" and Liara scolds her "Don't even think about it".
Jason later says he is "not looking for the entanglements a political marriage would bring".
A political match: Zara notes whether Jason chooses "Zareen, myself, someone else or no one at all" is up to him; Dara and Baseph exchange looks about Zareen's absence from dinner.
Rufus guesses she would be the royal choice, since her sister is "pure adventurer" without political sensibilities.
Liaison: she is the royal family liaison to Jason's team.
Liara scolds her for making "a bold move instead of talking to your mother about it because you knew she would be against it".

At the duel and ball: she sits with Jason and Liara at the confrontation with Hector de Varco, asks whether he is "remotely torturing a group of gold-rankers", and asks "Did you plan for the king to step in?".
Intelligence on the duel: she explains that most of a rival guild fought the city attack on Livaros, with its special members on monster watch on Provo.
Book 12: she is assigned to the Rimaros diplomatic delegation to Earth.

Book 13: "technically a princess, but far enough down the hierarchy that she was formally referred to as 'lady'"; she is something like a lady in waiting to Princess Zara and "had a history with Jason... mostly a social connection, through her mother".
She teases Zara by swooning at her pacing.
A silvery metal body that flows "like quicksilver", reshaping itself to produce combat abilities.
On top of things: Jason says "He does seem pretty on top of things... I actually kind of like him" and invites him to join team "Hopelessly Outmatched".
Convinced of victory: "Zato knew that his victory was imminent. He knew that the adventurers were no match for his power".
Quiet in command: he stands with his back to the door, eyes lingering on Timos's neck marks, saying nothing.
Recruiter: "I see your true potential".

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Silver rank, with a metal body of shifting abilities.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Immovable in the final fight: no damage seems to impair him, even Humphrey's strikes.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Trump card: after baiting out Sophie's absorb power, his body explodes into a mass of shrapnel.

"The last silver-ranker left in the Builder cult's local forces"; tasked with leading the evacuation when the island stronghold was invaded, he escaped with a good number of people, though none of the other silver-rankers survived.

Book 3: leads the evacuation; stands before the inert archway; recruits Thadwick; asks what to do with bronze-rankers the cult cannot convert with clockwork cores; falls before Jason and Sophie flee to the gate; the climax with Humphrey and Sophie.
Thadwick Mercer: his recruit.
Humphrey and Sophie: opponents in the climax.
Timos: his follower, whose neck he notices.

sec: 4. Powers and skills as world facts
claim: Boris counts him among the few who can truly shake the cosmos.
Jason tells Allayeth: "His name is Zithis Carrow Vayel. He was a sixteen-year-old diamond-ranker when the great astral beings recruited him to replace the old Builder"; the Builder was a messenger.
Jamis says Zithis's debt to the astral kings will be paid when the task is complete.
Book 8: the token Jason loots is bound to him and to Jason; Jason wonders who Zithis is.
Book 9: Kaal names him with the World-Phoenix's "now-former prime vessels".
Book 10: Jamis says "Zithis Carrow Vayel will have fulfilled his debt to us"; Allayeth asks "The Builder was a messenger?" after Jason's account.
Book 11: Boris names him among the few who can truly shake the cosmos.
Jamis Fran Muskar: creditor astral king.
Named: Jason says, "I've decided to call him Colin. And his friends. Team Colin", and calls the swarm "Leechy" in the same fight.
Lives in Jason's blood: Jason pricks his finger and the leeches crawl into his hand and vanish into his blood.
His rapid regeneration only works while the familiar is in his bloodstream.
Method: Jason sprays him out over a target like a fire hose and Colin crawls over armour to find flesh. Colin wiggles happily when pleased.

Where he comes from: a summoned familiar is created through different means from the sanguine horror, but Clive observes it is what Jason summoned, and if Jason reached diamond his familiar would reach the full strength of a sanguine horror.
Silver vessel: he needs a silver-rank vessel with simple requirements, such as a wheelbarrow-load of silver-rank blood quintessence.
Blood clone: Colin takes a form like a blood clone of Jason, and Clive can switch-teleport him.
Origin: he comes from the border between the realms of the All-Devouring Eye and Legion, where life and annihilation are neighbours.
Refined: Jason refines his physical vessel with the astral throne and his connections with the astral gate.
A window offers him the chance to awaken as a Voice of the Will after extended hibernation in the astral kingdom.
Voice of the Will: "Your familiar and bonded avatar [Colin] has become your [Voice of the Will]".
He spends time in a cocoon while Jason is busy.
"Smarmy?" he calls back at Jason; Jason thanks him quietly.
Hunger: Shade names Colin an avatar of hunger.
Colin says that going over his usual limit burns through the magic he feeds on and he must keep feeding on the vine to keep it up.
He devours a creature's remains and brings back a sample, and a bloody hand grows out of his bowl of leeches and meat to wave at Jason.
Shaped by Jason: Shade says Jason has shaped Colin and Gordon "like a parent".
Summoned: the doom essence ability Avatar of Doom summons a familiar.
At first it is unnamed, an iron-rank incorporeal familiar whose orbs make sustained beams, one of disruptive force and one of resonating force, and whose damage leaves Vulnerable.
Named: asked if it wants a name, it flashes its blue orb, and Jason says, "I'm going to call you... Gordon".
Orange is no and blue is yes: Gordon's orange orb flashes brightly as his signal for no.
Shade relays him: "Gordon says that I should be last".
Appearance: a disembodied cloak with a nebula-like cloud of blue and orange in the shape of an eye, and eyeball-patterned orbs drifting around it that fire unrelenting beams.
In a fight: his beams inflict Vulnerable on a lizard; his energy dash is fast but his reflexes are sluggish, and a blow can dissipate his vessel entirely.
Subsumed: while he is subsumed into Jason at silver rank, Jason can call up one of each orb to use for himself.
Shields: his orbs make shields that protect Jason.
Reputation: the Magic Society has only iron- and bronze-rank information on the "floating death orbs" and finds it terrifying.
Origin: he comes from the realm of the All-Devouring Eye.
The orrery: in Book 9 he draws a glowing orrery that looks like a solar system made of fireworks, a work he completes by floating down next to Jason.
The library: he spends months with some of Jason's avatars in the soul-realm library.
Intrinsic-mandate magic: Jason can reach it through Gordon, who executes the actual magic while Jason guides the authority with will.

Personality: he answers Colin with more flashing lights, sits next to Jason on the couch and sends an orb to absorb a portion of the juice, watches the film with his orbs and fights a flying dogfight with an enemy.
He detonates orbs to clear space for Jason.
Nature: Shade calls him a herald of annihilation.
Note that a different Gordon, a human, is called "Other Gordon" in Books 4 and 5 (: "Hanging Rock?" Other Gordon asked).
First sight: Onslow is at the front of Clive's airboat with his head jutting forward "like a dog with its head out a car window".
Clive sits on his shell with Jason beside him.
Powers: he fires elemental attacks from the magic runes on his shell, which Clive recharges with his own mana. A rune dims when he takes a hit.
A seat for the team: Clive picks up Stash and climbs on Onslow's shell with Neil, and the tortoise floats off the rooftop on a cushion of air.
Clive drops down off him when the tower is threatened.
Precaution: when a familiar tears open the side of a ship, Clive sends Onslow out as a precaution.
Power in a fight: he pours elemental magic into the enemy from his rune shell, throwing hailstones and lightning bolts.

Open-sided craft: he expands his shell into an open-sided flying craft, and the unshelled tortoise takes the form of a small green humanoid wearing a child's clothes from Clive, "an adorable team mascot".
Under fire: his shell draws constant barrage from the monsters, which Clive answers with ritual-enhanced wind barriers.
Humphrey tells Belinda to keep anyone from focusing on Onslow.
"Little buddy": Clive asks, "What do you say, little buddy? Can you get us down any faster?".

Bunker and command post: the shell serves as a bunker where Neil, Clive and Belinda work and where freed silver-rankers recover, and as the safest location of the expedition because it absorbs elemental attacks.
Carrier: it holds adventurers and brighthearts in an empty tunnel, and the team crosses overland in it with the sides open.
House-sized: in Book 13 the shell has expanded to the size of a house, serving as a combination command centre, rest area and triage tent.
Those who cannot fly ride in Onslow's expanded shell.
Plodding: when a child demands he go faster he plods over the grass on thick legs, to the child's complaint.
Friendly: he returns Neil's fist bump with a three-fingered fist.
The invigilator: he appears as the shadowy figure who runs the trials of the City of Fallen Echoes and offers to explain their practical dangers or their origins.
He hands out vials and medallions with his shadowy hands, which are cold to the touch.
A familiar before: he tells the competitors that the grandmaster who built the place was an outworlder with the dark essence like Jason, "I was his summoned familiar once".
Summoned by Jason: when Jason chooses to summon a familiar after the trials, he greets Shade with "I was hoping it would be you".
Bodies: he appears as three bodies that become horses for a ride or large lizards for rough terrain, and his bodies move among monsters as elusive shadowy figures.
The Reaper's child: the Reaper says "Of all my children, Shade has ever followed his own path".

He objects to "a decidedly indiscreet practice in the middle of the day", is told by Jason to "please show our guests out", and is described by Jason as "very nice" and "a good friend, even if he does occasionally keep things from me".
The Reaper's view: he tells Jason, "You have a habit of not staying dead. This is not something the Reaper likes. You have its gratitude, however".
Vehicles: he drives as a sports car and then a sleek four-door sedan, and drives a motorhome onto the water.
Jason calls him "the single greatest thing on this planet" when he arrives as the car.
A voice: his voice can come from Jason's shadow, as when he speaks for Jason in a meeting, and Jason can channel his sight and voice through him.
Jason compares talking through him to a better phone.
Silver rank: his bodies can teleport between each other.
Brother: Umber trapped him in an astral space for centuries; see../Umber.md.

Nature: Shade tells Jason that astral beings are things of spirit with defined natures, and that Colin was born an avatar of hunger, Gordon a herald of annihilation and he himself a shepherd of death.

Familiars develop personalities: he says astral beings are uniform until physical reality gives them idiosyncrasies, "that is the gift that mortals give us", and that Jason has shaped Colin and Gordon "like a parent".
A falling out: his previous summoner severed their bond and bound him to the place where he and Jason met, with Umber's interference.
Shade explains that Umber fixed on the idea that changing from the original state means falling from grace.
Sanctioning himself: Shade spends authority accumulated over tens of thousands of years, becomes a Shadow of the Hegemon, and accepts avatar status, which makes the familiar contract permanent.
The Reaper warns "Sanctioning can so easily go wrong".
Vehicles in the astral kingdom: his black skimmer is free of colour, and letting Colin and Gordon influence it would add defensive properties.
Size: Jason's gold-rank sheet lists Shadow of the Hegemon as three bodies at iron, seven at bronze, thirty-one at silver and two hundred and eleven at gold.
Summoned: the final ability of Belinda's power set is a summoned familiar, an astral lantern. Belinda names it: "How about Shimmer?".
In a fight: it projects shields to protect the team and, with Gordon, beams the enemy to split their attention.
The force bolts of a lantern familiar prove more dangerous to its own side against Hendren's defences.
Mana supply: against constructs its attacks do little, so it mostly replenishes mana.
At the battle of Yaresh it fires force bolts at worms and pumps out mana to the team.
Pairing: Belinda's other familiar replicates Humphrey, swinging a huge sword.
Rapid-fire bolts: its force bolts are as effective as Gordon's beams against flaming and gaseous elementals.
Echo spirit: Belinda's two summoned familiars are the astral lantern, which orbits her droopily, and an echo spirit that looks like a blurry version of her.
Name: "It's short for Velitraxistaasch. He likes 'Stash,' though.".
Jason works out what he is at once and Humphrey is startled.
Bond: "Our mothers arranged him becoming my familiar. Or me becoming his person, depending on how you look at it".
A bonded familiar is an actual magical creature that can die, unlike a summoned familiar.
Shapes: a canary on Humphrey's head and a puppy, a bird that swoops from the sky and turns into a puppy in his arms, a barking lizard, and a bark lurker or a darting bird in a fight.
Biscuits: Jason feeds him a biscuit and he turns into a puppy to snuffle it from Jason's hand, then yaps his agreement.
Speech: "Stash chase worm! Stash chase worm!".
Scouting: he leads Humphrey's party by barking in the right direction to the margolls.
Special attack: Humphrey's racial ability evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon.
Mother: his mother is Carlivexistrix, a vast dragon with scales of changing rainbow colours who asks to be called Carli.
Humphrey apologises for not doing the best job of helping her little boy grow up.
Language: "Porky pies!" and "Stick it up your bum, lady" at a Magic Society official, and "Telling people to bugger off is kind of my thing".
With Sophie: he is sprawled in Sophie's lap in puppy form, and she keeps biscuits for him.
Forms in battle: a marsh hydra, a copy of Belinda and then of Jason, and a hopping insect that pulls Neil out of a messenger's path.
Given a task: Jason tells him to stick to the messengers and keep them safe.
Team Biscuit: asked whether a familiar picked the team name, someone answers "Actually, yes, they did".
Size and strength: he is a giant who smashes Dustin and Rick together, impaling messengers.
In Book 11 the text calls him "boy Stash", who demands "Faster!".
Bird-lizard: he leaps from Humphrey's clothes as something between a bird and a lizard.
A clerk at the Adventure Society who introduces himself as Albert and says his brother was Bertram, "feel free to just call me Bert"; he records Jason's contracts at the jobs hall.
He mentions the lumber mill owner's fergax complaint and later remarks on the fate of Jason's early captors.
Deputy director of the Adventure Society branch, an elf who looks uncharacteristically aged for a silver-ranker.
She meets Jason and Elspeth in a black parlour in Book 2.
A cultist who loudly demands worship in the Vane estate ("the magic of Darryl Caruthers") and says "I'm the Darryl".
In Book 12 a Darryl among the Earth refugees ranked up without cores and grows naturally powerful; the text checked does not state they are the same man, and a High Priest Darryl lies dead in.
The Duke of Greenstone's brother, Thalia's husband and Thadwick's father, who facilitated a Mercer scheme and raised Thadwick himself.
Jason notes in Book 10 that the Builder cult's Beaufort shares his name but not his villainy.
Dean Tuckell is an iron-rank adventurer who summons monsters at the Clementson mill for Thadwick Mercer.
Clementson is the mill owner, a normal-rank man.
Kyle Lindover, the leonid mill owner, is the victim of the fergax contract.
The landlady of the Greenstone inn where Jason lodges, who berates a tall man in scholar's robes in her lounge.
Jason calls her "a small business owner who works very hard to run a quality establishment".
By Book 12 she finds second-tier adventurers the perfect clientele for long-term tenancy.
Jory's teenage receptionist and assistant at his shop. Jason pleads with her for crystal wash.
A Janice manages a patisserie in Vitesse in Book 11; the text does not say she is the same person.
A Geller team leader who looks like Humphrey, with the same height and broad shoulders; Jason does not assume a close relation.
He makes a "teaching moment" of his team's choices, leads the team at the sand barge battle and later guards Jonah Geller.
The burly thug adventurer, toughest of those Thadwick Mercer took under his auspices; he fights with a spiked sphere on a chain and is quietly struck off the Adventure Society roll afterwards.
A guardian-type who conjures heavy armour and a huge shield, added to a party with Jory in the Reaper trials and then to Jason's party.
A short, stocky runic man, blue-black skin with glowing markings, whom Jason asks about the temples of the Divine Square; he explains "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles".
When Hero appears he drops to his knees and drags at Jason's sleeve to make him kneel.
In Book 12 an Arash, whose nephew Jamar is a bartender, has "never been further than Hornis, down south".
An Old City thug who tries to beat Jason, certain he is weak: "that Geller lady set up a fight so you could beat all her fancy trainees... the whole thing was rigged, and really you're weak".
One of his companions doubts him after feeling Jason's aura.
A man "of late-middle years", shorter than Jason with a barrel chest and ropy muscle, who watches the aperture that is the source of the waterfall and guides Jason up the track.
He has a might essence that "makes me strong".
Emir Bahadir's granddaughter, the child of his dead son; she was raised by her grandmother, "not a woman of means", and never sought Emir out for money.
Emir greets her warmly and says she will "get the best of everything".
Arabelle says she got her essences so young she has been waiting longer than most to go out into the world: "She's full of rebellious ideas".
A stern Adventure Society official, plain in dress apart from her black Adventure Society pin, who leads the inquiry team into the Greenstone events.
She is the de facto head of the Society while the inquiry lasts and chairs the meeting on the Builder cult's next moves.
The Mercer family butler, in "uncharacteristic panic" when Thadwick is missed.
Thalia has him gather the team tracking Thadwick.
A thirty-one-year-old Melbourne detective sergeant who "looked like a detective from a TV show", investigating the missing chunk of Jason's apartment building.
A woman with a swelling presence offers him the answers: "come work for us".
By Book 6 he is "a former detective and a former EOA member", an ordinary man among powerful company.
The Storm Kingdom's ambassador to Estercost, a silver-ranker who used to adventure with his friend Orin, who went on to travel with Asano.
An upper-echelon member of House Headingway, one of Estercost's pre-eminent families, who is held in a suppression collar in Sadi Andali.
A different Garret leads a superhero team in Book 5.
The chief membership officer of a guild in Cyrion who deals with Jason and is not on the guild master's side.
A pirate rabble-rouser aboard Jota Withers's ship who plots against him and wants to return to Jakaar triumphant.
A Voice of the Will serving a minor astral king who is secretly one of the Unorthodoxy's rare astral kings.
Director of the Adventure Society's Cyrion branch, in one of the organisation's most political posts, who confronts Danielle after the System's withdrawal message.
The CIA director who briefs the international group on Pakistan and Jason.
A monster-core user from Gormanston's aristocratic faction, confronted by Marcus over who keeps Adventure Society membership after the messenger invasion.
Director of the Network's Geneva branch.
She is the only silver-ranker among the gold-rankers Jason fights on the flying bus and accuses Bussinger of turning traitor.
A gold-rank messenger in the Cardinas zone alongside Galis Jay Vahal.
Belinda's hidden circle leaves her badly hurt.
Director of the Office of External Affairs in Yaresh, who insists on being addressed "Lord Bynes" at all times.
Arabelle pointedly invites him through a portal to see messengers for himself; Allayeth says he lacks the perception his rank should give.
A silver-rank messenger, unhappy that she has been placed on the chopping block; she was "born" at her rank limit and is too unimportant to be caught between Jes Fin Kaal and Jason.
She fought during the attack on Yaresh and knows "the lesser races had members that weren't so lesser at all".

Deputy to Lenora Coleman at the Australian artefact site; he phones the Minister for Supernatural Affairs from the Asano Circle's monitoring station and appears as deputy director in Book 12 and Book 13.

A priest of Dominion who greets Ben Headingway, leads him into a plain tent with an altar and kneeling mats, and explains that his church does not venerate power itself, "but the establishment of power over others". See the Church of Dominion file.
A new, competent and frazzled assistant to Lenora and Barry at the artefact site.
A troll were-crocodile from the rainforests of Far North Queensland and the only Earth outworlder who is not an essence user; he is aligned with the Cabal.
He grows more powerful naturally and wants to be near Asano and his team.
In Book 13 he is in the Cabal contingent led by Boris, with Koa.
A young silver Welsh adventurer with the Global Defence Network, whose childhood hero was the man she saw fighting monsters on television.
Her set is Gun, Swift, Trap and Skirmish, built around laying traps, and she holds a stand while her team runs.
Jason later gives her a System window for her soul and the title Resolute.
A brightheart militia member in Rexion who enjoys portal duty, "the most coveted posting in the militia".
Her aura senses are a little stronger than most brighthearts', and she joins the militia after feeling a protection go away, though she has little talent for combat.
The young bartender on Jason's cloud ship, Arash's nephew; Jason warns him the job will be "danger adjacent" and pays him well for discretion.
A Māori Earth refugee, a friend of Darryl, who rides a stormspire drake and has the Absorb Electricity power; he offers Jason a lift: "Can you fly, or will you need a piggyback or something?".
A diamond-rank arbiter who arrives at Jason's cloud palace and feels threatened by it for the first time in a long time; he tells Jason "you may call me Van".
The top gold-ranker of House Headingway, who speaks for the noble houses of Cyrion. See House_Headingway.md.
A bronze-rank Network operative suited to quiet scouting rather than combat.
An older Network category four with "aggravating shield powers" who goes into the Slovakia dome with Gerling and two Chinese category fours; he kills anomalies fast with beak-like finger strikes.
The government representative at the negotiations with Jason, a man with no magic.
In Book 11 he snatches a phone and says he is onsite and taking command of operations.
In Book 13 he is said to need the publicity.
Deputy Director of the Network and Gerling's handler, angry that Jason escaped Berlin.
Gerling says he is better than past handlers who treated him like a monster in a pit.
A silver-rank (category three) Earth healer who gives her name to Jason's team; in 2038 she treats Nanna's Alzheimer's and lectures with Neil.
A Belgian official of the International Committee who runs the Saint-Étienne operation.
A different Hector appears in Book 9 among those intimidated by the royal family.
A silver-ranker with 94 percent core taint and the territory claimant in the Saint-Étienne zone.
A category-three member of the capture team that hunts Jason through a large city in Book 5; his light essence gives him the speed to keep up and the aura to light the slum town.
Jason's aura stops his dead, and Jason ends the fight with a threat to his soul.
The head of the security team at the base where Travis is put in charge of the Special Munition Stockpile Division. Jason says she gives off an Anisa vibe.
A silver-rank dino-man who chose his own name, leading almost thirty dino-monsters through the Makassar proto-space in search of the unknown being behind the rainbow smoke.
He loses control of them as Jason's afflictions spread.
A bronze-rank vampire who fights beside Craig Vermillion and Franklin and calls himself the Night Stalker; Farrah threatens to put him down for it.
A member of Nigel Thornton's team who, with Darcy and Jonno, takes and gives the big hits.
He conjures a shield and prefers Higgy to "Captain America".
He is still with the team in Book 12, steering a conversation back on topic, and in Book 13 calls "CONTACT!" as the squad guards Itsuki.
A peaceful Cabal vampire who "did not share the ambitions of many others in the Cabal" and spends as little time in the transformation zone as his role requires.
He declined Craig Vermillion's invitation to leave and bitterly regrets it.
He later fights beside Vermillion as a bronze-rank vampire.

A diamond-rank member of the Rimaros royal house who oversees checks of the most prestigious visitors, stands by the throne with Soramir and with Soramir smashes the defences of an aristocratic house that protested. A speaker refers to her as "Aunt Zila".
Baseph is Liara's husband, silver rank.
He hammers a pipe to draw raiders in a trap and holds Liara's hand under the table.
Their children are Dara (eldest), Zareen (middle) and Joseph (youngest and only son), all silver.
Liara's husband's cousin "Gibbie", originally of the Amouz family, who managed an underwater mining operation.
He is held by the Purity order and freed, and by Book 9 floats unconscious in a containment tank for recovery.
Proprietor of the tailor shop Sensual Attire for the Sensual Gentleman in Rimaros, with formidable society connections; he adjusts the formalwear for the celebration ball.
A priest named Aldrich "Al" Albericci appears in Book 7; the relation is not stated.
An information broker who owns a building through layers of paperwork.
In Book 9 he promises Killian Laurent for a price and is carried off unconscious.
An adventurer Jason met before reaching Rimaros, with a frog essence and a frog familiar ritual.
Familiars: she mourns her bonded companion and finds a new familiar, a long-tongue jumping hydra the size of a two-storey house that is closer to the frog-like end of the scale.
A valash outworlder in Yaresh with a silver-rank aura and no core use, later held in the campus prison.

Members named in Book 8: Sendira, Fila and Ramona, all women, Ramona once a celestine; Rhett and Jaime, silver-rank members who stand apart from the compelled majority; Caitlyn, Heston, Marika and Elise, who challenge Melody Jain; Kelleigh, Melody's cell member; Laront, an ordinary Purity priest who never passed the flames.
A Ramona on Miriam Vance's team, Moon's Edge, is a different person unless the text says otherwise.
Caitlyn's group thinks pain purifies the soul.
The commander of a fort, a minor local lord and a silver-rank core user, who watches the first shab fall to the town's defences with little joy. Melody Jain works on his sympathies.
He has sunk favours and most of his surge earnings into it and hired a costly tracker and an Adventure Society communications official.
Shade judges his team the best prepared of the hunters.
Two team leaders hunting Jason in the jungle.
Rangel admits he stole Maldonado's plan, and Jason takes four people from his group.
A healer in Rangel's party, told to cleanse a poisoned teammate before Jason drags him into the scrub.
A thug and loan collector in Yaresh who kicks Jason on the floor while Bellory fetches the repayment.
He is silver rank and pushes past others in a crisis.
A tournament duellist of House de Varco and sometime adventurer, well known in the mirage arenas, who is touchy about being called a coward.
An arrogant silver-team member who announces "I am Argrave Mericulato, son of Ramon Mericulato. You think you can talk to me like that?" and storms out when Jason suppresses his aura.
In Book 9 an Adventure Society functionary of that name pushes a food trolley in the secure residence building, hiding "seething anger" at his menial work behind an aura mask.

A man who introduces himself in a rumbling voice and sees through Jason at once; he says "the most powerful in any given region are relatively few in number and immortal, so we all meet eventually" and that Shade can guide Jason to Interstice once he reaches diamond.
Liara and Baseph's eldest child, a one-star adventurer happy to hunt monsters, with Liara's height, Baseph's dark copper hair and eyes and a muscular frontline build.
Her later remark about "the one from up north" with the elf twins refers to Rick. See Baseph_and_the_Rimaros_Children.md.
The order's church advisor, a young-looking human priest of Purity who never passed through the flames, so he can visit cities safely.
He buys information from an Adventure Society functionary and says "I am the church's eyes".
A gold-rank adventurer who has seen more of the order's operation than Melody and Laront like.
A cell leader who says Melody advances her personal agenda and risks the order's assets; she warns that most of their forces will be lost.

A blank-faced, dedicated member of Melody's cell who delivers a prisoner and quotes resonating-force siege weapons.
Beth's cousin and teammate, who asks Jason questions about where he comes from and enters the Adventure Society looking flustered. A bolt hits him in the Ustei fight.
A smoulder with dark skin, glowing red eyes and jet-black hair who throws iron harpoons and has fire and iron powers with a size buff.

Yumi Asano, Jason's paternal grandmother, whose flesh-warping powers restored her youth; she looks no older than her mid-twenties.

Jason's other grandmother, his mother's mother, is seen "chugging a beer" beside Yumi and had a miraculous recovery that sets his mother's thoughts racing.
Ken Asano, Jason's father, was born in Japan and raised in Australia from a very young age.
His brothers are the elder Shiro, "the favourite", and Hiro, "the disappointment"; Ken "laid low in the middle".
Cheryl Asano, Jason's mother, comes from a farming and mining family and was the one fascinated with Japan. Her brother is Robert.
Kaito is Jason's older brother by a year; Erika is the older sister. Jason is the youngest of the three.
Kaito married Amy, the girl next door, who is Jason's childhood best friend.
Their daughters are Hana (twenty-three in 2038) and Jace (nineteen). Kaito dies in Book 5.
Erika married Ian Evans, a doctor; their daughter is Emi, twelve in Book 4.

Nik, the rabbit Jason brought into being when his soul realm became a transformation zone, calls Jason "Dad".
Families brought into the clan through Jason's circle include those of Greg and Asya and Chloe Baudrillard's.
Its patriarch is a silver-rank man named Shiro, father of Akari; Jason's own eldest paternal uncle is also named Shiro, a different man.
Its strongest member is Noriko, the patriarch's mother.
Jason tells her "My Asano family and your Asano clan henceforth have no connections".
Akari married Itsuki Tiwari of the Tiwari clan; his father is Koya, youngest of three elders.
Book 12 calls Noriko "matriarch of the Asano clan" while Yumi is also called matriarch; the two descriptions are not reconciled.

Gabriel and Arabelle are husband and wife; Roland is Arabelle's father-in-law.
Their sons are Gwydion, the older, a priest of Hero, and Rufus.
Arabelle once said "I think it's time for another child, husband. A daughter, this time".
Danielle Geller and Keith Geller are husband and wife; their children are Henrietta, the older sister, and Humphrey.
Rick and Phoebe are brother and sister of a distant branch; Phoebe is a distant cousin of Humphrey.
Jonah Geller was Rick's cousin, whom he failed to save.
Henry Geller is also named on Rick's team.
Dustin Kettering replaced Jonah on Rick's team and is cousin to Hudson Kettering.
Rick married Hannah Adeah.
Beaufort Mercer is the Duke of Greenstone's brother and Thalia Mercer is his wife, a silver-rank adventurer.
Their children are Cassandra and Thadwick; Cassandra is the older.
Thalia "looked more like her daughter's sister than her parent".
Neil Davone grew up in the Mercer orbit because the Davone and Kettering families had close ties to the Mercers.
Soramir Rimaros is the founder; even the Storm King defers to him.
The Storm King's firstborn daughter is Zara, the Hurricane Princess.
Her brother Emiliano becomes Storm King; the notes for Book 13 call him her adopted cousin-brother.
Zara later adopts into her mother's House Nareen.
Vesper Rimaros is Zara's aunt and is sixty-seven.
Liara Rimaros comes from "one of the more remote branches of the royal family".
She married Baseph, born into House Amouz.
Their children are Dara, Zareen and Joseph.
Liara calls Cassin Amouz "Uncle Cassin" when angry.
Pelli is "Aunt Pelli" to Vesper; the text does not say she is a blood relative.

Book 13's present is 2038: a character asks how not knowing a kids' show in 2038 can be un-Australian.
If Jason left Earth in autumn 2021 and has been gone sixteen years, his return falls around 2037 to 2038, which agrees with the dated line.
Earth and Pallimustus run at the same rate. The two universes are linked and their time-space is synchronised.
Jason left Earth in late November and returned in early June, a year and a half later.
His birthday is 1 April ("April Fool's Day"); he has just turned 26 in Book 5.
He was 23 at arrival, 29 in Book 10, and was born forty-four years before the Book 12 Earth scenes.
Book 13 is set in 2038, and mentions transformation-zone events "like those in 2020".

A Book 12 speaker says the priests Jason freed were released "around twenty years ago now" and another says "it's been almost twenty years", which fits Book 2 at about M5 (April 2018) and the Pallimustus part of Book 12 in late 2037 or early 2038.
Ranks: iron within the first days, bronze around M15, silver in Book 5 (about M28-29), gold by Book 12 ("how you got to gold rank", notes, Book 12).
