claim: Five years before Book 7: the monster surge, normally due about every ten years, is "some five years overdue" when Book 7 begins.
(An earlier version of this document said fifteen years; that figure applies instead to the Church of Knowledge building up fighting forces "over the last fifteen years or so",.) (Level 2)
Earlier on Earth: in 1948 local Network operatives discovered the anomalous incursion space near Saint-Étienne, and that sector of the grid has been offline for about seventy years.
The Engineers of Ascension take Perth about two years before Book 4's scene, Melbourne a year later, and are pushing into Sydney.
Network partnerships with governments and militaries have been in place "over the last few years" before the monster waves of Book 5.

1 — Greenstone, the Vane Estate, the first astral space — M0 to about M4 (late Nov 2017 to about spring 2018) — Arrival in late November; the Leust conspiracy runs summer into autumn — Book_01_Timeline.md
2 — Greenstone, Sky Scar Lake and the City of Fallen Echoes — from about M4 to about M6 — "About four months" — Book_02_Timeline.md

3 — Greenstone, the veldt, the Builder's ship — winter of M6 to M7 until the death at about M15 to M16 — "A few months more than a year"; the farewell is more than a month after the memorial — Book_03_Timeline.md
4 — Earth: Australia, Saint-Étienne — early June 2019 to about September 2019 — Return to Earth "early June" — Book_04_Timeline.md

5 — Earth: grid failures, Broken Hill, Makassar, Kostroma — about March 2020 to about October 2020 — "Nine months" back; the birthday on 1 April; Kaito's funeral in an Australian winter — Book_05_Timeline.md
6 — Earth: the Nitra dome, the French zone, farewell — about October 2020 to a warm autumn day in 2021 — French domain six months old; farewell on a warm autumn day — Book_06_Timeline.md
7 — Rimaros: arrival, surge, Builder invasion — autumn 2021 to about January 2022 — Outworlders arrive together; a month since the war — Book_07_Timeline.md
8 — Rimaros: the end of the surge — about January to April 2022 — Chapter order; the six-day week — Book_08_Timeline.md
9 — The road to Yaresh and the battle — about April 2022 to no later than about early 2023 — Rimaros left "half a year" back; the monsoon road of four months — Book_09_Timeline.md
10 — Yaresh, Cardinas, the Death Pact — weeks after Yaresh, then the expedition, spring to mid 2023 — Jason is 29; the third week of adventuring — Book_10_Timeline.md

11 — The transformation zone, then the long epilogue in the void and on Earth — from mid 2023 (zone of months), then years — Zone less than two weeks old; Nik six months old; Gary "almost a year later" — Book_11_Timeline.md

12 — Pallimustus tour (late 2037 to early 2038), then the Earth arrival and the pirate battle at Dimensional Artefact Site One (2038) — about fifteen years after Jason left — "Fifteen years"; "twenty years" since the arrival; "seventeen years" — Book_12_Timeline.md
13 — Earth in 2038 — 2038 — "2038"; "sixteen years" gone — Book_13_Timeline.md
Jason's death in the Builder's tower — M18 — about M15 to M16 —;. The M18 figure belongs to the return to Earth
Book 2 start — M5 — about M4 —
Kaito's death — M36 — about M30 to M31 (about June 2020) —
Departure from Earth — M45 to M49 — autumn 2021 —
Battle of Yaresh — "M58, about 2022" — no later than about early 2023 — (Jason is 29 so after 1 April 2023) with "a few weeks"
Cardinas zone — "nine months" — months; Gary's divine power "four to eight months", Nik six months old — Book 11
Book 12 "now" — "M-count" — Earth arrival 2038: "seventeen years ago" and "forty-four years ago" —
A year has twelve months of thirty days plus five extra days.
The week is six days.
Earth and Pallimustus run at the same rate, so Earth dates can be laid beside Pallimustus events.
Gary — Hero's Cup in Book 10, the zone in Book 11, the sword line "six years", reincarnation in Book 13. See../07_Characters/Gary.md

Emi and Nik — Book 4 reveal to Erika and Ian first, Book 5 birthday party the evacuation day, Nik created by the zone in Book 11, gold by Book 13. See../07_Characters/Emi_Evans_Asano.md and../07_Characters/Nik_Asano.md
Boris — Introduced in Book 10, the Earth side of Book 11, the Cabal's open leader by the end. See../07_Characters/Boris_Ket_Lundi.md
The Cosmic Throne — Sundered long ago, met in Book 11 (Ch64), restored with the throne left empty, matters through Book 13. See../02_Cosmology_and_Powers/Gods_and_Churches.md
Resolved - surge delay: "some five years overdue", not fifteen.
Resolved - Book 5 opening: nine months after the June 2019 return, about March 2020.
Open - Emi's age against the sword line: Emi is "fifteen years old" when Rufus and Taika arrive; she was thirteen in spring 2020, so fifteen fits late 2022 to early 2023.
But "six years since you first gave it to me" and Jason's age of 29 place the departure in late 2023 or later, and Emi is "nineteen" later. Not resolved here.

Narrowed - Book 12 present: the Pallimustus chapters fit late 2037 to early 2038 by their roundings, and the Earth arrival is best placed in 2038 because Lenora counts seventeen years from the Earthlings' vanishing and Jota gives Jason's age as forty-four. Book 13 is dated 2038.
Narrowed - vampire war length: Book 13 gives "decades" and "a decade" for the initiative and the team's monster fighting.
The renewed war is placed "two years" in at (see Book_13_Timeline.md).

The clan "had not been heard from in two years" at the end of Book 11, "half a decade" at the opening of Book 12, and the city of Nitra shows "more than a decade of abandonment" by the Book 12 arrival.
Open - public reveal of magic: "Less than fifteen years ago, no one knew magic existed" against "twenty years ago"; likely different counting points.

Jason's death count is settled by Books 5-10: apartment (first), the Builder's tower (second, Book 3), the Dinosaur King at Makassar (third, Book 5), Shako (fourth, Book 6), shown by the Church of Death's certificate in Book 7.
The journey: the trip will take "about four months"; the convoy stays at Rajoras for a few days and clears Cartise's ruins on the way.

Orders from Knowledge: a priest of the Church of Knowledge tells Humphrey's team to follow the Adventure Society's orders for a couple of weeks, after which the church will requisition them for the main conflict.
Clive says Knowledge's forces are mobilising.
Yaresh: the walls are a line of massive trees with glossy black stone between.
Jason says "See you in two weeks" and returns to the city's defence. Hana Shavar runs the refugee camp.
The messengers: the messenger architecture is obsessed with circles; Jes Fin Kaal, the Voice of the Will, leads them.
Messenger agents in the city: Benella presents Jason to Kaal as a threat; Fal Vin Garath calls Shade "Reaper spawn".

Apocalypse beasts and worms: Carlos suspects a heat-consuming parasite with a swarm hive mind; "[Inexorable Doom] on [World-Taker Worm]"; the messengers know the apocalypse beasts and use them as weapons (Book 9, Ch62).
Defence plans: the two cloud palaces are reconfigured into defence bunkers; Hana directs the clergy away from Jason's bunker.
The trigger: an Adventure Society functionary hides his anger behind an aura mask; a naga egg is triggered in the city (see../../06_Places/Yaresh.md).
The breach: Marek Nior Vargas leads the breach force over the entertainment district; the breach is a trap.
Eilaf Hayel commands the defence of the entertainment district.
Intervention: Raythe tells Schaat "Leave Asano be. Turn around and leave this city"; Schaat is found dead.
The duel: Tera Jun Casta challenges Jason; Jason's last word stops her dead.
The end: the command council advises withdrawal; Marek orders his people in and later asks Jason to wait.
In the weeks following the battle, countless tons of rubble are repurposed to rebuild the city.
Jason's team: the convoy, Taika and Zara among them; Rufus, Sophie and Jason as mobile responders.
Messengers: Kaal, Marek, Hess Jor Nasala, Fal Vin Garath, Tera; their astral king is Vesta Carmis Zell.
The wider world: Knowledge's army gathering; Dawn's recording supplies the real list of auxiliaries.
Known by the end: a healer realises Jason is a silver-rank astral king.

sec: 2. The world at the start (Book 2, about M3 to M5)
claim: Where things stand: Jason is an iron-ranker in Greenstone; Farrah has just died covering civilians; the Adventure Society campus holds "a continual series of memorial services".

sec: 2. The world at the start (Book 2, about M3 to M5)
claim: The first sign: Cassandra says her brother Thadwick "woke up different"; Henry Geller is among the missing faces.

sec: 2. The world at the start (Book 2, about M3 to M5)
claim: A Continental Council inquiry team arrives.

sec: 2. The world at the start (Book 2, about M3 to M5)
claim: Rumours in the upper crust about Jonah, Thadwick and the others disrupt Greenstone's aristocracy.

The star seed: Danielle, Emir, Thalia, Arella and the archbishop of Purity witness Jonah Geller's death; the archbishop says a star seed was implanted in the boy and that star seeds are creations of entities that exist only in the deep astral.
Clive says he has simulated the enemy's goal: to reinforce an astral space and sever it from the world.
The enemy's shape: clockwork kings are creatures native to the world the Builder created, which make clockwork cores for constructs.

Aristocrats in the cult: Thalia reports that three star-seed survivors are awake with limited recollection; a hooded cultist posing as the foreman follows a woman, and the archbishop rebukes the cult's failures.
Guards have stood at Thadwick's door for weeks.

While the iron-rankers are away: in Greenstone, Thalia is uneasy because most iron-rankers left a few days earlier; in the Mercers' underground black parlour, Timos berates Thadwick, whose use as an infiltrator is at an end.
The strike: a small force of three gold-rankers, six silvers and a dozen bronzes, including Gabriel and Arabelle Remore, hits the cult's island; Timos runs for the nearest portal device.
Evacuation: Zato, the last silver-ranker in the cult's local forces, leads the survivors off the island.
Jason's capture: Cole Silva and Lucian Lamprey orchestrate Jason's kidnapping and star seed implantation; he is held in a stone box, emaciated and bloodied.
The war council: Jason's team and allies meet as a war council for the anti-Builder effort.
Into the astral space: the team arrives on one of twelve portal towers ringing the city; a legendary-set site is a subterranean forge.
The church of Purity arrives at the Vane estate through a portal, fifty-eight in all.
Hendren dissolves under transcendent light.
The truth of the place: Clive says the astral space is artificial, "a giant boarding vessel".
The ending: the Builder grabs Jason by the face; Zato is defeated; the Builder, the World-Phoenix and the Reaper negotiate.
Jason's soul is vouchsafed on his death.
Jason: iron in Book 2, bronze by Book 3; dies at the climax (Book 3, Ch69).
Humphrey, Clive, Sophie, Belinda, Neil: the team that enters the astral space with him.
The cult: Zato, Timos, Thadwick, Dougall and the abandoned vessel the Builder takes up.
Purity: the archbishop Nicolas Hendren and the priestess Anisa Lasalle, with fifty-eight others at the Vane estate.
Greenstone's powers: Thalia Mercer and Danielle Geller; Elspeth Arella; the Duke; Adris Dorgan as the effective mayor of Old City.
Known to Jason's team: the cult exists, star seeds, and the aim to seal an astral space.
After the battle: Yaresh is rebuilding, the messengers are Jason's captives, and the Adventure Society is deciding whether to revoke his membership.
The device: the messengers give Jason a device that is meant to turn the natural array into a soul forge; Clive says the messengers want this and cannot do it alone because the place corrupts them.
Allies: Musin Heath presides at the meetings; Marcus Xenoria names Jason operations commander; the gold-rank participants include Amos, Carlos and Hana Shavar.
The descent: Jason and Kaal go over the operation to descend the access shaft.
Brightheart stone-shapers guide thousands into switchback queues for the portal.
Cardinas: ruled from the Citadel of Pillars; Beaufort heads the Builder cult's forces as an uneasy ally.
Lorenn says the citadel chamber is the site of the echo array.
Undeath: Garth Larosse, a priest of Undeath about nine feet tall.
Death appears as a stocky, middle-aged woman in a colourful dress and names the pact "Death Pact: The Sanctity of Death".
Hero: Gary greets "Lord Hero"; a divine forge golem stands over twice Gary's height.
Gary and the avatar stare at each other like kaiju.
The tree: the birthing tree is the result of a failed attempt to create a soul forge.
Clive and Farrah overlook the ring of ritual circles round the tree.
A third zone: Jason's third transformation zone, unified by claiming all non-central territories.
A replica of Casselton Beach occupies one.
Battles: the Undeath priests fall quickly; Garth throws off his robes (Book 11, Ch24-26); Jason fights him in a warped castle (Book 11, Ch30-31).
Factions: each faction has Builder cultists, Undeath priests or brighthearts leading messengers.
Lorus Durrum tries to reconcile the Builder cult and the brighthearts.
Territory holding follows Lorenn's rules.
Nik: a four-foot humanoid rabbit Jason brings into being when his soul realm becomes a zone; he is "six months old" in the zone and calls the structure a weather machine, not a satellite weapon.
Boris: reveals himself as Unorthodoxy and tells the astral-king story; he says the process to become an astral king takes years.
Gary: drank from the Cup of Heroes; Jason offers to replace the divine power.
Reintegration: Jason separates the natural array, the soul forge and the tree and claims the forge.
The forest city has a soul of its own, like Nik.
Lorenn gathers her people in the new brightheart home.
The Cosmic Throne: Velius says the throne must be left empty as a neutral arbiter.
Departure: Boris can take two people to Earth, Taika among them.
Jason in the zone, leaving his body in a cloud chair during soul battles.
The team: Humphrey, Sophie, Clive, Belinda, Neil, Gary, Rufus, Taika and Farrah; Zara, Dustin, Korinne and Moon's Edge.
Local forces: Lorenn and the brighthearts; Miriam Vance as co-commander.
Earth: the clan holds two domains, Saint-Étienne and near Nitra.
Known: the soul forge is the third part of an astral kingdom; Boris is Unorthodoxy.

Reality cores as fuel: some Cabal upper echelons work on imbuing blood with the power of reality cores; Craig says the cores will only last so long, and "once they can't make any more of this, the old ones will go back to sleep".
Occupation: Russia and Europe suffer massive vampiric occupation.
Jason's approach: Farrah says cutting off the supply of cores will save more lives than killing vampires now.
Saint-Étienne: Elizabeth, Klaus and Georges choose to join Jason's side in the second zone; Elizabeth pairs her ritual magic with Mr North's against the vorger. The vampires later abandon France.
Skirmishes: a war of skirmishes between elite forces began in earnest shortly after Jason left.

Elizabeth and the détente: she leads the vampires and establishes a détente with the world; every major city hides vampires; bombings in Europe are answered by assassinations in Beijing, Washington, Moscow and London.
Humanity tries to kill her with a sunlight device based on Travis's design.
Jason's purge (Book 12): the most powerful vampires got that way by consuming blood infused with stolen reality-core power.
Jason removes the remnants and liberates a blood farm inside his domain, though one outside it is beyond his reach.
Nigel's team is embedded in France watching the edge of Saint-Étienne.
Ketevan shows Anna the cleaned-up French domain.
The war resumes (Book 13): Anna says the vampire war has resumed and military forces operate out of Asano territory again.
A symposium debates whether untested procedures on vampires violate the Saint-Étienne Summit Accords.

Marie Finnegan and McKean: investigators find Finnegan ran a tight operation with Elizabeth and McKean; Gerling opens a box on Elizabeth's order and is speared by a red tentacle. McKean takes Gerling from the queen.

The offensives: the offensive against Belgrade, the largest European city under full vampire control, begins with bombardment and a drop of enhanced soldiers; Prince Valdis lands with the paratroopers. Multan is infiltrated by Nigel's team.
McKean's castle: the facility grafts vampire flesh onto blood oaks; the blood vine revives the undead. The last vampire lord is killed.
Vampires: Elizabeth, Klaus, Georges; Gerling as her blood slave; McKean's vampire-magitech abominations.
Known: the vampires' power comes from reality-core blood and ends with a supply cut.
Blood farms outside Jason's domain, a queen who treats humans strategically, vampire-flesh experiments, and a diplomatic web that wants the war to end.
Jason wakes on Earth in early June, a year and a half after he left.
The era ends with Jason leaving Earth, in a warm French autumn.
Where Jason is: a maternity theatre in an abandoned hospital at Casselton West, with Shade's bodies merged into a car. He is bronze.
What has changed: a "gas explosion" in his Melbourne building and the army running "terrorist response exercises" cover the magic.
Earth's magic desolation slows his recovery.

The factions: the Network, a Cabal front man in Sydney, and the Engineers of Ascension, whom Vermillion calls those who came to magic from outside the normal channels. The EOA has seized Perth and Melbourne.
Contact: Hiro at the Stone Wall bar in Kings Cross; Anna Tilden and Ketevan Arziani of the Network (Book 4, Ch5; Book 4, Ch21).
Jason's coins left on Anna's counter are authentic category-one coins marked PRODUCT OF JASON.
The Starlight Rider: the media name for his cloaked figure.
Family: he says "Hello, Eri", reveals magic to Emi, and tells Kaito he has waited six years to say what he says.
The Saint-Étienne rescue: a French branch hides the Dimensional Fortress, an incursion space found in 1948; Jason frees Farrah from it (Book 4, Ch53).
Dawn's explanation: the link between worlds has been siphoning magic from Pallimustus for centuries, and Purity has struck a bargain with the Builder.

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: Setting: Jason has been home nine months and bronze for a year.

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: The family compound went up in six months.

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: The waves: the first recorded monster manifestation is in Angola.

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: Broken Hill is hit; the safe-zone claim is blamed.

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: Jason's broadcast: "If you want to find heroes, go digging through the rubble".

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: Japan: the old Asano clan's compound in Ashiya, near Kobe, and Noriko's challenge (Book 5, Ch36-37).

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: Transformation events: Kostroma first; reality cores become the prize (see../../09_Items_and_Artefacts/Reality_and_Genesis_Cores.md).

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: Vampires: ancient vampires rise using blood infused with reality-core energy.

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: The Berlin attack kills Kaito, Asya and Greg.

sec: Book 5: the waves and the compound
claim: Silver: Jason ranks to silver.
Nitra: a dome appears; Jason opens a door and claims territories, renaming the first Arrival Pagoda. 1,327 stable genesis cores are consumed in his apotheosis.
Shako: a red-haired, freckled man with bright green eyes kills Jason; Dawn tells him he has broken the compact.
Network schism: Jason says the Slovak government caused the violence when the Network split. Gerling goes rogue.
Travis Noble joins; the plan for a stolen backpack nuke.
Saint-Étienne: a second zone, claimed with vampires fighting alongside (Book 6, Ch44-46); it becomes a spirit domain encompassing most of the city.
Leaving: he says his farewells in France on a warm autumn day.
Family: Ken, Cheryl, Erika, Ian, Emi, Kaito and Amy; Yumi and Hiro; later the whole clan at Asano Village.
The Network (Anna Tilden, Keith, Mr North, Gerling, Nigel Thornton's teams), the Cabal (Craig Vermillion, Boris), the EOA (the Four Cardinals).
Pallimustus friends: Rufus, Gary, Humphrey, Sophie, Neil, Belinda and Clive are not on Earth in this era; Gary says he had not seen Jason in two years.
Known: magic is on Earth and rising; the link between worlds was tampered with by an outworlder who brought a door; Jason can enter transformation events.
Proto-spaces opening in towns, vampire occupation of Europe and Russia, political factions that fight over cores, and the family's safety.
The prize and the search: Emir spent most of two years looking for the conditions to open the astral space; the prize for the winning team is five legendary awakening stones.
The announcement: Emir declares Jason under his protection, explains the Order of the Reaper's contract and introduces Callum Morse.
The mood: Farrah's wake is held in the cloud palace's guest wing, with Padma and Farrah's parents present.
Emir tells the gathering "things are not as simple as described".
Launch: iron-rankers board the cloud ship once the palace has resumed its shape; adventurers spread across Sky Scar Lake by every means.
The zone is "City of Fallen Echoes (Gate Tower Three)".

Shade's account: the legacy goes to whoever embodies the ideals of the Order; the last grandmaster sent all the initiates into the city; the vorger do not kill, and the initiates were turned into abominations.
The city: siege golems and flesh abominations adapt to how they are fought. Imran Keane joins Jason's party.
A blood root vine is hit with Inexorable Doom.
Rival teams: Padma's team is the last to join, and Beth's team stays put beside Jason's near the end.
All reach the city centre, where Humphrey's team staggers in ragged.
The final day: Shade announces that the second trial ends in one day and warns of nightmare hags, diamond-rank astral entities.
Rewards include a True Light, Summoner's Die: Form and an Immortal Crest.
The Order's truth: Shade says the Order now "makes connections" instead of keeping a roster of assassins, and a Reaper Token goes into Jason's inventory (Book 2, Ch60).
After: Emir arrives with 419 time-displaced priests "asking for you by name".
The Healer thanks Jason for returning their people and Jason receives the title Godless Prophet.
The team spends days in Jayapura awakening abilities and getting tattoos.
Emir and Constance: host from the cloud ship and palace.
Jason's party: Neil, Jory and Keane fight together for several days, and Keane is added to Jason's party.
Humphrey's team arrives separately at the centre.
Other teams: Beth's, Rick's, Padma's, plus Valdis's Team Shining Scabbard.
Shade: the guide throughout (Book 2, Ch44).
Two accounts: Emir says churches scoured the Order away; Shade says it survives and the trials are a lure.
How he arrives: standing stones in concentric circles on a dirt oval on Earth; on Pallimustus the surge is "some five years overdue" and his companions gather in a recently fortified town.
Where the team is: Gary and Virid are sealed in a smithy for nineteen days; the team arrives in Rimaros by skyship, with Farrah pointing out "the city of islands".
The Storm Kingdom: obsessed with extreme specialisation; Emir is not allowed in it, having stolen from the royal family.
Dawn warns that invasion platforms are appearing worldwide.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: Registration and search: Rimaros requires outside adventurers to register, with tests for Builder infiltrators; the Builder cult response team takes Jason in.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: The royals: Zara's mourning period is nearly over; Liara Rimaros and Vesper Rimaros handle him; Soramir tells him he sensed his arrival.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: Settling: Jason's team reaches Palisaros and the cloud house. Humphrey names the team Team Biscuit.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: Purity stronghold: the Ecumenical Council declares Purity fallen and a strike force is prepared.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: The expedition: bone feasters attack the fortress town of Arcazitlan; Jeni Kavaloa leads a mixed expedition into an astral aperture and seals it.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: The Order: Melody Jain leads the enclave with Sendira.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: The war: Rick Geller reports a ground city of thick legs; Jason's team is given a device to carry into the city, only one of which is the true bomb.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: It had been a month since the War of Four Cities, or the One Day War.

sec: Book 7: the surge and the One Day War
claim: The cost: Ledev and Vesper both died saving the city.

sec: Book 8: the Order and the throne
claim: The Order: Sendira, Fila and Ramona raid; the Order travels by underwater vehicle.

sec: Book 8: the Order and the throne
claim: Liara leads an expedition into the Builder complex.

sec: Book 8: the Order and the throne
claim: The mining complex: below the sea floor; Korinne Pescos leads the rescue.

sec: Book 8: the Order and the throne
claim: The throne and gate: the Fundament Gate is broken down, an incomplete spirit realm consumes the Firmament Core, and the astral throne lets avatars exist in his domains.

sec: Book 8: the Order and the throne
claim: The Builder's deal: Jason tells the Builder "I want them gone. Today"; the Builder withdraws his forces.

sec: Book 8: the Order and the throne
claim: Weeks later the Builder's forces abandon the Storm Kingdom as a battlefront.

sec: Book 8: the Order and the throne
claim: Dawn says he is an astral king because he has an astral throne and gate.
Team Biscuit: Humphrey, Sophie, Neil, Belinda, Clive and Gary, with Rufus and Farrah.
Royals: Soramir, Liara, Vesper and Zara; the Storm King rises from the throne to look down at Jason.
Elsewhere: Dawn advising; Travis at the largest Artifice Association workshop in Rimaros.
Known: the Builder's invasion platforms; the Church of Death's certificate says Jason has died four times.
How long: Jason tells those who waited "almost twenty years" and says he "only missed fifteen years or so".
A letter opens the book: friends write that everyone is getting super-strong and waiting for him.
What changed: the System appeared; Earth's magic is known to the public, because "less than fifteen years ago, no one knew magic existed".
The call: Clive tells friends "The portal to Jason's soul realm has opened up again. Finish whatever business you're on and make your way to Yaresh".
Reunions: Rexion and Gary's statue; Marla, with hair and eyes like molten steel; Rick's team arrives in a brothel fire; the Valdis duel in Yaresh's mirage chamber (Book 12, Ch17-19).
Greenstone and Boko: Jason reaches Greenstone quietly days before the official arrival.
Boko is destroyed after his assassination; massive portals disgorge an army, and the ghost fire phoenix arcs through the messenger host. Jamis Fran Muskar apologises.
New homes: Jason names the oasis city New Water.
The System: the mob outside his Cyrion palace has been there since the System went dark; see../../02_Cosmology_and_Powers/The_System.md.
The plan to Earth: a secret council of Earth's powers makes a deal to bring outsiders to remove Jason; Jason explains his plan, which depends on a favour owed by the World-Phoenix.
The pirates: a pirate captain, Jota Withers, arrives in a dimension ship; Team Biscuit and Farrah fight in stage two of Jason's plan.
The visit: the family reunion and Emi's cousins; a formal expedition tours Jason's astral kingdom.
Diplomacy: Li Mei and the international committee plan the handoff; Boris Ketland openly leads the Cabal.
The lecture: Jason tells the gathering about the great astral beings, the Cosmic Throne, outworlders and Knowledge's plan.
He describes the long process by which the original Builder was replaced.
The bridge anchor: a crowd gathers at the bridge anchor site in Australia, where no trace remains of the small town that stood there.
Item windows: the System shows each item with a rank and rarity in the form "Item: [Dread Salvation] (iron rank [growth], legendary)", then a description, a kind in brackets and effect lines.
Unidentifiable items show question marks, such as the "transcendent rank, legendary" World-Phoenix Token with "???" effects.
Growth items have a rank that can rise; soul-bound growth items are rare, Clive says, and the advancement requirements are "usually quite prohibitive".
Bound items "cannot be used by anyone else".
Rarities seen: common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, and "unavailable" for the Fundamental Realm Authority Token.
Tiers of power: ordinary items are ranked iron to gold; astral blessing tokens and divine awakening stones are "transcendent rank".
What they do: "An awakening stone that unlocks the power of consumption... Effect: Awakens an essence ability", requiring an unawakened essence ability.
The stone melts into the user's hand "with little fanfare".
Why they matter: Rufus tells Jason he cannot "properly progress towards bronze rank until you awaken every essence ability you have. That's all twenty".
Naming and rarity: stones are "unranked" and carry a rarity, such as the Awakening Stone of the Feast (common), of Adventure (rare), of the Stars (epic) and of the Reaper (legendary).
Affinity: the Reaper stone "sharing affinity with the Reaper" is used in Jason's awakening ritual with the Reaper token, and it gives Humphrey, a human, a special attack.
Divine awakening stones: a god-made stone is "transcendent rank, epic" and bestows a specific aura power.

Sources: looting an awakening stone or essence can pay better than the contract to kill the monster; the Adventure Society gives stones for exceptional service, "although rarely", and some open contracts offer them as rewards; otherwise stones are bought through brokers, almost always at auction, at exorbitant prices.
Brokers in a small city hold the valuable stuff, like essences and stones, for big auctions.
Family supply: the Gellers traditionally supply their scions with enough stones to get started, while the rest must be earned.
Restricted-essence trades: Adventure Society representatives offer good trades for restricted essences, as when Sophie trades a death essence for two epic stones.
Who makes it: the Adventure Society manages the badges but the Magic Society creates them, taking an aura imprint from the new member inside a magic circle in about a minute.
What it carries: every badge is paired with a tracking stone that tells the Society whether the member is alive or dead and finds them if they go missing.
Members claim adventure notices with it and hold it against a security screen to close a contract.
The wallet: the badge is a circular iron medallion embossed with a sword and rod crossed over a shield, carried in a leather wallet.
Stars are on the metal: an official taps a wedge-shaped stone to the badge and a star is added, or removed.
It tracks the badge, not the person: the tracking stones trace the badges, so a discarded badge hides its owner.
A change of aura leaves the imprint on the badge unmatched, so the wearer cannot be tracked until a new badge is issued.
When the Society wanted people's auras re-examined, their badges were also to be replaced.
Jason's case: the stone cannot track his aura imprint, and Farrah says some people have abilities that block magical tracking.
A new badge for a changed aura: when Jason's aura and personal crest change, he is told to present himself to the Magic Society for a new badge.
Using the tracking: adventurers find dead colleagues by following a crystal orb that points to the badge.
A diamond in place of stars: at gold rank in Book 12, Krensler gives Jason a new Adventure Society badge, gold, with a diamond symbol where one, two or three stars would normally be.
The Burning Violet guild: among his appointments in Vitesse, Jason joins the guild most of his companions belong to.
Its guild house stands across from the Remore Academy.
Applicants are taken by an intake clerk, assessed by an executive in an in-depth interview, and checked for identity late in the process.
The guild executive is divided over his membership, which Lord Bassingthwaite fears could become a flashpoint.
Emir's cloud ship: it arrives at the Greenstone dock and a walkway of cloud connects to the shore as a hole opens in its side.
Moored, it morphs over about ten minutes into a palace of clouds floating on the water.

Emir's cloud palace: floating just offshore on the north side of the Island, "fully exposed to the waves and currents, yet remained as immovable as solid ground", with wings and towers in blue, purple, orange and gold.
Walls, floors and ceilings glow with absorbed sunlight the palace stores and distributes, and the floors have a bouncy-castle spring.
Low-magic limits: out of Greenstone the ship's full functionality is restored when Emir's cloud ship floats above Kurdansk.
Team base: Jason's team move into Emir's palace after the contest.

Jason's Cloud Flask: it creates buildings and vehicles of cloud, with forms limited by rank, iron cloud houses, bronze cloud vehicles and silver cloud palaces; items inside a returned construct are stored in a dimensional space until another is formed.
Disguised constructs: in Venice his family and Dawn stay in a cloud palace disguised as a yacht.

Asano Village: Farrah prepares a place for Jason's cloud house at the end of a glass tunnel along the seafloor, two kilometres out, reached by a tramway from the compound and sealed by a wall of water, so the house can run underwater; the text checked does not show the house later sitting there.
Uses later: Hana Shavar runs relief operations from Jason's cloud palace after the messenger attack; in Cyrion he sits meditating in his cloud palace on the lake.

Lesser Miracle Potion: "iron rank, legendary", "Salvation in a bottle", it fully restores health, mana and stamina but only works on normal and iron-rank people, and its lingering magic delays other recovery.
Medallion of Escape: "silver rank, uncommon", evacuates the holder from the astral space when their aura is projected into it, and only works inside the City of Fallen Echoes.
Immortal Crest: "iron rank, rare", lets a mystical tattooist draw out a soul crest and only works on an iron-rank essence user.
Summoner's Die: Form: "iron rank [growth], legendary", it randomly alters the form of an iron-rank summon.
Clockwork Core: "iron rank, rare", the core of an artificial monster that simplifies the materials and processes of a construct creature; clockwork cores are made by clockwork kings.
Star seeds: great astral beings, not gods, "can send their followers star seeds"; once implanted and germinated the body transforms, "minor or major".
Reality cores: roughly the size and shape of an ostrich egg, dark crystal glowing with transcendent light; one appears in each affected zone and the factions scramble for it.
They are the source of the transformation zones' treasures and are common in node space.
Emir leaves skimmers waiting at Boko to carry the team into the desert.
Pushed past their limits: one of Emir's people specialises in magical tools and can periodically push the skimmers to speeds beyond their normal capability, so the whole vehicle vibrates.
Their limits: skimmers cannot go through an astral-space aperture, so the party continues on foot.
Requisitioned skimmers: expeditions requisition extra skimmers from the city and return them afterwards.
After Emir's ship sails south down the coast and into shore at an unremarkable patch of desert, his people unload three sand barges that carry the whole group inland to Sky Scar Lake.
The trip takes hours more, into the night.
Expedition transport: an expedition leaving Greenstone uses carriages to reach desert relay stations, then the captured Ustei barge and smaller barges supplied by the Magic Society.

The Ustei war barge: it is easily the size of a passenger liner, built on the skeletons of leviathan creatures, with three giant skulls on its flat-nosed bow, and the entire Ustei tribe lives in it. None of Emir's barges is its size.
Carriages on the Island: adventurers travel to the Island in a train of carriages.
Jason's inventory is "a video-game inventory only Jason could see", unlike Clive's storage, which is opened by making a circle of floating runes with a portal inside.
They add slots to an inventory in proportion to their rank, and at iron rank one bag slot is available and holds only iron-rank bags.
Bags come in novelty shapes, such as a pair of boots.
Storage as a profession: adventurers carry their possessions in dimensional bags or dimensional space abilities and travel light.
Some portal workers "aren't even adventurers and do storage space transport for a living".
Loot goes straight in: looted coins appear in the storage abilities of Clive, Humphrey and Jason, and Jason keeps a ledger of how much belongs to whom.
Storage can be looted: Jason could have taken the items from Farrah's storage space by looting her body like a monster, and neither man suggested such a defilement.
Limits on contents: it is "almost impossible to place living material inside dimensional storage", with only a few carefully chosen plants viable.
Portal-type abilities: they open only to places the user has visited before, along with other limits.
A portal fails if the destination has changed enough that the visualisation is wrong; redecorating is fine, demolishing the building is not.
Jason's shadow teleport: the iron-rank effect of Path of Shadows is "Teleport using shadows as a portal. You must be able to see the destination shadow".
Archways: the portal arches of the Order of the Reaper's astral space are built on the same ability, and the shadow gates there look like Jason's own.
Travelling through a dark aperture feels exactly like his shadow teleport.
Stability: a portal may not stay stable long, so travellers follow quickly.
Capacity and cooldown: portalling a silver-ranker uses all of Jason's portal's capacity, so the others wait out a ten-minute cooldown.
Magically sound destinations: the destination must be sound, while the start point can be shakier because the user is present and the ability adapts through the user's senses.
Beacons and range: some portal abilities can target places never visited if an aura-based marker is there to home in on.
Jason's ability to skip the visit works at less than a tenth of his normal portal range.
The Builder cult's network: the cult and the Church of Purity moved about through a transportation network of portal arches, which the Magic Society cracked and could track.
Contract use: a contract in the Storm Kingdom would deploy Jason's team widely to give them many portal destinations for supply runs and rapid response.
Portal specialists of gold rank are in demand.

Gold-rank travel: with Sophie's time acceleration the team arrives at teleport-like speed without the disorientation of a real teleport, and they are "long past throwing up like first time portal travellers".
Relics of the King: the gift gives access to the astral throne, astral gate and soul forge to limited degrees.
The Sky Link network: Farrah and Travis built it, and an actual portal network "will throw whole countries and industries into disarray".
An object that resists storage: Thadwick says a relic resists placement in dimensional storage, which makes it hard to move and hard to hide.
Hegemon's Dominion: "silver rank [growth], legendary", "the scabbard to Hegemon's Will" and "the embodiment of hegemonic control, representing the hegemon's mastery of his domain".
Bound to Jason: it cannot be used by anyone else, shares his ability to ignore rank disparity, and is "treated as the same item" as the sword for all magical effects.
Anything the target resists or is immune to is negated and cannot be passed to another target.
Growth: its growth is no longer capped by rank, but the upgrade materials are ones Jason has never heard of and are presumably gold rank.
Gary's account: the crafting was strange and "it's almost like the sword knew how it wanted to be reforged".
Jason says that after a recent lost fight the scabbard's ability is exactly what he needed.

Hegemon's Will: "silver rank [growth], legendary", "reforged with a renewed sense of purpose" with the help of a grandmaster craftsman, bound to Jason, and sharing his ability to ignore rank disparity.

Invoking conjured weapons: the wielder may invoke all effects of one conjured weapon into the blade at the weapon's normal conjuring cost, one at a time, and add extra damage for an ongoing mana cost scaled by aura strength.

Available invocations are Ruin, the Blade of Tribulation (low cost; the item screen lists corrosive damage and Corrosion) and Penitent, the Blade of Sacrifice (moderate cost; disruptive-force damage).
The invocation message for Ruin says necrotic damage will be inflicted, not corrosive.
Each cleansed affliction gives the enemy an instance of Hegemon's Mercy and the wielder an instance of Benevolent Hegemon.
Hegemon's Mercy is a holy affliction that suppresses all magical abilities and drops off rapidly outside the wielder's aura; Benevolent Hegemon strengthens overlapping allied auras.
Set effect: as part of the Regalia, enemies struck are drained of mana and inflicted with Hegemon's Tribute, and the wielder gains Benevolent Hegemon.
Visible effect: the white sigils on the blade glow life-force red for Ruin and blue for Penitent.

In use, Book 8: Hegemon's Will prevents a conjuration and gains all the properties of the conjured weapon; an affliction that cannot be resisted is moved into the scabbard, and returning the sword to it makes the next attack inflict that affliction.
Relics need transcendent power and most of their abilities stay sealed until Jason gains it.
Mercy at work on Earth: touching a captured pirate with the sword absorbs her holy afflictions and inflicts an instance of Hegemon's Mercy for each, with a matching Benevolent Hegemon for Jason.
Jason calls the sword the first and last gift he got from Gary.

sec: 2. The Trap Weaver Battle Robe (iron rank)
claim: Where it comes from: Gilbert sells it, with Gary haggling the price, in bronze coins, which is unusual for iron-rank equipment.

sec: 2. The Trap Weaver Battle Robe (iron rank)
claim: It is made from trap weaver silk, alchemically treated, with leather panels, "the magic integrated right down to the weaving pattern of the cloth".

sec: 2. The Trap Weaver Battle Robe (iron rank)
claim: Look: "almost a robe", in shifting shades of dark grey, with black leather panels over the torso, arms and legs and flowing cloth draped over it; "a strange combination of tactical armour from Jason's world and some kind of wizard robe".

sec: 2. The Trap Weaver Battle Robe (iron rank)
claim: The drape breaks up the body's lines in the dark.

sec: 2. The Trap Weaver Battle Robe (iron rank)
claim: Item entry: "[Trap Weaver Battle Robe] (iron rank, epic)", full body armour of silk and leather.

sec: 2. The Trap Weaver Battle Robe (iron rank)
claim: Effects: increased resistance to damage, strong against cutting and piercing but weaker against blunt; repairs damage over time, though extensive damage may need external repair; absorbs blood so it leaves no trail; resists bleed and poison; resists adhesives; adapts its fit to the wearer.

sec: 2. The Trap Weaver Battle Robe (iron rank)
claim: Source monster: trap weavers are iron-rank monsters "responsible for more iron-rank adventurer deaths than any other monster in the Greenstone region".

sec: 2. The Trap Weaver Battle Robe (iron rank)
claim: Jason later offers Sophie the same silk through his tailor.
Jason asks about the next robe once he nears bronze.
Gilbert makes it from umbral mountain snake leather Jason supplied, marsh hydra leather and a lining of deep wyrm silk.
The entry reads "[Dark Hydra Robe] (bronze rank, epic)".
It is darker than the old robe: mostly scaled matte black with grey trim, keeping the sleek draping lines.
Jason wears it as his bronze-rank battle robe.
Jason's silver-era robe is again custom-made by Gilbert; in Book 5 its magic has died after Jason pushed it close to destruction many times.
The robes change with Jason's ranks; the old iron-rank robe had much more grey than the black bronze one.
Outfits tab: Jason slots armour into an outfit in his inventory and taps equip; smoke surrounds him and the clothes swap.
Self-repair: a robe recovers to pristine condition in about four days, and it is cleaned with the rest of the wearer.
Recognised as adventurer dress: workers see the combat robes and weapons and know better than to interfere.
Fit for combat: loose but designed so it does not tangle in wheels.
Trade-off: light robes give up protectiveness for flexibility, a weakness Jason uses against Hendren's identical style.
What they are: "roughly the size and shape of an ostrich egg", dark crystal glowing with internal transcendent light; "batteries for the universe", fuelling the nodes of reality.
Where they appear: each transformation event reveals a single reality core.
Jason's door gives him ready access to a treasure trove of them under the landscape, which he leaves where they are.
Use: they offer a path forward to those bottlenecked at the top of power.
The power can be consumed directly with a simple ritual and is being tested for category-four suppression collars.
They have already pushed two near-category-four users over the threshold.
Factions: the Cabal claims the cores in Kostroma and Africa, the Network the one in the USA.
The fight over cores strains cooperation. The Network keeps a secure store.
Vampires: blood infused with reality-core energy makes the oldest vampires powerful.
Dawn says the cores have the same effect on advancement to a lesser degree.
Stopping the supply: Farrah says the only way to stop people from taking cores is to cut off the supply.
Jason's work stops the transformation zones forming.
Extraction elsewhere: a pirate admiral calls them impossible to extract normally and notes that Pallimustus is cracked like an egg, making them accessible.
Jason's own use: for ten years he sucks reality-core energy from vampire lords and builds a backup avatar.
Stable Genesis Cores: unranked, common items looted from anomalies in a zone.
Jason uses them to expand his spirit domain; the cost rises as the domain grows.
Unstable Genesis Cores: after corpses changed the cores they carried, refining them to a usable state, Jason reasons that since the ones he looted were stable, these must be the unstable variety.

Dread Salvation: a sword "crafted with gratitude, in hope it would be of the greatest use in the moment of greatest need"; "iron rank [growth], legendary"; when an affliction special attack meets a physical immunity it gains Stone Cutter, and for a magical immunity Spell Breaker. Gary made it, as a gift.

Dread Salvation in Book 6: bronze rank, bound to Jason and sharing his ability to ignore rank disparity; it can be imbued with aura for damage at an ongoing mana cost; "The original creator must demonstrate his growth and reforge the weapon".
The window says it "must be reforged by the original craftsperson in order to advance further".
The reforged sword is named Hegemon's Will on its item screen, with its scabbard Hegemon's Dominion treated as the same item; Gary gives it to Jason in Book 7. The reforging by Gary and Virid is.
Cloud Flask: iron rank growth item that Jason binds in Book 2; it creates cloud buildings and vehicles, with forms limited by rank.
By Book 6 it is silver rank, with the cloud house at iron, cloud vehicle at bronze and cloud palace at silver.
Its maker is "some unknown diamond-rank craftsman".
Amulet of the Dark Guardian: silver rank growth item, the last item produced by his old quest system, a reproduction of his personal crest on an obsidian chain.
Its boon Guardian's Blessing absorbs damage per affliction applied and can be given to another person by touch.
Soul-Imprinting Triune: Jason receives it with a hoard of spirit coins in Book 5; it turns three soul-bound growth items into a set when all three are on his person.

Regalia of the Dark Hegemon: the set bonuses are Hegemon's Authority from the amulet (allies in his aura resist aura suppression, and he can spend instances to strengthen his own suppression), a mist shroud from the cloud flask, and mana drain with Hegemon's Tribute from the sword.
Robes of the Astral Verdict: bronze rank, rare cloth armour for summoners that boosts dimension spells, summon damage reduction and disruptive-force resistance.
The Regalia window states that Dread Salvation must be reforged to advance; the reforging happens in Book 7.
The third element: Dawn tells Jason that a space like his needs an astral throne and an astral gate and a third thing, the soul forge, "for soul engineering".
Soul engineering: an ethically fraught crafting profession.
Jason is put off by "souls being used as crafting mats".
Every astral king has one: "every astral king but one" lacks it.
Form unknown: Jason does not know if it is a physical thing, a loose matrix or a purely spiritual construct; it might be a tree.
What an astral kingdom without one lacks: Marek thinks Jason's astral kingdom is unstable because it lacks a forge.
The goal: the messengers want to turn the natural array beneath Yaresh into a soul forge.
Why Kaal wanted it: a soul forge would explain the resources she spent; Boris says Kaal believed Destruction wanted a massive explosion once the messengers claimed it.
The result: the failed attempt produced a corrupted birthing tree: "the result of a failed attempt to create a soul forge".
The messengers tried to force the whole array to stay together instead of separating a part.
The goal: he wants the forge for himself, partly to use a gift from the Healer that only works once he has one.
Why messengers failed: they treated it as theirs and applied messenger sensibilities to it.
The extraction: he separates the natural array, the forge and the tree, and puts each in its proper place.
The array is pushed out of the soul realm; the forge stays within it.
Result: the astral throne, astral gate and soul forge set him on the path to becoming an astral king and his soul realm begins to break down.

The door: Mr North tells Jason "It's not a literal door... It's an astral construct with the power to manifest in physical reality in the form of a portal", and that Jason must absorb it so it cannot be taken from him.
Jason notes "This door is an object of the Builder".
The Fundament Gate: a ring of rough marble standing stones in a dell, "transcendent rank, legendary", whose window lets Jason incorporate it into his Spirit Vault, purging the Builder's influence.
It improves his sense of Builder items and adds to Path of Shadows the ability to open a portal to the Fundamental Realm.

Consequences: Jason used the Builder's door when he flooded himself with magic and later "accidentally trashed it for parts"; "the magic of the Builder's door that Jason had absorbed" is distinct from the soul-attack trick he learned from the star seed.

Builder's view: in Book 6 Shako says that without the Fundament Gate the Builder forged, Jason could not have remade the zone, and Dawn asks for the designs so the World-Phoenix can create a complementary item to anchor the bridge.
Later items: the Fundamental Realm Authority Token and the Firmamental Bridge Anchor are looted from the destroyed artefacts; see Tokens_Stones_and_Relics.md.

Astral blessing tokens: Clive says they are "something great astral beings give out to bestow blessings, as signs of approval"; they trigger racial gift evolutions, and are harmless, unlike star seeds.
World-Phoenix Token: Jason finds it in his starting inventory, "transcendent rank, legendary", "Uses remaining: 1/1" with unreadable effects. It is consumed in Book 3.
Reaper Token: an obsidian square engraved with a silver scythe, "transcendent rank, legendary".
Jason takes the Scythe of the Reaper by placing his inventory window behind it, and the token is added.
It is melded into his body with the awakening stone of the Reaper in Clive's ritual and consumed.
Knowledge's token: a small stone square like the World-Phoenix Token but washed-out blue, offered with two awakening stones; Jason is told it would take him home and wonders whether to trust it.
Divine Awakening Stone of Inevitability: "transcendent rank, epic", crafted by a god to bestow a specific aura power.

The stone's effect line names the ability [Inescapable Doom] but its ability description names [Inevitable Demise]; the compendium uses Inevitable Demise and treats the other as a variant, since no later list shows either.
The Soul-Purgation Tablet (aura) removes an existing aura essence ability and cannot be forcibly used on another.

Fundamental Realm Authority Token: "transcendent rank, unavailable", bound to Jason and usable only by him and Zithis Carrow Vayel; it lets the wielder open gates to the fundamental realm of any physical reality.
Jason looted it from the destroyed artefacts.
Dawn tells him "You can't have this" and that he will need to give it back.
Firmamental Bridge Anchor: the other looted item, "transcendent rank, legendary", with unreadable effects and one use.
Cup of Heroes: the god of heroes' offer of divine power; Gary "has drunk from the Cup of Heroes" and the window warns the divine power will work to leave his soul and rejoin the god.
Calendar: Jason arrives in late November; Leust's lumber conspiracy falls in late summer moving into autumn.
Scale: iron rank; Jason's badge is iron with one star.
Field testing is held at the start of every month.
Live dangers: a traditional blood cult in the hedge-maze estate; the Ustei raiding spirit coin convoys; Old City's "Big Three" crime lords.
Turning points: Farrah dies covering civilians; Emir's contest and the City of Fallen Echoes free 419 time-displaced priests.
Calendar: the book opens in a mild Greenstone winter.
Scale: Path of Shadows reaches bronze; the Reaper-trial astral space has twelve towers about eight kilometres apart.
Live dangers: the church of Purity under an ecumenical inquiry; star seeds, implanted through the cult; energy ghouls.
Turning point: Jason dies covering the team's escape. Spoiler level: 1.
Calendar: Jason wakes on Earth in early June, a year and a half after leaving; Book 5 opens about nine months after that; a cold winter day in Book 6 and a warm autumn farewell.
Scale: bronze at the start, silver by the Book 5 chapter "Silver".

Live dangers: the EOA has seized Perth and Melbourne; the Network is publicly known as the Global Defense Network after the monster waves begin; transformation zones begin with Kostroma; gold-rankers explore Jason's Nitra domain a month after the dome falls.
Calendar: Book 7 opens at the standing stones; the surge is "some five years overdue".
Scale: silver rank in the Storm Kingdom, where sky islands house the cream of society.
Live dangers: a hundred and nineteen outworlders appear at once; the One Day War, after which "It had been a month"; the Order of Redeeming Light converting towns.
Turning point: the Astral Throne and Gate appear. Spoiler level: 2.
Calendar: Jason says he is twenty-nine.
Scale: silver-rank adventurers and gold and diamond power brokers in a small elf city.

Live dangers: a messenger camp and Knowledge's army outside the city; world-taker worms; the Aristocratic Faction undermining the Duke; the Church of Undeath striking when its god has "saved up his chances to intervene".
Calendar: the zone lasts "months"; Gary is a haggard figure "almost a year later".
Setting: the underground city of Cardinas and its natural array; a third transformation zone that Jason reshapes.
Calendar: "almost twenty years" since the Reaper's priests were freed; Book 13 is set in 2038.
Live dangers: Boko destroyed; the System withdrawn from regions that keep indenture; a pirate dimension ship led by Jota Withers; a back-in-full-swing vampire war on Earth; Knowledge's plan.
Jason's circle: Rufus, Gary, Farrah (she dies at the end of), Humphrey, Clive, Belinda, Jory, Sophie, Neil.
Authority: Elspeth Arella, Vincent Trenslow, Lucian Lamprey, Pochard Finn, Danielle Geller.
Patrons and staff: Emir Bahadir, Constance, Hester Maharala, Gilbert Bertinelli.
Old City and the Island: Cole Silva, Clarissa Ventress, Adris Dorgan, Thalia Mercer.
Builder cult: Zato, Timos.
Teams and rivals: Beth Cavendish, Valdis Volaire, Sigrid Freyn, Padma Parsell, Dustin Kettering, Hannah and Claire Adeah.
Purity: Anisa Lasalle and Nicolas Hendren; Cole Silva's right hand Killian Laurent; Callum Morse.
Dawn appears in person, with Shako and Velius in the dome chamber.
Jason's family: Erika, Ian and Emi, Hiro, Ken and Cheryl, Kaito and Amy, Akari.
Network and allies: Anna Tilden, Nigel Thornton, Asya Karadeniz, Greg, Travis Noble.
Cabal and EOA: Craig Vermillion, Mr North, Gerling.
Network figures: Ketevan Arziani, Adrien Barbou, Audrey Blaine, Noriko Asano, Li Li Mei.
Returned: Farrah is freed from Barbou and the EOA; Dawn returns in a new avatar.
Storm Kingdom: Soramir, Zara Rimaros, Liara Rimaros, Pelli, Argy, Kasper Irios.
Adventurers: Korinne Pescos, Estella Warnock.
Church and order: Gabrielle Pellin as priestess of Knowledge, Melody Jain and the Order of Redeeming Light.
Rimaros and guilds: Trenchant Moore, Jeni Kavaloa, Orin and Amos Pensinata, Baseph and the Rimaros children, Miles Cotezee, Helsveth (for her first appearance).
Elf diamond-rankers: Allayeth and Charist.
Yaresh officials and clergy: Musin Heath, Hana Shavar, Carlos Quilido.
Messengers: Jes Fin Kaal, Fal Vin Garath, Benella, Marek Nior Vargas, Tera Jun Casta; their astral king is Vesta Carmis Zell.
Council of Kings: Jamis Fran Muskar.
Yaresh politics: Marcus Xenoria, Gormanston Bynes, Hess Jor Nasala; the Builder's vessel Erigo Fin Desca.
Expedition: Gary, Gwydion Remore and Danielle, Boris Ket Lundi.
Beyond Pallimustus: Raythe and Velius, the peak diamond-rankers who lead the descent.
Cardinas and the undead: Marla, Garth Larosse, Beaufort the cult commander.
Pallimustus: Travis, Zara, now gold, Jota Withers.
Earth 2038: Holly Macrossan, Natalie Park, Lenora Coleman, Rufus teaching the clan, Yumi Asano, Emi and Vincent Baudrillard, Nik, Belinda and Estella, Clive and Lorelei.
Antagonists: Elizabeth, whose blood slave is Gerling, and Knowledge's plan.
More 2038 figures: Vincent Baudrillard, Lorelei Grantham, Audrey Blaine, Marie Finnegan, Umber, Hassan Dukhtar.
Check absence as well as presence. Farrah is dead from the end of Book 1 until Book 4; Kaito, Asya and Greg die in Book 5.
The Ustei in the desert: nomads from the north are raiding spirit coin convoys far from home. Why did they come south?
An unregistered spirit coin farm: a coin that did not come from a registered farm means an unregistered one "needs to be found and shut down". Who runs it?
A corrupt branch: the Magic Society's local director was banished to Greenstone for improprieties and uses the Fortress as his office. Who protects him?
An indenture sale: criminals' indentures are sold or auctioned to recoup the cost of their crimes.
The Healer's temple: a priest tells those who stand against the church that they are no longer welcome.
Star seeds: a captured adventurer will not consent to examination, and his family must authorise it. Who else carries a seed?
Purity under inquiry: an ecumenical council investigates the church of Purity.
A rain elemental over the Old City: it appears in the city and bronze-rankers gear up to confront it.
Hunting Killian Laurent: Jason's team spends days in the hunt for the man who possessed a star seed.
The veldt contract: an unconventional contract east of Greenstone beyond the desert astral space.
The EOA moves on Sydney: they have "seized control in Perth and Melbourne, and now they're making no secret of their overtures into Sydney".
The Dimensional Fortress: a sector of the grid has been offline for seventy years.
Grid sabotage: shutting down only localised areas, with a wider failure expected in two months.
Reality cores: one appears in each affected zone and the factions scramble for it.
A domain nobody can enter safely: gold-rankers explore Jason's Nitra domain until the hostile effects grow dangerous.
The atomic device: Jason, Farrah and Travis work on a semi-disassembled device on a cold winter day.
The outworlders: a hundred and nineteen appear at once and must be placed.
A political marriage that fell through: Zara was matched with a member of House Irios for stability before the surge.
Guild quotas: guilds receive sixty percent of the surge quotas though few adventurers belong to them.
Towns massacred under cover of monster attacks: the Order of Redeeming Light disguises its conversions and killings.
A kidnapped heir: Gibson Amouz is spirited away from the island.
A messenger camp: Knowledge's army and the messengers set camp outside Yaresh while the city's government and Adventure Society worry.
Servant races and masters: messenger masters may treat servants as they please within limits.
An alliance that will betray: Emir calls the plan to ally with Jes Fin Kaal one in which she will betray them.
The Aristocratic Faction: landowners with no adventurers behind them undermine the Duke.
A branded messenger: Tera Jun Casta's brand was her astral king's tool for keeping her at silver.
A buried city: Cardinas lies under the mountains, ruled from the Citadel of Pillars, where fewer than ten thousand brighthearts survive.
Undeath's patience: the church lies dormant and then acts all at once.
A soul forge: messengers were sent down to create it from the natural array.
A hero's price: Gary drinks from the Cup of Heroes and the divine power will try to leave him.
Gathering the Earthlings: seventy-four are to return and about thirty cannot or will not.
Indenture and the System: the System will withdraw from regions that keep indenture, and the Queen of Estercost asks Jason to arbitrate.
A pirate admiral's ship on Earth: Jota Withers is hosted by the Asano clan matriarch.
A vampire war turning in humanity's favour: it is "back in full swing" and Europe is largely liberated but vampires hold a few cities.
Finnegan, Elizabeth and McKean: Finnegan's backers called using Elizabeth "the smart choice", and there has been no confirmed trace of McKean for over four years.
Knowledge's long plan: she has been preparing for around half a millennium.
Jason is an outworlder: he tells Rufus that coming to this world is "a fresh start"; Danielle later investigates him at Gabriel Remore's request. Level 1.

Star seeds and the Builder: an archbishop explains that great astral beings send followers star seeds; Clive explains that great astral beings cannot act in physical reality directly and recruit others. Level 1.
The Order of the Reaper: Emir says the churches "scoured" it away; Shade says it survives as a network of quiet allies and the trials are a lure. Level 1.
Dawn's role: the World-Phoenix's First Servant is its primary vessel; her true body is a celestine with ruby eyes. Level 1-2.
Jason's deaths: the Church of Death's certificate reads "died four times. So far.". Level 2.
Magic on Earth: hidden until the monster waves bring the Network into public view; "less than fifteen years ago, no one knew magic existed". Level 2.
Purity, Disguise and the Order of Redeeming Light: the gods may already have sanctioned Purity; Disguise created the order. Level 2-3.
Astral king: Jason's astral kingdom appears with the Throne and Gate; a healer realises he is a silver-rank astral king. Level 2.
The Builder's identity: the new Builder is the mortal messenger Zithis Carrow Vayel. Level 3.
The messengers' brand and the Unorthodoxy: rank limits are a function of the brand. Level 3.
The Cosmic Throne's sundering: told by Raythe and Velius and in Jason's briefing. Level 3.
Knowledge's plan and the Network's founder: Knowledge has been preparing for around half a millennium. Level 3.
The System as Jason's: the System administrator gift. Level 3.
Emir's account of the Order of the Reaper is contradicted by Shade's account; treat a character's story as belief unless a later line confirms it.
Gods are limited: a goddess cannot see into an astral space Jason holds, and a priest says his god cannot see into a hidden building. Characters often assume they can.
A great astral being need not fear a god's retribution because gods cannot see into an astral space outside their world.
Deadpan humour inside the setting: Jason answers an unreadable item description with "Question marks. That's enlightening. Do I have to pay a wizard to identify items?".
Modern references in a fantasy world: he suggests the Builder and Knowledge "play Mario Kart" and likens a projected face to Emperor Palpatine.
Australian idiom: "G'day" and "mate", "Strewth" and "yonks".
Bleeped profanity: Nik's swearing is bleeped on the page: "[Bleep]ing rubes".
Humour does not cancel stakes: Jason jokes about kneeling to the Storm King, and then answers a threat of execution flatly: "Die on my feet. I've done it before".
Titles for officials: "Instructor Trenslow" and "Instructor Spalding" during an assessment; "Priestess Pellin".
Shade uses "Mr Asano" and "Master Nik".
Messengers are addressed as lord whatever their sex, and a Voice of the Will as "Voice Kaal".
Jason: sarcastic, deferential only when rank forces it, with a dry understatement when he is grieving ("It's not a celebratory time").
Rufus: courteous and formal, apologising for discourtesy to a priestess, gesturing with a sausage on a stick while explaining guild quotas.
Farrah: lectures on any subject and is blunt when angry ("Barbou belongs to me").
Gary: deep and growling, plain about death ("rattling around in a hole").
Humphrey: precise and a little shy about romance, then crisp in command.
Sophie: wary of kindness, silent about pain.
Clive: a lecturer who loses the thread and apologises and jokes about wrestling an eel.
Neil: tentative before he commits.
Belinda: delighted by her own power and teasing.
Danielle: blunt and quick on a weakness, certain that "diplomacy is war".
Emir: smooth and showy, fond of grand entrances and a polished aside.
Dawn: composed and dry, lying lightly to Jason's face ("Of course I wasn't").
Shade: butler-formal courtesy.
Zara: courtly with a threat in the smile.
Boris: measured and careful.
Emi: sharp and political at thirteen, telling a reporter his story on mining deregulation was "an exercise in buffoonery".
Nik: foul-mouthed, a four-foot rabbit in a top hat and tuxedo whose swearing is bleeped. He says his name is "NIK, no C".
Taika: casual, as in "That legit sucked, bro".
Mr North: amused and unhurried.
Raythe: terse and final. Knowledge: "detached and untouchable".
Astral blessing token: an item great astral beings give as a sign of approval; it triggers racial gift evolutions (see 09_Items_and_Artefacts/Tokens_Stones_and_Relics.md). [2]
Fundamental Realm Authority Token: transcendent-rank item that lets its wielder open gates to the fundamental realm; Jason looted it and Dawn says he must give it back. [2]
In Book 12 Jason defines the role as putting yourself between the bad things and those who need protection. [0]
Ancestral Majesty: the form of address for Soramir Rimaros, used by Vesper and Liara and by a branch director. [2]
Blood root vine: a plant-animal monster of Pallimustus.

Blood oaks are a vampire-side threat on Earth whose revelation is "good for Elizabeth's negotiating position", with limbs each ending in a body used as weapon, shield and potion; that they are Elizabeth's weapons is Jason's guess, from notes. [2/3]
Brand (messenger): a mark in a messenger's soul; Boris says a messenger's rank limits are a function of the brand. [2]
Cabal: Earth's old magical society, with vampire members; see The_Cabal.md. [2]
Defier of the Will: a bond choice offered to Farrah in Book 12; it lets the holder negate the influence of the Astral Nexus in various ways and confers immortality. [3]
Dimensional ulceration: Dawn's term for a transformation zone forming in a space already coterminous with a proto-astral space: an open wound in the dimensional membrane.
Dumpling soup: Clive's model of the cosmos. [1]
EDJI: the Earth Defence Joint Initiative. [3]
Engineers of Ascension (EOA): an Earth faction; the Lyon branch's dimensional-space project head, Adrien Barbou, defected to it. [2]
Hump: a nickname for Humphrey Geller. [1]
Lesser Miracle Potion: iron-rank legendary potion that fully restores health, mana and stamina of normal and iron-rank people. [0]
Moon's Edge: Yaresh team of six gold-rank women raised by Allayeth and led by Miriam Vance; members include Ramona the ritualist and shield specialist, Valetta and the berserker Alice. [3]
Mr East: seat on the Network's inner committee; Adrien Barbou becomes the second Mr East. [2]
Network: Earth's coalition of essence users. [2]
Quintessence: elemental/essence crystal gems used in crafting. [0]
Reaper, the: great astral being of death's finality; Shade is one of its shadows. [1]
Red Table: blood cult with branches in remote areas, destroyed in Greenstone. [1]
Regalia of the Dark Hegemon: the set of Jason's three soul-bound items, made by the Soul-Imprinting Triune (see 09_Items_and_Artefacts/Soul_Bound_Items_and_Regalia.md). [1]
Rejector: the name Builder cultists give Jason. [1]
Shades, the: Shade's several bodies speaking as one. [1]
Shining Scabbard, Team: team led by Sigrid Freyn. [3]
Soph: a nickname for Sophie Wexler. [1]
Soul-Imprinting Triune: consumable that turns three soul-bound growth items into a set. [1]
Special-interest territory: the Australian government's status for the standing stones and for Asano Village, managed by a multinational organisation. [3]
Storm Shredder, Team: Rimaros team of buffed high-damage ranged specialists led by Korinne Pescos, with Orin Pensinata, Kalif, Rosa and Zara. [2]
Team Biscuit: Jason's team; a familiar picked the name. [1]

Umber: a figure who "likes to play games" and told of trapping a servant of the Reaper's kind in an astral space for centuries; that he is Shade's brother and plans against Jason in Book 13 is from notes. [3]

World engineer: one of the Builder's diamond-rank super-golems, comparable to a diamond-rank monster in size; twelve lie dormant in the Reaper-trials vessel, and the toppled remains of others lie beyond Cyrion's outer wall. [1/3]
