Why did the Ustei come south? (Narrowed in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Known: they raid spirit coin convoys far from home and are nomads from a region to the north, and they came south about three years before the Earthlings.

The Adventure Society learned the cause: the desert astral space was failing, the waterfall shutting off in brief isolated instances near the city and much worse in the north, until the oases connected to it could no longer support all the nomad tribes.
The tribe was shipped back north in its sand barge.

Does Marek Nior Vargas lead the Unorthodoxy? (Narrowed in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Known: Marek served Vesta Carmis Zell until recently and Jason calls his group "Marek's Unorthodoxy" with "victory or death" energy.
It is Boris who explains the movement to messengers and who passes as a branded servant of Vesta Carmis Zell, and Marek's people subordinate themselves to Boris as the Unorthodoxy's "messiah".

Who does the Unorthodoxy include among astral kings? (Narrowed in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Known: the Council of Kings does not know that Boris is Unorthodoxy, nor how many kings are outside it; Boris says the original astral kings were not messengers, that the Unorthodoxy has astral kings, and that there are "too many astral kings for anyone to keep track of", with the Unorthodoxy ones "slipping back into the general population".
One is the king of Navise Den Rigal, a "rare" Unorthodoxy king.

Before the brand there were no limits on rank, and the brand was instituted by messengers who became astral kings; only at diamond rank can a messenger begin to resist the brand. A silver-rank seal caps Tera Jun Casta.

What is the debt of Zithis Carrow Vayel? (Narrowed in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Known: while the Builder's world engineers prepare to move the planet, Jamis says "When this task is complete, the price is paid. Zithis Carrow Vayel will have fulfilled his debt to us", and Erigo says the messengers' ritualists provided "some low-level ritual magic" as a service for a reward.

What is Hero's sanction? (Resolved in the build plan 2A.6 pass.) Gwydion tells Gary that Hero has decided to sanction himself, as he has considered for longer than any of them has lived, in order to add "another miracle option. Something less powerful than the Cup of Heroes, with less of a price" by making the relics of dead demigods usable again for a short time.
A sanction changes an immortal in some way.

Did Death return the resurrection power Jason gave away? (Resolved in the 2026-10-22 pass.) Yes: "I will return what was taken, Jason Asano, now that it cannot be used for its original purpose", and the reality material forms his prime avatar.

What do the lesser-named great astral beings govern? (Narrowed in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Known: Legion administers the cosmic rules that govern life itself; the Celestial Book locked off essence combinations after the sundering and is venerated through a loose network tied to the Magic Society and the Church of Knowledge; the Reaper is the god of finality of death.
The Celestial Book, the Seeker of Songs, the Whisper in Corners and Legion take part in the Book 11 gathering.

What does the Firmamental Bridge Anchor do? (Resolved in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Dawn identifies it as something Jason can use to establish the bridge, and says using it consumes the authority in the item, so it is single-use and the great astral beings will not object to it.
Jason also calls it a "firmament bridge anchor".

Why can Jason not keep the Fundamental Realm Authority Token? (Resolved in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Dawn says it is a major demonstration of the Builder's failure and that great astral beings will not tolerate a mortal holding it, so he must give it back.
Jason trades it for concessions, including one opening of the way into the fundamental realm, and transfers the authority to the Builder.

How did Disguise take part in recruiting the Network's founder? (Resolved in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Jason explains that Knowledge helped Disguise pose as Purity and, in return for help including the elimination of Purity's troublesome followers, "the fake Purity brought an outworlder from Earth into his church". Not known: how the founder was chosen.

Is the Sky Link island Ascension's Gate? Known: Jason and Farrah first arrived on an uninhabited island that is later a town with storm accumulators, and the island renamed Ascension's Gate was seized by the Church of Knowledge's Holy Army.

Resolved as far as the text goes: Jason names the Storm Kingdom island as the bridge's Pallimustus anchor and later says the Church has annexed it; the two names are never put in one sentence, but both describe that island.

How strong is Vitesse's magic? Known: it is a high-magic city whose manifestations are powerful and frequent, the magic around it is strong enough for a cloud ship to fly, and iron-rankers in high-magic areas are not allowed to hunt alone.
Vehicles that need a special power in weak-magic Greenstone run on ambient magic in high-magic zones. Not known: a figure.

Narrowed 2026-10-24 (2F.5): the books do give a rank band: typical monsters are silver, with as many golds as bronzes and the occasional diamond, against Greenstone's mid-iron. A numeric figure is still missing.
Who governs the Old City? (Narrowed in the 2026-10-22 pass.) Known: Adris Dorgan is mayor of Old City and the Duke of Greenstone is the city's ruler, over the town constables.

How long did the Cardinas zone last? (Narrowed in the 2026-10-22 pass.) Known: Nik is "six months old" at, so the zone lasted at least about six months from his creation; Gary is "almost a year" past the Cup of Heroes at, which caps it at roughly eleven months; "months" at.

What set off the System's withdrawal from regions that keep indenture? (Narrowed in the 2026-10-22 pass.) Known: the withdrawal is Jason's act as System Administrator (the petitioners ask him to arbitrate "your withdrawal of the System"), and Cyrion's house guards are a form of indenture.
What part did Gerling play at Saint-Étienne? (Resolved in the 2026-10-22 pass.) Gerling did not set the device: Mr North names Shako and Chen as the ones who placed it in the aperture.
Gerling entered separately, taking Adrien Barbou from the EOA headquarters and forcing him to open the dimensional space, and later fights beside Jason in the zone.

When is the Book 12 present? (Narrowed in the 2026-10-22 passes.) Known: "almost twenty years" since the priests were freed, Jason's "fifteen years or so" away, magic known "less than fifteen years ago" and Book 13 in 2038 with sixteen years gone.

The Earth arrival fits 2038 better: Lenora and Jason count "seventeen years" from the Earthlings' vanishing in autumn 2021, and Jota says Jason was born "forty-four years ago", which with a 1 April 1994 birth is April 2038 or later.

How long has the vampire war lasted? (Narrowed in the build plan 1.5 pass.) Known: the first vampire war "ended without conclusion" when both sides were exhausted and the vampires got nuclear weapons; the war was back "in full swing" and a character places the symposium "two years into the renewed vampire war".
Jason says the operation will bring it to a final conclusion, and it ended in the months before the farewell.
Simon McKean says it has been fought "off and on for decades". Not known: the first war's length.

How old is Emi when Rufus arrives, against the sword line? (Resolved in the 2026-10-22 pass: not a contradiction.) Emi is twelve in June 2019 and thirteen in Book 5, so she is fifteen when Rufus first reaches Earth about 2021-22.
The "six years" of Gary's sword are counted from late 2017 to Jason's departure into the void in late 2023, a later moment; Emi is then about sixteen.

Where does the Order of the Reaper survive? Known: a coalition of churches wiped out the original order centuries ago; the new structure persists as a volunteer network of quiet allies, with the trials as a lure, and Jason fears "the Order of the Reaper that still existed".
Is Adrien Barbou Mr East? (Resolved in the 2026-10-22 pass.) Yes, as the second Mr East: the previous Mr East is "the late Mr East" and Barbou is "now going by Mr East".

Where does the Adventure Society's continental council sit? (Narrowed in the build plan 1.5 pass; the text disagrees with itself.) Known: Book 6 puts it in Vitesse, "rather than the capital city, Cyrion"; Book 6 also calls Rakesh, on the north coast of the Africa-like continent, "the home of the Adventure Society's continental council"; Book 7 calls Cyrion "home to the Adventure Society's continental council".
Greenstone's inquiries come from "the Continental Council".
Who leads Moon's Edge? (Resolved in the 2026-10-22 pass.) Miriam Vance leads it; Allayeth raised and supervises the team.
Why does Sigrid call the Mirror King "Father"? (Resolved in the 2026-10-22 pass.) She does not: she greets Hastor, the king's portal specialist, who is her father.
